notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 026 for the As-Ge host: three of the four samples are GeAs and the paper is titled GeAs: Highly Anisotropic van der Waals Thermoelectric Material.

Materials Project gives GeAs C2/m (12) mp-9548 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, which fixes the space group. The block is led by GeAs2 Pbam mp-17524 on 3 references, but that is a different compound rather than a polymorph, and GeAs I4mm mp-7591 at hull 0.096 is a computed higher-symmetry alternative.
SiAs is isostructural and GeP is closely related, which is why the archetype is written over silicon and germanium with phosphorus and arsenic rather than scoped to the one compound.
The Ge-Ge dimer inside each slab is what separates this from the GeS type and is the origin of the transport anisotropy; it should survive into any v4 wording.

formula_archetype: AM4X3 (A = alkali, M = Zn or Cd, X = As or Sb)

discriminate_from.caal2si2_zintl: the layered trigonal Zintl entry with the closest look, since both stack a cation layer against an anionic slab in a trigonal or rhombohedral cell. That archetype is AM2X2 with one slab type; NaZn4As3 carries twice the transition-metal content in a thicker and differently connected zinc arsenide block
discriminate_from.pbfcl_matlockite: the tetragonal P4/nmm MXY arrangement of NaZnAs, which is the 1:1:1 compound of these same three elements and the phase TEDesignLab returns for this chemistry. Different stoichiometry and different symmetry, and worth stating because a Na-Zn-As composition list can contain both
discriminate_from.zrcusias_1111: the other layered pnictide of alternating cation and pnictide layers, but tetragonal P4/nmm and built on a fluorite-like oxide layer
discriminate_from.alpha_nafeo2_layered: shares the R-3m stacking symmetry and nothing else: that entry is an ordered rocksalt AMO2 with octahedral coordination, this is a tetrahedral zinc arsenide framework

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 026 for the As-Na-Zn host: all four samples are NaZn4-xCuxAs3 and the paper title states that the compound crystallises in the rhombohedral system.
Materials Project gives NaZn4As3 R-3m (166) mp-1078703 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference, fixing formula and space group. TEDesignLab covers only NaZnAs P4/nmm mp-13097, a different compound.

The slab description - an alkali layer alternating with a thick tetrahedral zinc arsenide block - comes from materials knowledge on top of one ICSD-backed space group, not from a structure file, and is what should be checked at v4 review.
Charge balance is clean at one Na+ and four Zn2+ against three As3-, which is why it is filed as a Zintl polyanion rather than as an intermetallic.

formula_archetype: B12X2 with wide homogeneity, X = P, As, O or S
typical_space_group: R-3m (166), R3m (160) when the inter-icosahedral site orders

discriminate_from.boron_carbide: the entry a B-S composition would otherwise be forced into, and the nearest relative. B4C-B13C2 is built on the same R-3m array of B12 icosahedra, but the species between the icosahedra is a three-atom C-B-C chain that is itself part of the covalent network. In the B12X2 members the inter-icosahedral site holds a two-atom X-X dumbbell or a single heavier atom, which changes the electron count per icosahedron and is why B12P2 is a wide-gap semiconductor while B4C is a p-type semimetallic conductor. The seed entry also folds beta-rhombohedral boron into boron_carbide, and that is a 105-atom cell, different again
discriminate_from.alb12_icosahedral: the other icosahedral boride already split out of boron_carbide. AlB12 is a tetragonal P4_12_12 framework of B12 and B19 units with the metal in channels and only partial occupancy; there is no ordered inter-icosahedral site at all
discriminate_from.cab6_hexaboride: B6 octahedra rather than B12 icosahedra, in a simple cubic framework with a divalent cation in the cage
discriminate_from.ub12_boride: cubic B12 cuboctahedra, not icosahedra, with the metal on an ordered fcc site
discriminate_from.mgalb14_boride: orthorhombic Imma, icosahedra bridged by isolated boron atoms and two metal sites

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 027 for the B-S host. All four samples are B6S0.60-B6S0.63, which is B12S1.2-B12S1.26 per icosahedron, and the paper is titled An alpha-rhombohedral boron-related compound with sulfur: Synthesis, struc[ture ...]. The structure type is named in the source rather than inferred from the formula.

Materials Project has B12S R3m (160) mp-1228640 at hull 0.076 with no ICSD reference. Its block for this chemistry is led by B2S3 I4_1/a mp-1199451 and BS2 P2_1/c mp-1200183, which are the molecular thioborates and a different chemistry entirely, so the reference is of little help here and mp_id is left null.

The sub-stoichiometric occupancy of the inter-icosahedral site, S0.6 per B6 rather than S1 per B6, is the carrier knob in these compounds, the same role the C content plays across the B4C homogeneity range. Stage 3 should read it as non_stoichiometry, not as doping.

Whether v4 keeps this separate from boron_carbide or folds both into one icosahedral-boron entry with a variant field is a real choice. Kept separate here because the inter-icosahedral species is the only structural variable in the family and it is what distinguishes every member.

formula_archetype: A8M16Pn30 (A = Ba, M = Cu, Pn = P)

discriminate_from.clathrate_i: the entry the formula invites, since A8M16X30 is exactly the type-I stoichiometry of Ba8Ga16Ge30. It is the wrong one. Type I is cubic Pm-3n and its framework is built from two pentagonal dodecahedra and six tetrakaidecahedra per cell. The Ba-Cu-P framework is not cubic and its cages are truncated octahedra, the Kelvin cell, which is a polyhedron that does not occur in any of the standard clathrate types. Matching on the 8-16-30 ratio alone would file this wrongly
discriminate_from.clathrate_ii: cubic Fd-3m, A24M136, a different cage ratio again
discriminate_from.clathrate_viii: the I-43m type of beta-Ba8Ga16Sn30, which is the other non-type-I A8M16X30 already in the taxonomy and therefore the closest competitor on formula. Type VIII has a single distorted 23-vertex cage per guest; this has the Kelvin-cell framework
discriminate_from.clathrate_iii_ix: the remaining standard types, again with their own defined cage sets
discriminate_from.caal2si2_zintl: a layered Zintl pnictide rather than a cage framework, and what a Ba-Cu-P composition at a different ratio might be instead

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 027 for the Ba-Cu-P host: three of the four samples are Ba8Cu16P30 and one of the three papers is titled Twisted Kelvin Cells and Truncated Octahedral Cages in the Crystal Str[ucture ...]. A second, Unconventional Clathrates with Transition Metal-Phosphorus Frameworks, states the family classification directly. Both say the framework is not one of the standard clathrate types.

typical_space_group is deliberately null. The cell is tetragonal and I-42d (122) is what I recall for this compound, but that is materials knowledge with no database entry behind it here, and a wrong space group in the taxonomy is worse than an absent one. Materials Project returns no Ba8Cu16P30 at all for this chemistry -- its block is Ba(Cu2P)4 I4/m mp-14785, Ba2Cu3P4 Ibam mp-28661, BaCuP P6_3/mmc mp-16254 and Ba4Cu8P15 Pbcn mp-1197658, all different compounds at one ICSD reference each. Fix the space group from the 2015 Chem. Mater. paper at v4 review.

The framework is Cu-P rather than the group 13/14 frameworks of the conventional clathrates, which is the point of the Accounts paper: a transition metal in the cage wall changes both the electron count and the bonding, and these are the compounds that let the guest concentration be varied independently of the framework charge.
The fourth sample in the host, BaCu2P4, is a different phosphide and is not covered by this entry.

formula_archetype: AM2Pn2 orthorhombic (A = Sr, Ba; M = Ga, In; Pn = Sb, Bi)

discriminate_from.caal2si2_zintl: the entry an AM2Pn2 formula points straight at, and the wrong one here. CaAl2Si2 is trigonal P-3m1 with flat alkaline-earth layers alternating with a single kind of tetrahedral anion slab. BaGa2Sb2 is orthorhombic Pnma: the barium is too large for the trigonal slab and the gallium antimonide anion condenses into a three-dimensional framework of corner- and edge-sharing GaSb4 tetrahedra with barium in its channels. Same 1-2-2 ratio, different dimensionality, and the two cannot be told apart from the formula
discriminate_from.zintl_2_1_2_a2cdsb2: the A:M ratio is inverted -- two large cations per one tetrahedral cation there, one per two here
discriminate_from.zintl_3_1_3: a different ratio again in the same family, with isolated or chain-like anion units rather than a framework
discriminate_from.zn4sb3: the other Zintl antimonide with a low lattice thermal conductivity from disorder, but its disorder is interstitial zinc, not a framework topology
discriminate_from.yb14mnsb11_zintl: the 14-1-11 antimonide, a far larger cell built from isolated MnSb4 tetrahedra, Sb3 units and free Sb anions

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 027 for the Ba-Ga-Sb host: all four samples are BaGa2-xZnxSb2 and the paper is titled Thermoelectric Enhancement in BaGa2Sb2 by Zn Doping.

Materials Project gives Ba(GaSb)2 Pnma (62) mp-29938 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference, which fixes formula and space group. The rest of its block is other Ba-Ga-Sb Zintl stoichiometries -- Ba3GaSb3 Pnma mp-28296, Ba7Ga4Sb9 Pmmn mp-28314 -- and none of them is what the samples are.

The description of the anion as a three-dimensional tetrahedral framework rather than a layer comes from materials knowledge sitting on top of one ICSD-backed space group, not from a structure file, and is the part to check at v4 review. What is certain from the reference is that it is Pnma and therefore not the trigonal CaAl2Si2 type.
SrGa2Sb2 is written into the archetype because the strontium analogue is the compound this family is usually introduced with; only barium appears in this dataset.

Zn-for-Ga is an acceptor on the framework cation site: it removes one electron per substitution from the polyanion and is the carrier knob the paper uses. Stage 3 should not read it as a dilute impurity.

formula_archetype: AB13 (A = alkali, alkaline earth, rare earth or actinide; B = Be, Zn, Fe-Si)

discriminate_from.cab6_hexaboride: the other cubic AB6-to-AB13 cage type in the taxonomy and the nearest idea. CaB6 encloses the cation in a framework of covalently bonded B6 octahedra; NaZn13 encloses it in a snub cube of 24 metal atoms built from icosahedral B13 units, and the bonding is metallic throughout with no covalent cluster
discriminate_from.ub12_boride: cubic UB12 is the other uranium cage boride and is AB12 in Fm-3m built from B12 cuboctahedra. Different cluster, different space group, and easy to confuse with UBe13 by name alone
discriminate_from.laves_phase: AB2 close packing of two atom sizes with no cage at all
discriminate_from.cecu6: the other heavy-fermion intermetallic prototype reached from this chemistry, orthorhombic and at AB6
discriminate_from.solid_solution_alloy: what an Be-U composition would fall to by default. UBe13 is an ordered line compound with eleven ICSD references, not a disordered alloy

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 027 for the Be-U host: all four samples are UBe13 across four papers, all of them on the heavy-fermion superconductor.
Materials Project gives UBe13 Fm-3c (226) mp-1163 at hull 0.000 with 11 ICSD references, the best-attested entry in that block by a wide margin, which fixes formula and space group without inference.

The taxonomy had no AB13 entry at all. The cage description -- the A cation at the cube corners and face centres, each surrounded by 24 Be atoms, with the remaining Be forming icosahedra -- is standard for the type and is why these compounds have unusually low Debye temperatures for their density.

The type is wanted beyond this host: LaBe13 and the LaCo13-related La(Fe,Si)13 magnetocaloric compounds are the same arrangement, and the rare-earth beryllides recur in low-temperature transport work.

UBe13 is the textbook heavy-fermion superconductor, so the transport being measured is dominated by f-electron physics rather than by the structure. That does not change the structure assignment but is worth knowing when the numbers are used.

display_name: Ca2SiO4 belite orthosilicate and its polymorphs
formula_archetype: A2SiO4 (A = Ca, Sr, Ba; also the Ca2SiO4-Ca3P2O8 solid solution)
typical_space_group: P2_1/c (14) for beta-larnite; Pnma (62) for the gamma olivine form

discriminate_from.x2_re2sio5_monosilicate: the other isolated-SiO4 entry in the taxonomy, and the closest relative. RE2SiO5 carries one free oxygen per formula unit that is not bonded to silicon at all, sitting in an OA4 tetrahedron of its own; in A2SiO4 every oxygen belongs to an SiO4 group and the ratio is 4 per silicon, not 5
discriminate_from.thortveitite_re2si2o7: Si2O7 dimers with a bridging oxygen. Belite is a true orthosilicate with isolated tetrahedra and no Si-O-Si bond anywhere
discriminate_from.fresnoite: Ba2TiSi2O8, a layered silicate with a five-coordinate titanium, and a different anion topology
discriminate_from.garnet: also built from isolated SiO4 tetrahedra, but cubic Ia-3d with an eight-coordinate and a six-coordinate cation site. Belite has no octahedral cation at all
discriminate_from.antiperovskite: the other structure present in the Ca-O-Si host. Ca3SiO is an inverse perovskite with silicon as the anion, which is the opposite oxidation-state assignment from a silicate

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 027 for the Ca-O-Si host: three of the four samples are (Ca2SiO4)0.86(Ca3P2O8)0.14 and related belite-phosphate solid solutions, and the paper is titled Thermal Conductivity of 2CaO.SiO2 Bearing Solid Solution. 2CaO.SiO2 is cement notation for Ca2SiO4.

TEDesignLab covers this chemistry properly for once: Ca2SiO4 P2_1/c (14) mp-4180 at hull 0.035 with 19 ICSD references is its primary, and Ca2SiO4 Pnma (62) mp-4481 at hull 0.000 with 12 references is also listed. That ordering -- the well-attested phase above the hull, the hull minimum less attested -- is the standard signature of a metastable form that is what people actually make, and it is exactly the belite situation.

The polymorph sequence is the reason this needs its own entry rather than a generic silicate label. Ca2SiO4 runs gamma (Pnma, olivine-like) to alpha-prime-L to alpha-prime-H to alpha on heating, while beta (P2_1/c) is the metastable room-temperature form retained by quenching and stabilised by the phosphate and other substituents -- which is why the cement literature always reports it and why the Ca3P2O8 component in these compositions is there. A 6 percent volume expansion on beta to gamma is what dusting in cement clinker is.

Transition temperatures are approximately 1000 K for beta to alpha-prime-L and approximately 1430 K for alpha-prime-L to alpha-prime-H, both composition-dependent and both from materials knowledge rather than from the paper. They are recorded on the assignment at low confidence and should be checked at v4 review.
The archetype is written over A = Ca, Sr, Ba because the alkaline-earth orthosilicates are isostructural in their high-temperature forms, but only calcium appears in this dataset.

formula_archetype: RSi2 and the defect RSi2-x range (R = rare earth, Th, U); the germanide analogues take the same type
typical_space_group: I4_1/amd (141); the silicon-deficient members distort to Imma (74)

discriminate_from.alb2: the competing arrangement for the same RSi2 formula, and the one that actually matters. AlB2-type disilicides are hexagonal with flat graphite-like silicon sheets; ThSi2 has a genuinely three-dimensional net of three-connected silicon atoms. The series swaps from one to the other near the middle of the lanthanides, and the light rare earths that appear in thermoelectric work are on the ThSi2 side
discriminate_from.tisi2_c54: C54 TiSi2 is orthorhombic Fddd, a different stacking of silicon layers and a transition-metal rather than a rare-earth disilicide
discriminate_from.crsi2_c40: C40 CrSi2 is hexagonal P6222; it is the semiconducting transition-metal disilicide type, whereas ThSi2-type rare-earth disilicides are metallic
discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: shares Th and Si in the name and nothing else -- a layered 122 slab structure at a different stoichiometry
discriminate_from.mo2feb2_u3si2: the other structure present in the Ce-Si host, at R3T2 stoichiometry
discriminate_from.solid_solution_alloy: what an RSi2 composition would otherwise fall to. These are ordered line compounds with a dozen ICSD references, not disordered alloys

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 028 for the Ce-Si host: three of the four samples are CeSi2 and the paper is titled Thermoelectric properties of the solid solutions based on ThSi2-type CeSi2, which names the structure type outright.
The taxonomy had entries for ThCr2Si2, Th3P4, Th7Fe3 and ThMn12 but none for ThSi2 itself, which is the archetype of an entire rare-earth disilicide family.
[ref 2] fixes the structure without inference: CeSi2 I4_1/amd (141) mp-1072078 at hull 0.000 with 11 ICSD references, the best-attested entry in that chemistry.

The defect range matters for transport. CeSi2-x is stable over a wide silicon deficiency and the vacancies drive the tetragonal to orthorhombic Imma distortion as well as the magnetic behaviour, so an assignment to this type should not assume ideal stoichiometry.
The type recurs beyond this host in the rare-earth disilicides and in the ThSi2-type germanides, so it is wanted for its own sake rather than only for Ce-Si.

formula_archetype: MT1.5X (M = Ti, Zr, Hf; T = Co, Ni; X = Sn, Sb)
typical_space_group: F-43m (216) with the second tetrahedral 4d site half occupied; ordered variants lower the symmetry to larger supercells

discriminate_from.half_heusler: the same F-43m cell with the 4d site completely empty, MTX at 18 valence electrons. The three-quarter compounds are the halfway point of that vacancy, which is the whole reason they were made
discriminate_from.full_heusler: the same cell with the 4d site completely full, MT2X in Fm-3m at 24 valence electrons. A three-quarter Heusler is not a two-phase mixture of these, though a badly made one can be
discriminate_from.inverse_heusler: a different site ordering at full occupancy, not a partial one
discriminate_from.quaternary_heusler: orders four different elements onto four full sites; the three-quarter type orders vacancies on one site instead
discriminate_from.solid_solution_alloy: the partial occupancy is on a defined crystallographic site of an ordered cell, not a disordered alloy

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 028 for the Co-Hf-Sn and Co-Sn-Zr hosts, where HfCo1.5Sn and ZrCo1.5Sn appear alongside the full Heuslers Co2HfSn and Co2ZrSn. The shared paper is titled MCo1.5Sn (M = Ti, Zr, and Hf) ternary compounds: a class of three-quarter Heusler compounds, so the class is the paper authors own framing.

Neither reference carries a 1.5 entry at all. For Co-Sn-Zr [ref 2] offers ZrCo2Sn Fm-3m mp-914303 with 7 ICSD references and ZrCoSn P-62m mp-30563 with 2, the full and a hexagonal ternary; for Co-Hf-Sn HfCo2Sn Fm-3m mp-20730 with 5 and HfCoSn P-62c mp-22315 with 2. The half-occupied composition sits between the Heusler end members and is absent from the 2019 snapshot, which is exactly why it needs a taxonomy entry rather than being rounded to one of its neighbours.

Half occupancy of a single site is a strong point-defect phonon scatterer, which is the thermoelectric interest and distinguishes these from a simple two-phase half-plus-full mixture. Whether a given sample is genuinely half occupied or is a nanoscale intergrowth of the two Heuslers is a real question that only the paper can settle.

Note the hexagonal MCoSn entries in Materials Project: at 1:1:1 these chemistries also form a P-62m or P-62c ternary that is not a Heusler at all, so a composition near MTX cannot be assigned to the cubic family on stoichiometry alone.

formula_archetype: Cu(26-x)(Fe,Zn)(x)(Ge,As,Sn)4S32

discriminate_from.colusite: the nearest relative by far and the entry a germanite composition would otherwise be forced into. Both are P-43n cation-ordered superstructures of sphalerite with 32 sulfur atoms per cell, but colusite is Cu26V2Sn6S32 with a tetrahedrally coordinated group-5 transition metal and six group-14 atoms, while germanite has four group-14 atoms and eight iron. Different cation counts, different electron count, different transport
discriminate_from.tetrahedrite: Cu12Sb4S13, also a copper sulfide with 13 sulfur atoms per cell, but built around trigonal-planar copper and a lone-pair antimony rather than an all-tetrahedral framework
discriminate_from.chalcopyrite: CuFeS2, the simple 1:1:2 tetragonal sphalerite superstructure. Germanite is the same tetrahedral building principle at a much larger and more complex cell
discriminate_from.stannite_kesterite: Cu2FeSnS4 and Cu2ZnSnS4, the quaternary tetragonal sphalerite superstructures at 1:1:1:4
discriminate_from.famatinite: Cu3SbS4, a tetragonal sphalerite superstructure with a group-15 rather than a group-14 cation
discriminate_from.sphalerite: the disordered parent. The point of germanite is the ordering of four cation species over the zinc sites, which is what opens the gap

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 028 for the Cu-Fe-Ge-S host: all four samples are Cu22Fe8Ge4S32 and the paper is titled Structure, microstructure and thermoelectric properties of germanite-type Cu22Fe8Ge4S32, so the type is named by the authors.
The taxonomy has colusite but nothing for germanite, and the two are close enough that a colusite label would be a real misstatement of the cation chemistry rather than a rounding.

The references are unhelpfully split here. [ref 1] TEDesignLab gives only FeCu2GeS4 I-42m mp-917359 with 5 ICSD references, which is the stannite-type quaternary at a different stoichiometry, and [ref 2] offers Fe2Cu13(GeS8)2 P-43m (215) mp-1227624 at hull 0.017 with no ICSD reference. The P-43m entry is at the right composition and close to the right symmetry and is probably a computed relative of the P-43n germanite cell, but neither reference actually carries germanite itself.

The mineral germanite is nominally Cu26Fe4Ge4S32; the synthetic thermoelectric compositions push iron up to eight per cell at the expense of copper, which is the carrier-concentration knob for this family.

formula_archetype: Cu3RTe3 (R = Y, Sm, Dy, Er and other trivalent rare earths)

discriminate_from.cu2gese3: the other ternary copper chalcogenide built from tetrahedral copper in the taxonomy, but a diamond-like Cu2MX3 with a main-group partner rather than a rare-earth telluride, and orthorhombic Cmc2_1
discriminate_from.chalcopyrite: CuFeS2 and its relatives are strict sphalerite superstructures with one cation per anion; Cu3RTe3 has three copper and one rare earth for three tellurium, so the cation to anion ratio is 4 to 3 and the framework is not diamond-like
discriminate_from.acu5q3_layered: another copper-rich ternary chalcogenide with a mobile copper substructure, but layered and at a different stoichiometry
discriminate_from.argyrodite: the other copper and silver chalcogenide family whose interest is a disordered cation substructure. Argyrodites are cubic with a rigid anion framework; Cu3RTe3 is a polar orthorhombic ordered structure
discriminate_from.tetrahedrite: a copper antimony sulfosalt with a lone-pair cation, no rare earth, and a quite different cell

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 028 for the Cu-Er-Te host: the two papers are Cu3ErTe3: a new promising thermoelectric material predicated by high-throughput screening and Ternary Compounds Cu3RTe3 (R = Y, Sm, and Dy): A Family of New Thermoelectric materials, so the family is established in its own right rather than being a one-off composition.

[ref 2] supplies the structure: Er(CuTe)3 Pmn2_1 (31) mp-640885 at hull 0.000 with an ICSD reference, which is Cu3ErTe3 written in Materials Project ordering. The rhombohedral R-3 entry mp-1225130 at hull 0.048 is the same formula at higher energy with no ICSD backing and is not taken as the ambient form.
The space group is quoted from that reference rather than from independent knowledge of the type, and should be confirmed at v4 review.
A polar space group is worth flagging for stage 2: it permits piezoelectric and second-harmonic response, and it means the structure has no inversion centre to simplify the band structure with.
Silver substitutes for copper in the reported series, which is the expected behaviour for a copper chalcogenide and is how these compositions are tuned.

formula_archetype: Cu3BX4 (B = P, As, Sb; X = S, Se)

discriminate_from.famatinite: the entry a Cu3BX4 composition would otherwise be forced into, and the reason this one is needed. Famatinite Cu3SbSe4 is the SPHALERITE-derived tetragonal I-42m polymorph; enargite is the WURTZITE-derived orthorhombic Pmn2_1 one. They are two different structures at one stoichiometry -- enargite and luzonite are precisely that pair for Cu3AsS4 -- so a single id cannot carry both without asserting the wrong anion stacking
discriminate_from.stannite_kesterite: A2BCX4 with two distinct non-copper cations ordered over the cation sites; enargite has one, at Cu3BX4
discriminate_from.colusite: a much larger P-43n cation-ordered superstructure with 32 anions per cell and several cation species; enargite is the simple small-cell Cu3BX4 ordering
discriminate_from.chalcopyrite: CuFeS2, the 1:1:2 tetragonal sphalerite superstructure; a different cation ratio and, again, cubic rather than hexagonal anion stacking
discriminate_from.wurtzite: the disordered hexagonal parent. Enargite is wurtzite with copper and the group-15 cation ordered over the cation sites, which is what opens the gap
discriminate_from.sphalerite: the cubic parent of famatinite, not of enargite. Which parent a Cu3BX4 takes is exactly the distinction this entry records

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 029 for the Cu-P-S host, where all four compositions are Cu3P(1-x)Ge(x)S4 and the paper is titled Enargite Cu3PS4, naming the type directly.
[ref 2] agrees on the cell: Cu3PS4 Pmn2_1 (31) mp-3934 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references, ranked first for the formula.

The taxonomy already carried famatinite for the tetragonal Cu3BX4 form. Adding the orthorhombic form as a sibling rather than widening famatinite keeps the sphalerite-versus-wurtzite parentage visible, which is what governs the band structure and the anisotropy stage 2 will need.
Germanium substitutes for phosphorus on the group-15 site in the reported series, which is an acceptor and is how the hole count is set.

formula_archetype: Cu6(Sn,Ge)(W,Mo)(S,Se)8

discriminate_from.colusite: the nearest taxonomy entry and the one a Cu6WSnSe8 composition would otherwise be forced into. Both are cation-ordered superstructures of sphalerite in the same mineral group, but colusite is Cu26V2Sn6S32 with a group-5 metal and six group-14 atoms per 32 anions, while kiddcreekite is Cu24Sn4W4X32 with a group-6 metal at a 1:1 ratio to the group-14 atom. Different cation counts and a different electron count
discriminate_from.famatinite: the alternative reading of this composition at a smaller cell: Cu6WSnSe8 is also Cu3(W0.5Sn0.5)Se4, a famatinite A3BX4 with the B site shared equally by W(VI) and Sn(IV) to average the Sb(V) of Cu3SbSe4. Same tetrahedral framework, but famatinite is tetragonal I-42m with one B species and does not describe an ordered two-metal B sublattice
discriminate_from.stannite_kesterite: the quaternary A2BCX4 at 1:1:1:4 in a small tetragonal cell; kiddcreekite has six copper per two other cations and a cubic 2x2x2 sphalerite cell
discriminate_from.chalcopyrite: the simple 1:1:2 tetragonal sphalerite superstructure; the same building principle at the smallest possible cell
discriminate_from.sphalerite: the disordered parent. The point of this entry is the ordering of copper, tin and tungsten over the zinc sites

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 029 for the Cu-Se-Sn-W host, where all four compositions are Cu(6-x)WSnSe8 with x from 0 to 0.09.

The stoichiometry is the selenide analogue of the mineral kiddcreekite, Cu6SnWS8, and it charge-balances exactly as Cu(I)6 Sn(IV) W(VI) X(-II)8. Neither reference offers anything at all for this host, so the assignment rests on the composition and on the mineralogy rather than on a database entry.

The space group is quoted from the mineralogical description of kiddcreekite (cubic, a of about 10.86 Angstrom, a 2x2x2 sphalerite supercell) and has NOT been verified against a structure file here. Confirm it at v4 review, and consider at that point whether this and the germanite_type entry proposed from chunk 028 should be folded into one germanite-colusite group entry with the cation set recorded as a field.
Copper deficiency is the carrier-concentration knob: the reported series runs Cu6.00, Cu5.97, Cu5.94, Cu5.91 and the paper is about the charge localisation that comes with it.

formula_archetype: Tl2AXTe4 (A = Cd, Hg, Mn; X = Ge, Sn)
typical_space_group: tetragonal, I-42m (121) or I-4 (82) -- NOT VERIFIED, see notes

discriminate_from.stannite_kesterite: the entry these compositions would otherwise be forced into, and the reason this one is needed. The stoichiometry is identical, A2BCX4, but in stannite the A cation is tetrahedral Cu(I) or Ag(I) sitting inside the diamond-like framework, whereas here it is Tl(I), a large 6s2 lone-pair cation that cannot occupy a sphalerite cation site. The tetrahedral framework in Tl2AXTe4 is built from A and X only, with thallium outside it
discriminate_from.tl5te3: the other thallium telluride in the taxonomy, an intermetallic Tl(5-x)M(x)Te3 at 5:3 with no second framework cation; a quite different family despite the shared lone-pair chemistry
discriminate_from.inte_tlse: TlSe and InTe, the 1:1 thallium and indium chalcogenides with chains of edge-sharing tetrahedra and eight-coordinate Tl(I). The closest structural analogy for the role thallium plays, but at a different stoichiometry and dimensionality
discriminate_from.famatinite: Cu3BX4, a single non-copper cation in a sphalerite superstructure; no lone-pair A cation outside the framework
discriminate_from.chalcopyrite: the 1:1:2 tetragonal sphalerite superstructure, all cations tetrahedral

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 029 for two hosts from one paper, Ge-Hg-Te-Tl (Tl2HgGeTe4) and Hg-Sn-Te-Tl (Tl2HgSnTe4). The paper is Tl2AXTe4 (A = Cd, Hg, Mn; X = Ge, Sn): Crystal Structure, Electronic Structure and Thermoelectric Properties, so the family is established in its own right and its structure is reported there.
Neither reference database offers ANY entry for either composition, so there is no independent check on the cell here.

The space group is a reasoned guess from the A2BCX4 stoichiometry and is flagged as unverified. Read the crystal structure section of the paper before v4 review; if it turns out that thallium does sit in the tetrahedral framework after all, this entry should be withdrawn and the compositions filed under stannite_kesterite instead, which is why that id is recorded as the alternative on both ledger records.

The samples carry deliberate dopants at 0.001 per formula unit -- iodine on the tellurium site, lead on the thallium site, arsenic on the germanium site, gallium in the tin-bearing member -- which is a carrier-concentration sweep on a very lightly doped narrow-gap semiconductor, not contamination.

formula_archetype: A2TH4 (A = Mg, Ca; T = Fe, Co, Ni)
typical_space_group: C2/c (15) below about 510 K; cubic disordered above it

discriminate_from.interstitial_hydride: the entry this would otherwise be forced into, and the reason it is needed. An interstitial hydride is a metal lattice with hydrogen in its voids -- PdH0.66, the taxonomy exemplar, keeps the palladium fcc lattice and adds hydrogen to it, and the metal-metal bonding survives. Mg2NiH4 is not that: it is a salt of discrete tetrahedral [NiH4](4-) complex anions and Mg(2+) cations, the metal-metal bonding is gone, and it is a wide-gap insulator rather than a metal. The same host can hold both -- Mg2NiH0.7 IS an interstitial solid solution -- which is why they must be separable
discriminate_from.antifluorite: the cubic high-temperature form of Mg2NiH4 has its Mg2Ni units arranged antifluorite-like, so the disordered phase is often described that way; the entry here is for the ordered ambient structure in which the hydrogen positions and the complex anion are what matter
discriminate_from.perovskite: MgNiH3 (Pm-3m, mp-1017629 in the chunk reference list) is a perovskite hydride at a different stoichiometry, with hydrogen on the anion site of an ABX3 cell rather than in a discrete complex anion

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 029 for the H-Mg-Ni host, whose four compositions are Mg2NiH0.7, Mg2NiH1.3, Mg2NiH3.5 and Mg2NiH4 -- the two ends of the alpha-to-beta hydriding reaction, which are two different structures.
[ref 2] ranks Mg2NiH4 C2/c (15) mp-697331 first at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references, which is the ordered monoclinic form.

Mg2NiH4 undergoes an order-disorder transition near 510 K to a cubic high-temperature form. No measured temperature range is printed for this host, so whether that is crossed could not be judged at annotation time; it is worth checking in stage 2.

The structural_class is recorded as cluster compound because the defining feature is a discrete complex anion, not a close-packed metal framework. If a hydride class is ever added to the vocabulary this entry should move to it.

formula_archetype: A2BO5 or AB2O5, generally M3O5
typical_space_group: Cmcm (63), also given as Bbmm in the older setting

discriminate_from.corundum: the other M2O3-MO2 titanate motif. Corundum and ilmenite are hexagonal close-packed oxygen with cations in two thirds of the octahedra at M2O3 or ABO3; pseudobrookite is M3O5 and its octahedra form crosslinked chains rather than sheets
discriminate_from.rutile: the MO2 end member. Pseudobrookite is what forms when a divalent or trivalent oxide is taken into the titania framework at a 1:2 or 2:1 ratio, and it is a different framework, not a doped rutile
discriminate_from.spinel: AB2O4, cubic, oxygen close-packed with tetrahedral and octahedral cations. MgTi2O4 is the spinel of this chemistry and MgTi2O5 is the pseudobrookite; one oxygen apart and quite different structures
discriminate_from.magneli_phase: the shear structures TinO2n-1 of reduced titania. beta-Ti3O5 is formally the n=3 member and is also the pseudobrookite archetype, so the two families touch at that one composition; the entry here is for the ternary A2BO5 oxides, which are not shear derivatives of rutile
discriminate_from.ruddlesden_popper: layered An+1BnO3n+1 perovskite blocks; no perovskite block exists in pseudobrookite

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 030 for the Mg-O-Ti host, whose principal composition is MgTi2O5 and where [ref 2] ranks MgTi2O5 Cmcm (63) mp-28232 first at hull 0.000.

This is a large real family and the taxonomy had no entry for it. Al2TiO5 (tialite) and MgTi2O5 (karrooite) are the two thermally important members, both used as low-expansion refractories, and Fe2TiO5 and FeTi2O5 are the mineral end members.

Pseudobrookite is strongly cation-disordered: the A and B species mix over the 4c and 8f octahedral sites and the degree of order is quenching-rate dependent, so a structure file for it carries site occupancies rather than a fixed cation arrangement. Stage 2 should record which ordering, if any, the paper reports.

Also recorded as an alternative on the In-O-Ti host of the same chunk, where the cation-to-oxygen ratio works out at 25:42, within rounding of M3O5, but the identity of the phase could not be settled from a composition string alone.

formula_archetype: A4B3O8, i.e. A[A3B3]O8 with an ordered B sublattice

discriminate_from.spinel: the parent, and the entry this would otherwise be forced into. Na4Ir3O8 is a B-site ordered spinel: the octahedral sublattice of AB2O4 is shared one-to-one by sodium and iridium in an ordered way, which turns the pyrochlore lattice of corner-sharing tetrahedra into a hyperkagome net of corner-sharing triangles carrying only the iridium. That ordering is the whole point of the compound, and a plain spinel label would hide it
discriminate_from.pyrochlore: A2B2O7, also a corner-sharing tetrahedral B network, but a different structure and stoichiometry. The distinction matters because the magnetism of both is discussed in the same language
discriminate_from.delafossite: the other layered sodium iridate motif, ABO2 with two-dimensional triangular sheets; Na4Ir3O8 is three-dimensional
discriminate_from.alpha_nafeo2_layered: Na2IrO3 and the layered sodium iridates, where sodium and iridium order within honeycomb sheets rather than over a three-dimensional spinel sublattice. [ref 2] offers Na2IrO3 C2/m for this host and it is a different compound
discriminate_from.rocksalt_oxide: the close-packed parent of all of these; no cation ordering implied

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 030 for the Ir-Na-O host, whose compositions are Na3Ir3O8 and Na3.6Ir3O8 measured on single crystals.

[ref 2] offers nothing for this stoichiometry -- Na2IrO3 C2/m, Na4IrO4 I4/m and NaIrO3 Cmcm, each with a single ICSD reference -- so the assignment rests on the compound being a well known one rather than on a database entry.

Na4Ir3O8 is the canonical three-dimensional quantum spin liquid candidate: Ir(IV) is 5d5 with strong spin-orbit coupling on a hyperkagome net, and it shows no magnetic order down to very low temperature.

Sodium content is the carrier knob, not an impurity. Na4Ir3O8 is the insulating stoichiometric end; removing sodium oxidises the iridium and drives the metal-insulator transition that the paper measures across, which is why the two compositions here are Na3 and Na3.6 rather than Na4.
The space group is quoted from the published description of Na4Ir3O8 and has not been verified against a structure file here. Confirm at v4 review.

formula_archetype: MX with one quarter of both sublattices vacant, M3X3 in a rocksalt cell

discriminate_from.rocksalt_oxide: the parent, and the entry this would otherwise be forced into. NbO is not a rocksalt with a few vacancies; a quarter of the cation sites and a quarter of the anion sites are vacant and the vacancies are ordered, which leaves square-planar NbO4 units, four-coordinate niobium instead of six, and direct Nb-Nb bonding across the cube edges. That bonding is why NbO is a metal and why it superconducts, and a rocksalt label would not predict any of it
discriminate_from.rocksalt_nitride_carbide: TiN, TaN and the transition-metal carbonitrides, which are genuine rocksalts carrying random non-stoichiometric vacancies rather than an ordered vacancy superstructure. The distinction is order, not vacancy concentration
discriminate_from.perovskite: NbO in Pm-3m is sometimes described as a perovskite with the A and B cation sites swapped and the body centre empty; the cell metric is the same but there is no ABO3 cation pair
discriminate_from.magneli_phase: the other way a reduced early-transition-metal oxide accommodates non-stoichiometry, by crystallographic shear rather than by ordered point vacancies

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 030 for the N-Nb-O host, whose bulk composition is NbON0.17 and whose paper is Vacancy filling effect in thermoelectric NbO.

The vacancies are the subject of the thermoelectric work: nitrogen entering the vacant anion sites of NbO is the carrier-concentration variable, so a prototype that does not carry the ordered vacancies cannot describe what the paper varies.
[ref 2] offers only NbNO P2_1/c (14) mp-7596 and a set of computed Nb-N-O cells; none of them is NbO itself, so there is no database anchor for this entry in the chunk.

The other host in the same chunk that reaches this chemistry, N-Nb-O-Ru, is a reactively sputtered amorphous film and is filed under amorphous instead. The same elements can give either, so the two must be separable.

formula_archetype: MSi3P4 (M = Ni)

discriminate_from.stannite_kesterite: the nearest tetragonal I-42m entry and the one this composition would otherwise be forced into. Stannite is A2BCX4 at 2:1:1:4 with a single anion species; NiSi3P4 is 1:3:4 with silicon and phosphorus both in the framework and no separate cation and anion sublattice of that kind
discriminate_from.chalcopyrite: the 1:1:2 sphalerite superstructure, tetragonal I-42d; the same tetrahedral building principle at a different cation count
discriminate_from.defect_chalcopyrite_ovc: the ordered-vacancy variants of chalcopyrite. Worth revisiting at v4 review, because if the NiSi3P4 cell turns out to carry ordered cation vacancies it may belong with them rather than standing alone

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 030 for the Ni-P-Si host, whose four compositions are NiSi3P4 with boron substituted for silicon at 0 to 0.2 per formula unit. The paper is Thermoelectric properties of polycrystalline NiSi3P4.

[ref 2] ranks Si3NiP4 I-42m (121) mp-8311 first at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference, which is where the space group here comes from. The single reference makes it a weak primary by the chunk criterion, but it is also the only entry at this stoichiometry and it matches the measured compound exactly.

The framework description -- that this is a tetrahedral diamond-like network rather than something else at the same space group -- is inferred from I-42m, from the main-group stoichiometry and from the semiconducting transport reported, NOT read from a structure file. Verify it before v4 review, and withdraw the entry if NiSi3P4 turns out to belong to an existing family.
The two neighbouring MP entries, Si2NiP3 Imm2 and Si2Ni5P3 Pbca, are different line compounds of the Ni-Si-P system and are not polymorphs of this one.

formula_archetype: A2M3O12 (A = Sc, Y, Al, In, Lu, Fe; M = W, Mo)

discriminate_from.zrw2o8_type: the other tungstate negative-thermal-expansion family, cubic Pa-3 at AM2O8 with one terminal oxygen per WO4 tetrahedron. A2M3O12 is orthorhombic, fully corner-linked and contracts anisotropically rather than isotropically, and it takes up water where ZrW2O8 does not
discriminate_from.scheelite_awo4: not in the taxonomy, but the structure the high-pressure forms of these compounds go to, with eight-coordinate A and one third of the A sites vacant. Sc0.67WO4 is exactly how a defect scheelite of this composition would be written, which is why it matters here
discriminate_from.garnet: A3B2C3O12, the other well known A-B-O12 framework; different cation count and cubic
discriminate_from.thortveitite_re2si2o7: the A2M2O7 rare-earth pyrosilicates, corner-linked tetrahedra again but with the tetrahedra joined to each other; in A2M3O12 every tetrahedron shares corners only with octahedra
discriminate_from.pyrochlore: A2B2O7 with both cations octahedral; no isolated tetrahedral anion group

structure_database_candidates.source: ref 2, hull 0.025, no icsd; a candidate for the denser high-pressure form, unverified

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 030 for the O-Sc-W host, whose single composition is written Sc0.67WO4, which is Sc2W3O12 in defect-scheelite notation.

The family is large and thermally important: A2M3O12 is one of the two standard negative-thermal-expansion oxide families, and the ambient orthorhombic Pbcn form is what [ref 2] attests with 5 ICSD references at mp-19588.

The paper for that host reports a high-pressure synthesis of a NEW scandium tungstate, so the measured sample may well not be the Pbcn ambient form. That is recorded on the ledger record rather than resolved here. If the high-pressure phase turns out to be a defect scheelite it needs its own entry, since a defect scheelite is a different framework and not a polymorph within this type.

Several members of the family take up water reversibly at room temperature and change cell markedly when they do, so a room-temperature structure measured on a hydrated sample is not the same as the dry one. Worth checking in stage 2 for any A2M3O12 assignment.

formula_archetype: AgBi3S5 and the wider pavonite homologous series (Nn,1L), built from thin and thick NaCl-type slabs meeting across a mirror plane

discriminate_from.bi_chalcogenide_complex: the catch-all this would otherwise fall into. Pavonite is a named mineral type with a defined homologous construction and a settled C2/m cell, so it does not belong in a bucket reserved for compositions that cannot be typed at all
discriminate_from.mbi4s7_type: the nearest proposed entry, also a monoclinic C2/m bismuth sulfosalt of rocksalt-derived slabs, but at M:Bi 1:4 with the divalent cation stitching the slabs octahedrally. Pavonite is 1:3 and the silver sits in the thin slab of the two-slab pavonite stacking. Separate them on the M:Bi ratio
discriminate_from.tetradymite: Bi2S3 and Bi2Se3 chemistry is adjacent but the tetradymite quintuple layer is rhombohedral with van der Waals gaps; the pavonite slabs are continuously bonded and monoclinic
discriminate_from.stibnite: orthorhombic Pnma Bi2S3 with ribbon chains, the binary parent of this chemistry and a different framework
discriminate_from.argyrodite: the other silver chalcogenide family with high silver mobility, but built on a tetrahedral central cation in an A8BX6 anion cage rather than on NaCl slabs

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 031 for the Ag-Bi-Cl-S host, whose three compositions are AgBi3S5 with chlorine progressively replacing sulfur: AgBi3S4.2Cl0.8, AgBi3S3.35Cl1.65, AgBi3S2.5Cl2.5.

Neither reference covers this host at all -- there is no TEDesignLab entry and no Materials Project line was printed -- so the type is assigned from the chemistry and the paper title alone, which names AgBi3S5 directly. mp_id is left null rather than guessed.

The chlorine substitution is the electron doping the paper is about, not an impurity: Cl on the sulfur site donates one electron per substitution, which is how an intrinsically p-type sulfosalt is driven n-type. Stage 3 should treat it as the doping variable.

The homologous character is the reason this may be better filed at v4 as one member of a pavonite series alongside homologous_tetradymite, gst_homologous and mbi4s7_type rather than as a standalone type.

formula_archetype: RTAl4 (R = rare earth or Ca; T = Ni, Co, Cu), commonly off-stoichiometric on the T and Al sites as in YbNi0.8Al4.2

discriminate_from.caco2al8_pbam: the 1-2-8 channel framework, orthorhombic Pbam, and the entry a rare-earth nickel aluminide of roughly this aluminium content would otherwise be pushed into. The stoichiometry is the discriminant: one transition metal per formula unit here against two, and four aluminium against eight
discriminate_from.ybfe2al10_cage: the 1-2-10 cage compound, also Cmcm, in which the rare earth sits inside a closed aluminium cage. The 1-1-4 has no such cage and half the aluminium content, so sharing a space group is coincidental and not a reason to merge them
discriminate_from.cecu6: the other low-symmetry heavy-fermion aluminide-like entry, but an RT6 with a quite different metal-to-ligand ratio
discriminate_from.cu3au_l12: the cubic RAl3 L1_2 phase that sits nearby in the same Yb-Al chemistry -- YbAl3 itself. That is a simple ordered fcc structure with no transition metal on its own site

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 031 for the Al-Ni-Yb host, whose dominant composition YbNi0.8Al4.2 is titled in its own paper as a novel intermetallic compound with an enhanced thermoelectric power.

The space group is recorded at medium confidence. Neither reference offers this compound: [ref 2] lists YbAl2Ni Cmcm (63) mp-12782, which is a 1-2-1 phase and not the same stoichiometry, plus Yb4Al23Ni6, YbAlNi and Yb2AlNi2. So the Cmcm assignment rests on the YNiAl4 structure type rather than on a database entry for this exact formula, and stage 2 should confirm it before attaching an mp_id.
The off-stoichiometry is intrinsic to the type: the reported composition is Ni-poor and Al-rich against ideal YbNiAl4, which is the usual homogeneity range of this family rather than a doping level.

formula_archetype: RT3Al9 (R = rare earth; T = Ni, Co, Rh, Ir)

discriminate_from.ynial4_cmcm: the other Yb-Ni-Al line compound in the very same host, at 1-1-4 rather than 1-3-9 and centrosymmetric Cmcm rather than chiral R32. Separate them on the Ni:Yb ratio, which is about 1 there and 3 here
discriminate_from.cacu5: the hexagonal RT5 layered aluminide family. ErNi3Al9 also stacks rare-earth honeycomb layers between transition-metal-aluminium slabs, but the R32 stacking is chiral and the composition is far more aluminium-rich
discriminate_from.prni2al3_ordered_cacu5: the ordered CaCu5 derivative at 1-2-3, hexagonal P6/mmm and centrosymmetric
discriminate_from.ybfe2al10_cage: a cage compound at 1-2-10, orthorhombic Cmcm, with the rare earth enclosed rather than in honeycomb layers
discriminate_from.alb2: trigonal-looking layered aluminide with a planar honeycomb net, but a simple binary AB2 with a tiny cell and no chirality

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 031 for the Al-Ni-Yb host. The third paper there is titled as thin film growth of the heavy fermion chiral magnet YbNi3Al9, which names both the composition and the chirality, and chirality is only meaningful for a Sohncke space group -- R32 is the one this structure type takes.

Neither reference carries this compound. [ref 2] lists Yb4Al23Ni6 C2/m mp-18482, YbAl2Ni Cmcm mp-12782, YbAlNi P-62m mp-1078733 and Yb2AlNi2 Immm mp-1207023, none of which is 1-3-9, so mp_id is left null rather than taken from the nearest formula.

The chirality is the physically interesting part: it produces the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction behind the helimagnetic order, and a stage 2 structure lookup that returns a centrosymmetric approximation of this cell would lose exactly that.

display_name: YCrB4-type boride with five- and seven-membered boron rings
formula_archetype: RMB4, and the related RMB6 with six- and seven-membered rings (R = Y or rare earth; M = Cr, Mo, W, Mn, Re)

discriminate_from.alb2: the honeycomb diboride, and the entry an RMB4 composition would otherwise be forced into. Its boron net is one uniform six-membered honeycomb with a single metal between the sheets. Here the net is built of fused five- and seven-membered rings and holds two metals of different size, the large R in the seven-ring and the smaller M in the five-ring. YMoB4 and MoB2 are not the same structure and do not have the same electron count
discriminate_from.ub12_boride: cubic REB12 built from B12 cuboctahedra enclosing the rare earth, Fm-3m. A three-dimensional cluster framework rather than a planar boron sheet; it is the other rare-earth boride reached from these chemistries and appears in this same chunk as ErB12
discriminate_from.cab6_hexaboride: a cubic framework of B6 octahedra at AB6. YCrB6 has the same 1:6 ratio of boron to large cation in its formula and is easy to confuse on stoichiometry alone, but its boron forms a planar ring net and a second metal is present
discriminate_from.boron_carbide: the icosahedral boron-rich entry. B12 icosahedra only appear above roughly B12 per metal atom; at B4 to B6 the boron is a two-dimensional ring net with no icosahedra at all
discriminate_from.crb_feb_chain: the other low-boron transition-metal boride, with boron in zigzag chains rather than rings, and binary rather than ternary
discriminate_from.mo2feb2_u3si2: the ternary transition-metal boride at 2-1-2, tetragonal P4/mbm with isolated boron pairs. The same idea of two metals plus boron, but a different boron motif and far less boron

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 032 for the B-Cr-Y and B-Mo-Y hosts, which between them hold YCrB4, YCrB6 and YMoB4. One paper is an electron-counting screen of prospective boride thermoelectrics and covers both hosts, so the family is being sampled deliberately rather than turning up by accident.

Both hosts are supported by ref 2 on the same space group from two different chemistries: YCrB4 Pbam mp-20450 and YB4Mo Pbam mp-7691, each at hull 0.000 with a single ICSD reference. One reference apiece is thin attestation, but the agreement across chemistries is worth something.

YCrB6 is folded in here rather than given its own entry. It is the next member of the same idea, with six- and seven-membered rings instead of five- and seven-, it is reported alongside YCrB4 in the same papers, and no sample in this set distinguishes the two by anything other than the nominal boron count. If a later chunk turns up RMB6 compositions on their own, splitting them out would be reasonable.

display_name: beta-rhombohedral boron (B105) and its metal-doped derivatives
formula_archetype: B105 with partially occupied interstitial sites; MxB with M = V, Cr, Fe, Sc or Cu at a few atomic per cent

discriminate_from.boron_carbide: the seed entry that currently absorbs beta-rhombohedral boron along with B4C. They share R-3m and both get described as icosahedral boron, but B4C is a fifteen-atom cell of one B12 icosahedron plus a three-atom C-B-C chain, while beta-boron is a 105-atom cell built from B12 icosahedra, a B28-B-B28 unit and a set of partially occupied interstitial sites. Those partial occupancies are not a detail to be smoothed over: they are where the metal goes, and the hopping conduction and the metal-insulator transition of the doped material are properties of exactly those sites
discriminate_from.b12x2_alpha_boron: alpha-rhombohedral boron with an inter-icosahedral X species, also R-3m and also proposed by this project. That is a twelve-plus-two atom cell with full occupancy. Beta is the thermodynamically stable allotrope at all temperatures and is the one that takes metals interstitially
discriminate_from.alb12_icosahedral: tetragonal aluminium boride in P4_12_12. Icosahedral, but a different framework, and the aluminium is a framework-forming constituent rather than a dilute interstitial
discriminate_from.alb2: the metal diboride reached from the same binary. VB2 and vanadium-doped beta-boron both appear in the B-V host and are not remotely the same structure: one is a layered honeycomb intermetallic at 33 atomic per cent metal, the other a boron framework with metal in cavities

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 032 for the B-V host. Its V11B89 and V32B68 compositions are vanadium-doped beta-rhombohedral boron: one paper is on the vanadium concentration dependence of the thermoelectric properties of beta-rhombohedral boron, the other on the low critical concentration of its metal-insulator transition.

The b12x2_alpha_boron proposal from an earlier chunk already noted in passing that the seed taxonomy folds beta-rhombohedral boron into boron_carbide and that a 105-atom cell is different again. This entry makes that split instead of leaving it as a remark.

Metal content is the working variable of this family rather than an impurity. Transport moves from hopping in undoped beta-boron towards metallic as the interstitial sites fill, and that is what both papers measure, so stage 3 should report the metal fraction as the controlled variable.

Ref 2 printed nothing resembling a beta-boron cell for the B-V host, only the line compounds VB2, V3B2, V2B3, VB and V5B3. mp_id is left null; the 105-atom partially occupied cell is not something to take from a nearest-formula match.

formula_archetype: A2OBO3 (A2 = Fe2, Mn2, MgTi, MgSc, NiSc)
typical_space_group: Pnma (62), commonly given in the Pbnm setting; Fe2OBO3 lowers to a monoclinic charge-ordered form below about 317 K

discriminate_from.spinel: the structure an iron oxyborate gets read as once the borate group is overlooked. Fe3O4 is the mixed-valence iron oxide everyone reaches for when charge ordering in an iron oxide is mentioned, and Fe2OBO3 does have the same one-to-one Fe2+ to Fe3+ ratio and its own Verwey-like ordering. But the iron here sits in ribbons four octahedra wide, isolated from one another by BO3 triangles, not in a three-dimensional framework of tetrahedra and octahedra
discriminate_from.corundum: the other iron oxide prototype reachable from this chemistry, Fe2O3 with iron in a single trivalent site. Warwickite is mixed-valence and contains an oxoanion
discriminate_from.ca3co2o6_chain: a genuine one-dimensional transition-metal oxide chain. Warwickite is quasi-one-dimensional too, but its ribbons are four octahedra wide and edge-sharing, which is why it charge-orders rather than behaving as an isolated chain
discriminate_from.cu2v2o7_pyrovanadate: another transition-metal oxide built around a discrete oxoanion group. Different anion, different connectivity, and no oxygen outside the anion group
discriminate_from.metavanadate_chain: chain oxide with the transition metal inside the oxoanion rather than outside it

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 032 for the B-Fe-O host, whose only composition is Fe2OBO3 across three samples. Both papers name the family outright: one is on the role of t2g versus eg interactions in the physical properties of A2OBO3, the other on electrical transport in charge-ordered Fe2OBO3.

The diagnostic is the oxygen that is not part of a BO3 group -- A2(O)(BO3) rather than a plain borate. Ref 2 has nothing of that kind for this chemistry: it lists Fe3B7IO13 R3c mp-1194881, Fe2B2O5 P-1 mp-19333, Fe3BO6 Pnma mp-25746, FeBO3 R-3c mp-19097 and Fe5(BO3)6 Pmmn mp-1198168, all ordinary borates. mp_id is left null.

The charge-ordering transition near 317 K sits inside the 163-649 K measured window for this host, and the resistive switching reported in the second paper is a property of the ordered state, so transport across that window is not a single regime. The transition is a symmetry lowering within the warwickite framework, not a change of prototype.

Ludwigite, A3O2BO3, is the near neighbour that is not in the taxonomy at all. If a ludwigite composition appears later it needs its own entry rather than being filed here -- it has three metals per borate and a different ribbon width.

display_name: Rare-earth boron carbonitride homologous series REB17CN / REB22C2N
formula_archetype: REB17CN, REB22C2N, REB28.5C4 -- a homologous series of B12 icosahedral layers separated by varying numbers of B6 octahedra and C-B-C chains
typical_space_group: monoclinic, reported as C2/m (12); see notes, the setting is not confirmed here

discriminate_from.boron_carbide: the closest relative and the entry these compositions would otherwise fall into. B4C is one B12 icosahedron plus a C-B-C chain in a fifteen-atom rhombohedral cell with no metal at all. The carbonitrides keep both the icosahedra and the chains but insert B6 octahedra and a rare-earth site, and the rare earth is the whole point: these are a rare n-type counterpart to p-type boron carbide, which is what all three papers on these hosts are about
discriminate_from.ub12_boride: cubic REB12 from B12 cuboctahedra in Fm-3m, with no carbon or nitrogen and a metallic rare-earth sublattice. It is the other rare-earth boride in the B-Er host and the two coexist there
discriminate_from.cab6_hexaboride: cubic REB6 built from B6 octahedra alone. The carbonitrides do contain B6 octahedra, but as one component of a layered icosahedral framework rather than as the entire structure
discriminate_from.alb12_icosahedral: tetragonal icosahedral boride with no rare-earth layer of this kind and no light-element chains
discriminate_from.mgalb14_boride: the other ternary icosahedral boride entry, orthorhombic, B12 icosahedra with metals in the interstices. Related in spirit, but no carbon or nitrogen and no B6 octahedra
discriminate_from.b12x2_alpha_boron: alpha-boron icosahedra with a two-atom inter-icosahedral unit and no metal

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 032 for the B-C-Ho-N host (HoB17CN, three samples) and for the carbonitride composition inside the B-Er host (Er1.12B17.64CN). The three papers across those hosts are titled on homologous p- and n-type boron-rich borides, on homologous rare-earth boron cluster compounds as a possible n-type counterpart, and on the doping effect in n-type rare-earth boron carbonitrides, so the series is named explicitly and repeatedly.

Neither reference carries any member of the series; for B-C-Ho-N nothing was printed at all. mp_id is null and stage 2 will have to work from the structure literature rather than from Materials Project.

The space group is the weak part of this entry and I want that recorded rather than buried. The series is monoclinic and I have written C2/m (12), but I am not confident of the setting and it should be checked against a published structure report before this is folded into a v4 seed file. Everything else here -- the icosahedra, the B6 octahedra, the C-B-C chains, the rare-earth site and the n-type conduction -- is on firm ground; the symbol is not.

Carbon and nitrogen are framework constituents in these compounds, not impurities. They arrive below the 5 atomic per cent threshold only because boron dominates the atom count, so a stage 3 pass that treats them as dilute dopants would be wrong.

display_name: Molecular coordination crystal (metal halide with neutral organic ligands)
formula_archetype: MX2Ln -- a transition-metal halide whose coordination sphere is completed by neutral organic ligands, packing as discrete molecules or as halide-bridged chains held together by van der Waals contacts
typical_space_group: low-symmetry monoclinic or orthorhombic; the copper chloride bis-dimethylsulfoxide compound is reported as orthorhombic, and the setting should be confirmed in stage 2

discriminate_from.organic_polymer: a purely organic conducting polymer with no metal coordination sphere at all
discriminate_from.bedt_ttf_salt: a charge-transfer salt in which the organic molecule carries the conduction electrons and the counter-ion is closed-shell. Here the organic ligand is an insulating spacer and the physics lives on the metal ion
discriminate_from.conductive_mof_2d: an extended coordination framework with covalent metal-ligand connectivity in two or three dimensions; this entry is for discrete molecules or single bridged chains
discriminate_from.formate_mof_perovskite: a three-dimensional coordination framework with perovskite topology
discriminate_from.cdi2_1t: an inorganic layered halide. Once neutral molecular ligands complete the coordination sphere the packing is molecular rather than layered-ionic

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 033 for the C-Cl-Cu-H-O-S host, whose only composition is CuCl2.2((CH3)2SO) across three single-crystal samples. The paper is on the low-temperature thermal conductivity of an antiferromagnetic S = 1/2 chain material, so what is measured is magnon and phonon heat transport along an isolated copper chain.

The entry is deliberately generic. What matters downstream is that these crystals are molecular: the electronic structure is that of an isolated complex, the band picture the rest of the taxonomy assumes does not apply, and Materials Project does not index them. No reference line was printed for this host and mp_id is null.
Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and sulfur here are constituents of the dimethyl sulfoxide ligand, not impurities or milling residue. A stage 3 pass must not read them as dopants.

formula_archetype: AM2O4 with a large divalent A (Ca, Sr, Ba, Eu) and an octahedral trivalent M (Cr, Fe, V, Ti, Sc, Al)

discriminate_from.spinel: the same AM2O4 formula and the entry these compositions would otherwise be filed under. Spinel needs the A cation to fit a tetrahedral site; calcium is far too large, so the structure instead builds double chains of edge-sharing MO6 octahedra enclosing eight-coordinate tunnels. It is the post-spinel phase, which is what the high-pressure work on these compositions is about
discriminate_from.hollandite: the other AM2O4-derived tunnel oxide. Hollandite tunnels are square and built from a different arrangement of double chains, and the tunnel cation is usually monovalent and partially occupied
discriminate_from.post_perovskite: CaIrO3-type, also a densified oxide reached under pressure, but at AMO3 with sheets of octahedra rather than at AM2O4 with tunnels
discriminate_from.rutile: the double chains of edge-sharing octahedra here are rutile-like fragments; rutile itself is the binary MO2 with no large A cation
discriminate_from.ruddlesden_popper: the other calcium chromium oxide structure present in the same host, at A2MO4 rather than AM2O4: perovskite slabs separated by rocksalt layers, with the transition metal in corner-sharing octahedra

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 033 for the Ca-Cr-O host: CaCr2O4 and Na0.25Ca0.75Cr2O4 are two of its three compositions, and one paper is on the electronic, thermoelectric and magneto-dielectric properties of the Ca1-xNaxCr2O4 series.
CaCr2O4 is a frustrated triangular-lattice antiferromagnet as well as a semiconductor, which is what brings it into a transport dataset; sodium on the calcium site hole-dopes the chromium sublattice.
Materials Project printed nothing at this stoichiometry for the host -- its entries are chromates, an oxychloride and Ca5Cr3O12 -- so mp_id is null and Pnma comes from the structure literature.
Marokite, CaMn2O4, is the near neighbour that is not this type: it is a different post-spinel, in Pbcm. Do not file a manganese member here without checking.

formula_archetype: A2X with A = Ca, Sr, Ba and X = N, plus the isoelectronic A2C carbides such as Y2C

discriminate_from.cdi2_1t: the same slab of edge-sharing octahedra, but the cation and anion roles are exchanged and the stacking is rhombohedral rather than single-layer hexagonal. In CdI2 the van der Waals gap is empty; here it holds the anionic electrons that carry the current
discriminate_from.bixbyite: anti-bixbyite Ca3N2 is the other calcium nitride and the one that dominates this host. It is a cubic vacancy-ordered framework with six-coordinate nitrogen and a wide gap, not a layered metallic subnitride
discriminate_from.alpha_nafeo2_layered: also R-3m with alternating cation layers, but an ordered rocksalt with every site occupied; the electride has a vacant layer holding electrons instead
discriminate_from.rocksalt_oxide: the parent structure. Remove every second cation layer from rocksalt and reduce the anion charge and this is what is left

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 033 for the Ca-N host, where Ca2N is one of two compositions alongside Ca3N2. The two are different materials: Ca3N2 is an insulating nitride and Ca2N is a two-dimensional electride, a metal whose conduction electrons sit in the interlayer gap as the anion rather than on any atom.

[ref 2] fixes the structure: Ca2N R-3m mp-2686 at hull 0.000 with 7 ICSD references, first on evidence for the host. mp_id is still left null here, per the rule that the taxonomy carries no structure ids.

The electride character is the reason this needs its own entry rather than being folded into a layered-halide prototype. The anionic electron layer is what a stage 2 structure file will not show and what a stage 3 electron count must not forget: Ca2N is formally (Ca2N)+ with one electron per formula unit in the gap.
The same structure holds for Sr2N, Ba2N and the carbide Y2C, so the entry is written for the family rather than the single compound.

display_name: Anhydrite CaSO4 and related AXO4 oxoanion salts
formula_archetype: AXO4 with a large divalent A (Ca, Sr, Ba, Pb) and a discrete tetrahedral XO4 group (X = S, Se, Cr)
typical_space_group: Cmcm (63) for anhydrite; the larger-cation members of the same formula take the barite type, Pnma (62)

discriminate_from.thortveitite_re2si2o7: another oxoanion salt, but built on a condensed Si2O7 double tetrahedron rather than an isolated XO4 group
discriminate_from.cu2v2o7_pyrovanadate: oxoanion oxide whose anion groups are condensed into pairs, with a transition metal outside them
discriminate_from.fresnoite: an isolated-tetrahedron oxide as well, but a layered polar titanosilicate rather than a simple divalent-cation sulfate
discriminate_from.perovskite: an ABO3 framework of corner-sharing octahedra with no discrete oxoanion. Sulfate oxygen belongs to the SO4 group and is never shared into such a network

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 033 for the Ca-O-S host, whose compositions are CaSO4 and Dy0.002CaSO4. The taxonomy had no sulfate or simple oxoanion-salt entry at all.

[ref 2] settles the structure: CaSO4 Cmcm mp-4406 at hull 0.000 with 12 ICSD references, well ahead of everything else offered for the host. Anhydrite is chains of alternating eight-coordinate CaO8 polyhedra and SO4 tetrahedra running along the c axis.

The hydrated calcium sulfates -- gypsum CaSO4.2H2O and bassanite -- are different phases with different structures and are not covered here; a composition carrying water must not be filed under this entry.

These materials reach a thermoelectric dataset as dosimeter phosphors and ionic conductors rather than as thermoelectrics. Rare-earth activators on the calcium site are charge-compensated by cation vacancies, which is worth carrying into stage 3.

formula_archetype: R2T3X9 with R a rare earth, T = Co, Rh, Ir or Pd, and X = Ga or Al

discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: the other cerium rhodium gallide in the same host, at RT2X2 in body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm. The 2-3-9 is C-centred orthorhombic, far more gallium-rich, and its rare-earth sites are dilute enough that the Kondo lattice is much weaker
discriminate_from.alb2: a simple hexagonal intermetallic with flat honeycomb nets; the 2-3-9 stacks corrugated transition-metal-gallium slabs with the rare earth between them
discriminate_from.cecu6: another orthorhombic cerium intermetallic with a low ordering temperature, but a Cu-rich CeCu6-type with no transition-metal-trielide slab
discriminate_from.caco2al8_pbam: also a rare-earth-poor ternary trielide with a transition metal, but a primitive Pbam framework at RT2X8 rather than the C-centred 2-3-9 stack

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 033 for the Ce-Ga-Rh host, one of whose three compositions is Ce2Rh3Ga9. The paper is on the transport and magnetic properties of new ternary Ce2T3X9 compounds, which names the family outright.

[ref 2] supports the setting: Ce2(Ga3Rh)3 Cmcm mp-1213907 at hull 0.000 is the same stoichiometry and space group, though it carries no ICSD reference, so Cmcm should still be confirmed against a published structure report.
These are dilute-rare-earth systems showing non-Fermi-liquid and heavy-fermion behaviour rather than thermoelectrics; they enter the dataset through their thermopower.

prototype: CaIn2, and its ordered LiGaGe variant
formula_archetype: RTX equiatomic, with a puckered honeycomb TX net and the large cation between the layers
typical_space_group: P6_3/mmc (194) for the disordered CaIn2 setting; P6_3mc (186) once T and X order, which removes the inversion centre

discriminate_from.tinisi_co2si: the RTX structure most equiatomic compounds take, orthorhombic Pnma with a three-dimensional TX framework. The hexagonal type has the same 1:1:1 ratio but builds a puckered honeycomb layer instead; these are genuinely different structures for one formula and the choice has to be made per compound
discriminate_from.zrnial_fe2p: the third common RTX type, hexagonal P-62m, built from trigonal prisms rather than a puckered honeycomb net. It is the type the neighbouring CePdIn and CePtIn hosts take, which is why the distinction matters in this chunk
discriminate_from.half_heusler: the cubic RTX ordering in F-43m, the cubic analogue of this stuffed-wurtzite stack. A hexagonal member of this family is sometimes called a hexagonal half-Heusler for exactly that reason
discriminate_from.wurtzite: the binary parent net. Pucker wurtzite and insert a cation layer between every pair of sheets and this is the result
discriminate_from.alb2: also a hexagonal layered intermetallic with the large cation between nets, but the net there is flat and graphite-like rather than puckered and tetrahedral

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 033 for the Ce-Pd-Sb host, whose single composition is CePdSb across three samples. CePdSb is a ferromagnetic Kondo compound with an unusually large thermopower, which is what both papers measure.

[ref 2] printed nothing at 1:1:1 for this host -- its entries are CeSb3Pd, Ce2(SbPd3)3, Ce(SbPd)2, Ce3Sb5Pd6 and Ce8SbPd24 -- so there is no database support and mp_id is null. The structure comes from the intermetallic literature.

Whether a given sample is the centrosymmetric CaIn2 setting or the ordered polar LiGaGe one is not settled here, and it is not a detail: the ordered variant is non-centrosymmetric, which matters for any spin-orbit or magnetoelectric reading of the transport. Both are named in the entry deliberately.

display_name: RnTmIn(3n+2m) homologous cerium indides (2-1-8 and 3-1-11 members)
prototype: Ho2CoGa8 for the 2-1-8 member, Ce3PtIn11 for the 3-1-11
formula_archetype: RnTmIn(3n+2m), built by stacking n RIn3 blocks with m TIn2 layers

discriminate_from.hocoga5_115: the m = n = 1 member of the same series, RTIn5, which the taxonomy already carries. This entry covers the members with more than one RIn3 block per transition-metal layer, the 2-1-8 and the 3-1-11, which are distinct structures with their own cells. A v4 seed file may prefer to merge the two entries into a single homologous family, as the taxonomy already does for the tetradymites
discriminate_from.cu3au_l12: the end member with no transition-metal layer at all: CeIn3 itself, cubic Pm-3m. It is the block this whole series is built from and it appears in the same chemistries
discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: a body-centred tetragonal BaAl4 derivative at RT2X2 -- a different stacking principle and a different stoichiometry
discriminate_from.zrnial_fe2p: the equiatomic RTIn phase that coexists with these members in both example hosts, hexagonal P-62m and built from trigonal prisms

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 033 for the Ce-In-Pd host (Ce2PdIn8) and the Ce-In-Pt host (Ce3PtIn11). Both are quantum-critical heavy-fermion superconductors and both of the papers behind them are thermoelectric studies of that criticality.
[ref 2] supports the 2-1-8: Ce2In8Pd P4/mmm mp-1102172 at hull 0.000 with one ICSD reference. Nothing was printed at 3-1-11, so that member rests on the structure literature alone.

The layer count is the tuning parameter of the family. Dimensionality falls from three-dimensional CeIn3 through the 3-1-11 and 2-1-8 to quasi-two-dimensional CeTIn5, and the ground state changes with it, so which member a sample is matters more here than the usual prototype assignment does.

formula_archetype: R4T3 with R a trivalent rare earth and T = Co or Ni, sitting between the R-rich R3T and R12T7 phases and the Laves phase RT2

discriminate_from.th7fe3: the other rare-earth-rich hexagonal P6_3mc binary in this corner of the phase diagram, at R7T3 rather than R4T3. Same space group and a similar trigonal-prismatic metalloid coordination, so the stoichiometry is the only discriminant and it has to be taken from the formula
discriminate_from.laves_phase: RT2, the cubic C15 MgCu2 phase that dominates the same binaries and that the neighbouring Ce-Ru and Co-Y hosts in this chunk take. It is far poorer in rare earth and has no R-R contacts of the kind that carry the magnetism here
discriminate_from.cacu5: RT5, the transition-metal-rich hexagonal end of the same binary series. R4T3 and RT5 are at opposite extremes of the Gd-Co system and must not be conflated because both are hexagonal

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 034 for the Co-Cu-Gd host. The taxonomy carries no rare-earth-rich R4T3 entry at all, only Th7Fe3 at R7T3 and the Laves phase at RT2.

The host is recorded with a genuine conflict and the entry should be read with that in mind. The three composition strings parse as Gd(Co1-xCux)3, i.e. R:T = 1:3, while the paper is titled Thermoelectric power of Gd4(Co1-xCux)3 compounds, i.e. R:T = 4:3. This entry follows the paper. If the composition strings turn out to be right, the correct prototype is instead the PuNi3-type RT3 rhombohedral stacking of CaCu5 and Laves blocks in R-3m, which the taxonomy also lacks and which a v4 file should add alongside this one.

No reference line was printed for this host, so there is no database support either way and mp_id is null. Stage 2 has to resolve which of the two stoichiometries was actually made before attaching a structure.

R4T3 compounds enter a thermoelectric dataset through their thermopower as itinerant magnets rather than as thermoelectrics; copper substitution on the cobalt site is a band-filling knob on that magnetism.

formula_archetype: M7X8, i.e. M1-xX at x = 1/8, with the metal vacancies ordered onto alternate metal layers of the NiAs parent; the wider family M1-xS runs from troilite FeS at x = 0 to Fe7S8
typical_space_group: C2/c (15) for the 4C monoclinic superstructure; the vacancy-disordered parent is NiAs P6_3/mmc (194), and 5C, 6C and 11C hexagonal superstructures appear at intermediate vacancy contents

discriminate_from.cr3s4_defect_nias: the same vacancy-ordering principle applied to the same NiAs parent, but at M3X4 -- one vacancy in every second metal layer rather than one in eight -- which gives a monoclinic C2/m cell of a different size. The vacancy concentration is the whole discriminant and it sets both the superstructure and the carrier count, so the two cannot share an entry
discriminate_from.nias: the undefected parent MX with every octahedral metal site filled. Troilite FeS is the vacancy-free end of this series and pyrrhotite is what it becomes as iron is removed
discriminate_from.pyrite: FeS2, a disulfide built on S-S dimers with iron octahedrally coordinated in a cubic cell. It is a different anion chemistry, not a more sulfur-rich member of this series
discriminate_from.marcasite: the orthorhombic FeS2 disulfide polymorph, and for the same reason not part of this family

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 034 for the Co-Fe-S host, whose compositions are Fe7-xCoxS8 with x from 2.8 to 5.0. The metal-to-sulfur ratio of 7:8 is pyrrhotite exactly, and the paper writes the series that way in its title.

[ref 2] does not offer it. Its primary is Fe(CoS)8 Fm-3m mp-1188182 at hull 0.002 with one ICSD reference, which is the pentlandite (Fe,Co)9S8 structure at a different metal-to-sulfur ratio, and the remaining entries are computed FeCo3S8, FeCoS2 and FeCoS4. So mp_id is null here and the disagreement is recorded on the host rather than resolved silently.

Vacancy ordering is the physically interesting part: the vacancies are what make pyrrhotite a degenerate p-type semiconductor and a ferrimagnet, and the superstructure periodicity shifts with composition and with thermal history. A sample quenched from above the vacancy-disordering temperature near 600 K can be the hexagonal disordered form instead, so the space group here is the ordered one at ambient and should not be asserted for a hot-pressed sample without a diffraction pattern.

formula_archetype: M9X8 with M = Fe, Co or Ni and X = S or Se; cubic close-packed sulfur with M8S8 cubane-like clusters of edge-sharing MS4 tetrahedra linked through an octahedral M site
