discriminate_from.cr3s4_defect_nias: a NiAs-derived sulfide in which every metal is octahedral and the structure is layered. Pentlandite is a cluster compound built mainly on tetrahedral metal, so the two are different close-packing schemes despite both being ordered M-S phases near M:S = 1
discriminate_from.nias: the simple hexagonal MX parent. Pentlandite is cubic and has no NiAs relationship at all, which is why it is kept apart from the pyrrhotite side of the same binary
discriminate_from.spinel: the other cubic close-packed sulfide with metal on both tetrahedral and octahedral sites. Spinel is AB2X4 with isolated tetrahedra, pentlandite is M9X8 with the tetrahedra condensed into M8 cubane clusters, and the cluster is the reason pentlandite is metallic where thiospinels are often semiconducting
discriminate_from.shandite: the other cobalt sulfide prototype in the taxonomy, Co3Sn2S2, a rhombohedral kagome metal with a main-group element in the structure. Same chemistry, unrelated structure

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 034 as the cobalt-rich alternative for the Co-Fe-S host, whose compositions run to Fe2Co5S8. Cobalt has no stable M7S8 pyrrhotite, so as cobalt replaces iron across that series the pentlandite Co9S8 field is the phase the samples are most likely to fall into, and the host is flagged mixed for that reason.
[ref 2] supports the structure indirectly: Fe(CoS)8 Fm-3m mp-1188182 at hull 0.002 with one ICSD reference is a mixed-metal M9S8 at the pentlandite space group.

Pentlandites have a thermoelectric literature of their own as earth-abundant metallic sulfides, so this entry is worth keeping even though it enters here as an alternative rather than as a primary assignment.

formula_archetype: Ln2M2Se2O3, more informatively written Ln2O2M2OSe2, with Ln a rare earth and M = Fe, Mn or Co

discriminate_from.zrcusias_1111: the 1111 oxychalcogenide already in the taxonomy, LnCuOSe, in which a fluorite Ln2O2 layer alternates with an antifluorite Cu2Se2 layer of corner-sharing CuSe4 tetrahedra. Here the fluorite Ln2O2 layer is the same but the transition-metal layer is an anti-CuO2 square net of M2O with selenium apices, which is a different and much more strongly correlated block. The oxygen is split between the two layers rather than sitting only in the Ln block
discriminate_from.fese_pbo: the anti-PbO Fe2Se2 layer of the iron-based superconductors. That layer has edge-sharing FeSe4 tetrahedra and no oxygen in it at all; the Fe2O square lattice here puts oxygen at the centre of every iron square, which halves the iron-iron hopping and makes these compounds Mott insulators rather than metals
discriminate_from.na2ti2sb2o_oxypnictide: the closest relative and the reason this entry needs stating separately. Na2Ti2Sb2O has exactly the same anti-CuO2 M2O square net, with Sb apices and plain alkali layers between. The Ln2O2 fluorite spacer is what distinguishes the rare-earth oxychalcogenides, and it is what makes them chemically tunable by rare-earth substitution
discriminate_from.bi2o2se_layered: Bi2O2Se, also a fluorite-oxide-plus-chalcogenide stack, but its selenium layer is a simple square net of anions with no transition metal in it
discriminate_from.ruddlesden_popper: layered perovskite blocks. There is no octahedrally coordinated perovskite block here; the M2O layer is planar and square-coordinated

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 035 for the Fe-Mn-Nd-O-Se host, whose three compositions are Nd2(Fe1-xMnx)2Se2O3 and whose paper is titled Synthesis, structure and properties of new layered oxyselenides Nd2(Fe,Mn)2Se2O3.

The taxonomy had no entry for this family even though it covers a substantial literature: the Ln2O2M2OSe2 oxychalcogenides are studied as two-dimensional Mott insulators and frustrated magnets, and their very low thermal conductivity is what brings them into a thermoelectric dataset.

The anti-CuO2 [M2O] layer is the defining feature. Iron sits in an MO2Se4 octahedron, oxygen bridges four iron atoms in the plane, and the selenium caps above and below connect to the [Ln2O2] fluorite slab. Writing the formula as Nd2Fe2Se2O3 hides this; writing it as Nd2O2Fe2OSe2 shows where the three oxygens go.

No reference line was printed for this host, so no mp_id is proposed. Stage 2 should look for La2O2Fe2OSe2 or the neodymium analogue in I4/mmm rather than for anything at the Nd2Fe2Se2O3 formula string.
Mixed Fe/Mn occupancy of the single transition-metal site is the norm in this family, so a structure file for it carries partial occupancies.

formula_archetype: R2TX6 with R a rare earth, T a late transition metal and X = Ge or Si
typical_space_group: Amm2 (38), with the ordered variant commonly refined in Cmce (64)

discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: the AB2X2 BaAl4 derivative. The R2TX6 type is built from the same kind of slabs but inserts extra germanium layers, giving a longer stacking period and a much lower transition-metal content
discriminate_from.banisn3_i4mm: the other BaAl4 derivative reached from the same chemistry, at RTX3. LaPdGe3 is that type and La2PdGe6 is this one, in the same host system, which is exactly why both entries are needed
discriminate_from.ypd2si_ordered_cementite: RT2X, transition-metal rich rather than germanium rich, orthorhombic Pnma and built on trigonal prisms
discriminate_from.alb2: the simple hexagonal parent of many rare-earth germanides. R2TX6 has a puckered rather than planar main-group net and an ordered transition-metal site

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 035 for the Ge-La-Pd host, one of whose three compositions is La2PdGe6 and whose paper is titled Physical properties of polycrystalline Dy2PdGe6 and La2PdGe6.

The R2TX6 germanides are a sizeable family in rare-earth intermetallic chemistry and the taxonomy had nothing at that stoichiometry. They matter here because the same host also contains LaPdGe3 and LaPd2Ge, so without this entry a genuinely three-structure host would have had to be collapsed onto two.

The space group is the known difficulty with this type: Ce2CuGe6 was originally described in Amm2 and several members have since been refined in the centrosymmetric Cmce setting with a doubled cell. Stage 2 should record which setting the paper used rather than assume one.
No reference line covered La2PdGe6 and mp_id is null.

formula_archetype: MX with M = Ga or In and X = S, Se or Te, stacked as X-M-M-X tetralayers with a metal-metal bond through the middle
typical_space_group: R3m (160) for the gamma polytype and P6_3/mmc (194) for the beta polytype

discriminate_from.layered_in2se3: In2Se3, the sesquichalcogenide of the same binary. It is also layered but its layer is a quintuple In-Se-In-Se-In sheet with ordered indium vacancies and no metal-metal bond, and it has its own alpha-beta-gamma polytypism. Getting these two apart is the whole reason this entry exists
discriminate_from.in4se3: In4Se3, the indium-rich Zintl phase with (In3)5+ polycations, orthorhombic Pnnm. Same binary again, entirely different bonding
discriminate_from.inte_tlse: InTe in the TlSe type, a chain compound with indium in two different valence states. It is the 1:1 III-VI compound of the heavier chalcogen and is not layered
discriminate_from.mos2_2h: the transition-metal dichalcogenide layer, MX2 with trigonal-prismatic metal. Here the layer is MX with tetrahedral metal and a covalent M-M dimer
discriminate_from.layered_ges: the orthorhombic puckered GeS and SnSe layer. Same 1:1 stoichiometry and also van der Waals, but a group-IV monochalcogenide with a lone pair rather than a group-III dimer

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 035 for the In-Se-Si host, whose compositions are all In0.9Si0.1Se and whose paper is titled Thermoelectric Properties of Te-doped In0.9Si0.1Se with Enhanced Effective mass.

The taxonomy had layered_in2se3 and in4se3 for the In-Se binary but nothing for InSe itself, which is the most studied member of the III-VI layered semiconductors and has a long thermoelectric and optoelectronic literature.

Polytypism is the thing to record in stage 2. InSe is usually grown as the gamma rhombohedral R3m polytype and GaSe as the beta hexagonal one, they differ only in the stacking of identical tetralayers, and papers are frequently vague about which they have.
No reference line was printed for this host and mp_id is null.

formula_archetype: MO2 with M = Zr or Hf; a distorted fluorite in which the metal is sevenfold rather than eightfold coordinated

discriminate_from.fluorite_oxide: the cubic aristotype, Fm-3m, which is what zirconia and hafnia become at high temperature or when stabilised by yttria or ceria. Baddeleyite is the ambient monoclinic distortion of it and the two are the same family related by a displacive transition, not different structures in the usual sense. Recording them apart matters because the monoclinic-to-tetragonal step near 1400 K in zirconia is the transformation-toughening transition and is what a high-temperature measurement crosses
discriminate_from.rutile: the other common MO2 framework, tetragonal with sixfold metal. Titanium takes rutile and hafnium takes baddeleyite at the same stoichiometry, so the group-4 dioxides do not share one prototype
discriminate_from.anatase: the metastable titania polymorph, also sixfold
discriminate_from.corundum: M2O3, a different stoichiometry and hexagonal close-packed oxygen
discriminate_from.amorphous: what a sputtered or atomic-layer-deposited hafnia film usually is as deposited. The distinction has to be made from the processing, not from the formula

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 035 for the Hf-O host. [ref 1] TEDesignLab gives HfO2 P2_1/c mp-352 at hull 0.000 with 11 ICSD references, well ahead of every alternative, and the taxonomy had no monoclinic MO2 entry at all -- only cubic fluorite_oxide, which is the wrong ambient structure for both hafnia and zirconia.

The entry is wanted well beyond that one host: zirconia and hafnia are among the most studied oxides there are, and filing them under cubic fluorite would misstate the ambient structure of every sample that is not stabilised.

The polymorph sequence is monoclinic P2_1/c to tetragonal P4_2/nmc near 1400 K to cubic Fm-3m near 2600 K in zirconia, with hafnia higher still. A thermoelectric measurement rarely reaches these, which is why the monoclinic form is the one to assign by default.

Ferroelectric orthorhombic Pca2_1 hafnia, the phase behind hafnia-based memories, is a thin-film-stabilised polymorph and belongs in other_polymorphs rather than in a thermal sequence. [ref 2] lists it as mp-685097 at hull 0.029.

prototype: metal phthalocyanine and metalloporphyrin molecular crystals
formula_archetype: M(macrocycle) -- a square-planar metal ion held in a tetrapyrrole ring, packing as discrete neutral molecules
typical_space_group: low-symmetry monoclinic or triclinic, commonly P2_1/c or P-1; thin films are usually textured polycrystalline or amorphous rather than single crystal

discriminate_from.organic_polymer: a covalently linked conjugated chain. The transport physics is different in kind: a polymer conducts along its backbone and is doped by charge transfer onto that backbone, while a molecular semiconductor conducts by hopping between whole molecules and its mobility is set by how the rings stack
discriminate_from.molecular_coordination_crystal: the other molecular entry in the taxonomy, a metal halide completed by neutral organic ligands such as CuCl2(DMSO)2. There the organic part is an insulating spacer around a magnetic ion; here the macrocycle itself is the conjugated electronic system and the metal is a substituent on it
discriminate_from.bedt_ttf_salt: a charge-transfer salt with a closed-shell counter-ion and a partially filled band. Metalloporphyrin films as measured here are neutral and semiconducting, with a hopping activation energy rather than a band
discriminate_from.conductive_mof_2d: an extended coordination framework. These molecules are not linked to each other by coordination bonds at all

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 035 for the H-Ni-P host, whose only composition is recorded as NiTPP across three thin-film samples, from a paper titled Polaron activation energy of nano porphyrin nickel(II) thin films.

The taxonomy had organic_polymer for conducting polymers and molecular_coordination_crystal for metal-halide-plus-ligand crystals, but nothing for the metallomacrocycles, which are the oldest and largest family of organic semiconductors and recur in thermoelectric work on evaporated films.

The element set is a trap for an automated pass. H-Ni-P looks like a nickel phosphide with hydrogen; it is a metal-free formula parse of a molecule whose carbon and nitrogen have been dropped and whose P is the porphyrin label rather than phosphorus. Any stage 3 pass must not read H or P here as dopants.

Polymorphism is the rule in this family -- phthalocyanines have alpha, beta and x forms differing in the tilt of the stacks, with quite different mobilities -- and evaporated films are often the metastable form or amorphous. Stage 2 should not expect a single Materials Project entry; mp_id is null.

formula_archetype: AB4 with A an alkaline earth, europium or a rare earth and B a triel or tetrel

discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: the ordered ternary derivative of exactly this cell, in which the two crystallographically distinct B sites of BaAl4 are taken by different species. Same space group, same atom positions, same coordination; the only difference is whether the 4d and 4e sites carry one element or two. The taxonomy already had the derivative but not the parent, which is the gap this entry fills
discriminate_from.banisn3_i4mm: the other ordering of the same cell, BaNiSn3 in the non-centrosymmetric I4mm, reached when the ordering removes the inversion centre. Its polar axis is why these compounds are looked at for Rashba physics
discriminate_from.caal2si2_zintl: the trigonal AB2X2 Zintl layer type. It is easy to confuse with ThCr2Si2 by formula and is a completely different structure
discriminate_from.cual2_c16: the other common AB2-to-AB4 tetragonal intermetallic, I4/mcm, built on antiprisms rather than on the BaAl4 slab
discriminate_from.laves_phase: AB2 close packing with no distinct main-group layer

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 035 for the Eu-Ga host, whose three single-crystal samples are all EuGa4 and for which [ref 2] gives EuGa4 I4/mmm mp-21884 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references.

The taxonomy carried two orderings of the BaAl4 cell, thcr2si2_122 and banisn3_i4mm, but not the binary parent. Assigning a binary AB4 compound to the ternary ordered entry would have asserted an ordering that cannot exist when there is only one B species, so the aristotype has to stand on its own.

The family is large and thermoelectrically relevant beyond this host: EuAl4 and EuGa4 are charge-density-wave and valence-fluctuation systems, and the alkaline-earth gallides and aluminides recur in Zintl-adjacent transport work.

EuAl4 has a charge-density-wave transition near 140 K with a small orthorhombic distortion; EuGa4 does not, and both order magnetically near 15 to 20 K. The magnetic transitions are not structural and do not belong in a phases array.

formula_archetype: A0.33MoO3 (A = Li, K, Rb, Cs, Tl)

discriminate_from.blue_bronze_a03moo3: the entry this would otherwise be filed under, and the reason a second molybdenum bronze is needed. The two are separated by one third of an alkali atom per molybdenum and by their entire electronic character: A0.30MoO3 is monoclinic C2/m, built from slabs ten octahedra wide, and is a quasi-one-dimensional metal with a Peierls transition near 180 K, while A0.33MoO3 is monoclinic P2_1/c, built from finite condensed octahedral clusters linked into chains, and is a small-gap semiconductor with no charge-density wave. A transport paper that calls its sample a quasi-one-dimensional semiconductor is describing this structure and not the blue bronze
discriminate_from.tungsten_bronze: the AxWO3 tunnel and cubic bronzes, a fully three-dimensional corner-sharing framework with the alkali in tunnels rather than a cluster-chain slab structure
discriminate_from.vanadium_bronze: the same guest-in-a-bronze principle applied to the V2O5 host lattice, a different framework and a different octahedral connectivity
discriminate_from.hollandite: an oxide framework with genuine 2x2 edge-sharing octahedral tunnels, three-dimensionally connected
discriminate_from.li2mo3_honeycomb: a reduced lithium molybdate built on Mo3 triangular clusters in a honeycomb sheet, not an MoO3-derived bronze slab
discriminate_from.reo3_wo3: the stoichiometric corner-sharing MO3 network with no alkali guest at all

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 036 for the Li-Mo-O host, whose three single-crystal samples are all Li0.33MoO3 and whose paper is titled Anisotropic transport in the quasi-one-dimensional semiconductor Li0.33MoO3.

The taxonomy already carried blue_bronze_a03moo3, itself proposed in chunk 011 to stop molybdenum bronzes being filed under tungsten_bronze. That entry is explicitly A0.3MoO3 with A = K, Rb, Tl and space group C2/m, so it does not cover the 0.33 stoichiometry, a lithium guest, or a semiconductor. Stretching it would merge a Peierls metal and a small-gap semiconductor into one prototype.

The lithium member is the least well characterised of the family and the P2_1/c setting is carried over from the potassium and caesium red bronzes rather than measured here, so the Li-Mo-O record is recorded at medium confidence. Lithium is small enough that a different stacking or a different cluster condensation is possible; stage 2 should confirm the space group before accepting one.

Materials Project offers nothing at this stoichiometry for the chemistry -- [ref 2] for Li-Mo-O ranks LiMoO2 R-3m mp-19338, Li2MoO4 R-3 mp-25080 and three further lithium molybdates, each with one to three ICSD references, none of them a bronze. mp_id is left null rather than guessed.

formula_archetype: M3X4 (M = Nb, Ta; X = S, Se, Te), often written M3+xX4 with the channel partly filled

discriminate_from.mote2_1t_prime: the other compound of this same Nb-Te host. NbTe2 is a distorted octahedral layer with metal-metal zigzag chains inside a two-dimensional van der Waals slab; Nb3Te4 is not layered at all -- it is a three-dimensional framework of face-sharing NbTe6 octahedra forming infinite Nb chains along the hexagonal c axis, with wide empty channels between them. The two are the reason this host is recorded as mixed
discriminate_from.ta4site4_chain: the closest relative in the taxonomy and the entry Nb3Te4 would otherwise be forced into. Ta4SiTe4 is orthorhombic and built from discrete Ta4 chain columns held apart by silicon; here there is no third element, the chains are Nb3 triangles stacked into face-sharing octahedra, and the framework is hexagonal with channels that accept extra metal
discriminate_from.nbse3_chain: a true trigonal-prismatic MX3 column compound with van der Waals gaps between the columns, not a corner- and face-sharing octahedral framework
discriminate_from.tl2mo3se3_chain: also a cluster-chain compound, but built from Mo3 clusters condensed into chains that are separated by thallium; there the guest cation is essential to the structure, while the Nb3Te4 channel can be empty
discriminate_from.cr3s4_defect_nias: shares the M3X4 formula and is also derived from octahedral packing, but it is a monoclinic cation-vacancy-ordered NiAs derivative, a layered defect structure rather than a channel framework

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 036 for the Nb-Te host, where one of the two compositions is Nb3Te4 and its paper is titled Electrical Properties of a Quasi-One-Dimensional Nb3Te4 Single Crystal.

[ref 2] supports the structure: Nb3Te4 P6_3/m (176) mp-7564 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references. The block ranks NbTe4 P4/mcc mp-20196 first on 14 ICSD references, but that is the tetratelluride, a different compound and a different chain system.

The family is thermoelectrically and physically relevant beyond this host: Nb3X4 with X = S, Se, Te are quasi-one-dimensional superconductors, and the channel can be filled to Nb3+xTe4, which tunes the carrier concentration in the same way a skutterudite void filler does. A record in this prototype should therefore say whether the channel is filled.

Grouping this with the layered ditellurides would have been the alternative and is wrong: the transport anisotropy here runs along a chain axis in a three-dimensional framework, not within a van der Waals plane.

formula_archetype: R2M3X5 (R = rare earth, thorium or uranium; M = late transition metal; X = Si, Ge)

discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: the other compound of the La-Pd-Si host and by far the more familiar R-M-X silicide. RM2X2 is the body-centred tetragonal BaAl4 derivative, a clean alternation of R layers and MX4 tetrahedral slabs in I4/mmm. R2M3X5 is orthorhombic Ibam with a quite different building principle: the transition metal sits on two inequivalent sites, the silicon forms both isolated atoms and Si-Si pairs, and the rare earth occupies channels in that network. Neither the symmetry nor the coordination carries over, so a 2-3-5 composition cannot be filed under the 122 entry
discriminate_from.mo2feb2_u3si2: the U3Si2-type tetragonal R2MX2 relative, also built from a rare-earth network with main-group pairs, but P4/mbm and a different stoichiometry
discriminate_from.ce2cuge6_type: another orthorhombic R2MX6-class ternary with main-group dimers; it is a layered structure derived from BaAl4 slabs, while the 2-3-5 type is a three-dimensional channel framework
discriminate_from.zrnial_fe2p: the hexagonal equiatomic 1-1-1 type. It recurs in the same chemistries and is easy to reach for when a ternary silicide has no better home, but the formula and the coordination are both different
discriminate_from.tinisi_co2si: the orthorhombic equiatomic 1-1-1 type, Pnma, for the same reason

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 036 for the La-Pd-Si host, whose three samples are LaPd2Si2, Ce0.1La0.9Pd2Si2 and La2Pd3Si5. The first two are the 122 phase, already in the taxonomy; La2Pd3Si5 had no entry at all.

The R2M3X5 silicides and germanides are a sizeable family in heavy-fermion and Kondo-lattice transport work -- Ce2Pd3Si5 and U2Co3Si5 are both studied for magnetic ordering and hybridisation -- so this is a gap rather than a one-off. Without it La2Pd3Si5 would have had to go to unresolved_crystalline or be mislabelled as a 122.

The Ibam setting is the one usually reported for the U2Co3Si5 type; several members are described in the closely related Sc2Fe3Si5 type in P4/mnc, which is a distinct structure with the same stoichiometry. Which of the two La2Pd3Si5 takes was not determinable from the composition, so the La-Pd-Si record carries this only as an alternative prototype and stage 2 should check the space group.
[ref 2] for the host returns La(SiPd)2 I4/mmm mp-4954 with 4 ICSD references, plus two computed entries at other stoichiometries; there is nothing at the 2-3-5 formula, so no mp_id is proposed.

display_name: Tl4TiS4-type (isolated TiS4 tetrahedra with thallium counterions)
formula_archetype: A4MX4 (A = Tl, K, Rb, Cs; M = Ti, Ge, Sn; X = S, Se)

discriminate_from.chalcopyrite: the other way a group-14/transition-metal sulfide with tetrahedral MS4 units can be built, but there the tetrahedra share every corner into a continuous diamond-like framework. In the 4-1-4 type the MS4 tetrahedra are isolated ortho-anions separated by Tl cations, so the M-S connectivity that carries transport in a chalcopyrite does not exist here
discriminate_from.cdi2_1t: the layered TiS2 structure, which is what a Ti-S composition usually means. TiS2 is octahedral Ti in edge-shared layers; Tl4TiS4 is tetrahedral Ti in discrete anions, and the two share no structural motif despite the shared elements
discriminate_from.argyrodite: also a cation-rich chalcogenide built around isolated MX4 tetrahedra, but its cations are mobile in a cubic close-packed anion array and it is a superionic conductor. Tl4TiS4 is monoclinic with ordered Tl on fixed sites
discriminate_from.tl5te3: the other thallium chalcogenide in the taxonomy, a Cr5B3-derived tetragonal telluride with no isolated tetrahedral anion

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 037 for the S-Ti-Tl host, whose three samples are all Tl4TiS4 from one paper on the effect of nonstoichiometry on its thermoelectric properties.
[ref 1] TEDesignLab returns Ti(TlS)4 in space group 14 as PRIMARY, which is the monoclinic setting normally reported for this structure type and is the basis for the space group given here.

[ref 2] Materials Project has nothing at the 4-1-4 formula. It returns Ti(TlS2)2 Pbca mp-14441 and Ti5TlS8 C2/m mp-1101049, both of which are layered thiotitanates at quite different Tl:Ti ratios, so no mp_id is proposed and the two references do not agree about what exists in this chemistry.
Isolated ortho-thioanion salts of this kind are a recurring motif in low-thermal-conductivity chalcogenide searches, so the entry is written for the A4MX4 family rather than for Tl4TiS4 alone.

formula_archetype: A3B5 (A = actinide or rare earth; B = late transition metal or group 13-14)

discriminate_from.cu3au_l12: the other compound of the Sn-U host. USn3 is the cubic AuCu3 type, a simple ordered fcc arrangement; the 3-5 phase is orthorhombic with a much larger cell and a different coordination, so the host holds two prototypes and cannot carry one label
discriminate_from.mn5si3_d88: the hexagonal 5-3 intermetallic, close in stoichiometry when read carelessly but inverted (A5B3 rather than A3B5) and in P6_3/mcm rather than Cmcm
discriminate_from.th7fe3: another actinide-rich binary intermetallic from the same corner of the taxonomy, hexagonal P6_3mc at 7:3
discriminate_from.cmcm_snse_ht: shares the space group only. That entry is a high-temperature layered chalcogenide and has no bearing on an intermetallic

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 037 for the Sn-U host, whose compositions are U3Sn5 (2 samples) and USn3 (1). The paper is the report of the new uranium compounds U3Sn5 and U3Ge5, so the 3-5 phase is the subject of the measurement rather than an impurity.

[ref 2] Materials Project has no U3Sn5 entry at all. It returns USn3 Pm-3m mp-20336 on 9 ICSD references, which covers the minority composition, plus computed U3Sn7, U5Sn4, USn and USn2. The absence of the 3-5 formula from the snapshot is why no mp_id is proposed here; it is not evidence that the phase does not exist.

The Pu3Pd5 type is the structure usually assigned to U3Sn5 in the actinide intermetallic literature. That assignment was made from materials knowledge, not from either reference, and stage 2 should confirm the space group from the paper before an mp_id is attached.

formula_archetype: elemental actinide

discriminate_from.solid_solution_alloy: the entry the taxonomy uses for elemental metals that are simply close-packed or body-centred cubic, and the entry that gamma-U above 1049 K belongs to. alpha-U is not close-packed: it is a corrugated two-layer structure with strongly anisotropic bonding and a charge-density-wave instability, which is why it gets its own entry rather than being swept into the generic metal label
discriminate_from.beta_u_sigma_tp30: the intermediate phase of the same element, tetragonal with 30 atoms per cell, reached between about 941 and 1049 K
discriminate_from.a7_rhombohedral: the other low-symmetry elemental structure in the taxonomy, the Bi and Sb arsenic type. Both are distorted from a simple packing, but A7 is rhombohedral with three-fold coordination and A20 is orthorhombic
discriminate_from.beta_sn_a5: the other elemental distortion entry, tetragonal, for Sn

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 037 for the U host, three samples of polycrystalline uranium across two papers on electrical resistivity and thermoelectric power.
[ref 2] gives U Cmcm mp-44 at hull 0.000 on 21 ICSD references, far ahead of anything else in the chemistry, which is the ambient alpha phase.

Uranium was the only elemental host so far whose ambient structure is not covered by an existing entry. Every previous elemental metal in the ledger (Ca, Sr, Ag, Cu, Ni, W, Pt and others) went to solid_solution_alloy because fcc, bcc and hcp all sit under that display name. Putting alpha-U there would have asserted a close-packed metal, which it is not.

[ref 2] also lists U P4_2nm mp-43 on 4 ICSD references. That is the low-temperature alpha-1 charge-density-wave distortion of the same structure, below about 43 K, and is recorded on the host as another polymorph rather than as a thermal phase.

formula_archetype: elemental actinide, intermediate temperature phase

discriminate_from.alpha_u_a20: the ambient phase of the same element, orthorhombic Cmcm, below about 941 K
discriminate_from.solid_solution_alloy: where gamma-U, the body-centred cubic phase above about 1049 K, belongs. beta-U sits between the two and is neither the corrugated layer structure nor a simple cubic metal
discriminate_from.a15_cr3si: the other Frank-Kasper topologically close-packed entry in the taxonomy. A15 and the sigma phase are the two common Frank-Kasper types and are easily confused; A15 is Pm-3n with 8 atoms per cell, the sigma phase P4_2/mnm with 30
discriminate_from.cual2_c16: another tetragonal intermetallic entry, but a simple 2-atom-type structure with none of the Frank-Kasper coordination polyhedra

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 037 for the U host, whose robust measured window is 297-1019 K and whose full span reaches 1374 K, so the measurement runs through the alpha to beta transition and, at the top of the span, the beta to gamma one.

[ref 2] gives U P4_2/mnm mp-93 on 4 ICSD references, which is this phase. The chunk file ranks it below the bcc entry mp-108 at 6 references, but both are genuine high-temperature phases of uranium and the reference counts do not order the thermal sequence.

beta-U is isostructural with the sigma phase of the transition-metal alloys, which is why the entry names both. It is proposed separately from alpha-U rather than as a space-group variant of it because the two structures share neither symmetry nor coordination.
The transition temperatures recorded on the U host, about 941 K for alpha to beta and about 1049 K for beta to gamma, come from materials knowledge, not from either paper, and are marked as such.

display_name: CsAg5Te3-type (silver telluride tunnel framework with rattling caesium)
formula_archetype: AAg5X3 (A = Cs, Rb; X = Te, Se, S)

discriminate_from.argyrodite: the other silver-rich chalcogenide famous for ultralow thermal conductivity, and the one most likely to absorb this compound by mistake. Argyrodite is cubic with Ag disordered over many partially occupied sites in a close-packed anion array; CsAg5Te3 is tetragonal with Ag on ordered sites and its low thermal conductivity comes from concerted rattling of Cs and Ag rather than from superionic diffusion
discriminate_from.ag2se_naumannite: the binary silver chalcogenide entry. No alkali cation, no tunnel framework, and a superionic transition that CsAg5Te3 does not have
discriminate_from.clathrate_i: also a guest-in-framework structure with rattling, but the clathrate framework is a covalent tetrahedral cage network and the guest sits in a closed polyhedral cage. Here the caesium occupies open tunnels in an ionic Ag-Te framework
discriminate_from.ba3cu14te12_polytelluride: the nearest existing entry, another coinage-metal polytelluride with a heavy electropositive cation, but at a different stoichiometry and with Te-Te bonding that CsAg5Te3 does not have
discriminate_from.tl5te3: another A5X3 chalcogenide with a heavy monovalent cation, but the Cr5B3-derived tetragonal type, and the 5 and 3 are assigned to different elements

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 037 for two adjacent hosts: Ag-Cs-Te (CsAg5Te3, 2 samples) and Ag-Cs-S-Te (CsAg5TeS2, 2 samples). The second is the x = 2 member of the CsAg5Te3-xSx series reported in the same group of papers, so one entry covers both.

[ref 2] gives CsAg5Te3 P4_2/mnm mp-9206 at hull 0.000 on 1 ICSD reference, which is the source of the space group here. One reference is thin, so the PRIMARY is weak in the sense the chunk header describes, but it is the only structure reported for the formula and it agrees with the tetragonal cell the papers describe.

The papers are the 2016 report of concerted rattling and ultralow thermal conductivity in CsAg5Te3 and the 2018 report of the two-dimensional CsAg5Te3-xSx semiconductors. Both describe the structure, so a stage 2 reader can confirm the assignment from the text rather than from composition alone.
[ref 2] also returns CsAg3Te2 C2/m mp-1213692, a computed entry at a different stoichiometry; it is not this structure type.

formula_archetype: RAgX2 (R = heavy rare earth; X = Te, Se)

discriminate_from.alpha_nafeo2_layered: the ordered rocksalt ABX2 layered type, R-3m, where the two cations alternate in close-packed layers. RAgTe2 has the same ABX2 stoichiometry and is the trap this entry exists to avoid, but the reported cells are primitive trigonal or tetragonal rather than rhombohedral and the silver is tetrahedrally rather than octahedrally coordinated
discriminate_from.cdi2_1t: the parent layered MX2 type. Reading RAgTe2 as a filled CdI2 with the rare earth in the van der Waals gap is tempting and wrong; the rare earth is a framework cation, not an intercalant
discriminate_from.chalcopyrite: the other way an ABX2 ternary chalcogenide is commonly built, diamond-like and three-dimensional. RAgTe2 is layered and the rare earth is not tetrahedrally coordinated
discriminate_from.argyrodite: another silver telluride with low thermal conductivity, but cubic, silver-rich and superionic

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 037 for the Ag-Te-Tm host, two samples of TmAgTe2 from the 2015 computational and experimental investigation of TmAgTe2 and XYZ2 compounds.

The space group is deliberately left unresolved. [ref 2] returns TmAgTe2 P-42_1m mp-1078600 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference as PRIMARY and TmAgTe2 P-3m1 mp-12953 at hull 0.015 with 1 ICSD reference immediately behind it, plus a computed P3m1 entry. One reference each is not enough to separate them, and the two settings describe genuinely different layer stackings rather than a minor distortion.

That is why the entry is written for the RAgTe2 family with two candidate space groups rather than pinned to one. The Ag-Te-Tm record is assigned at low confidence for the same reason, and stage 2 should read the space group out of the paper, which reports a refinement.
The XYZ2 half of the paper title is a computational screen over many ABX2 compounds, so this family is likely to recur in later chunks and is worth a shared entry rather than a one-off.

formula_archetype: RMB4 (R = rare earth or actinide; M = Al, Cr, Mo, W)
representative_materials: YCrB4 relatives in the alpha form

discriminate_from.ycrb4_type: the alpha form of the same RMB4 composition, Pbam, and the reason this entry is needed. Both are boron sheets of fused five- and seven-membered rings alternating with metal layers, but the ring network is stitched together differently and the two have different symmetry and different physics. alpha-YbAlB4 and beta-YbAlB4 are distinct compounds with distinct ground states, and beta is the one with the quantum critical point
discriminate_from.alb2: the simple hexagonal diboride, planar six-membered boron rings. The RMB4 borides are built from the same planar sp2 boron idea but with a five-seven ring network and two different metals
discriminate_from.mgalb14_boride: the other Al-containing boride entry, an icosahedral boron framework at a much higher boron content. YAlB14 in this same chunk goes there and YbAlB4 does not, despite the shared elements
discriminate_from.ub12_boride: the cubic boron cage entry, again a different boron network

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 037 for the Al-B-Yb host. The paper is the report of the thermoelectric response near a quantum critical point of beta-YbAlB4, so the beta polymorph is explicitly the material measured.

This is a case where the reference and the paper point at different polymorphs. [ref 2] ranks YbAlB4 Pbam mp-1191244 first on 4 ICSD references, which is the alpha form, and lists YbAlB4 Cmmm mp-1095659 at 2 references below it. ICSD reference counts describe how often each has been deposited, not which one this paper made, and the title names beta. The host record follows the paper and keeps alpha as an alternative.

Without this entry the only available boride of the right composition was ycrb4_type, which would have filed the beta compound under the alpha structure and lost exactly the distinction the paper is about.
TmAlB4 in the same chunk is the opposite case: its only reference is Pbam and its paper says nothing about a polymorph, so that host goes to ycrb4_type.

formula_archetype: complex alkali / alkaline-earth aluminoborate fluoride

discriminate_from.fresnoite: the other non-centrosymmetric oxide entry reached for when a complex polar oxide has no home. Fresnoite is Ba2TiSi2O8, a tetragonal layered silicate; this is a hexagonal borate with BO3 triangles and a fluoride anion
discriminate_from.langasite: another non-centrosymmetric complex oxide entry, trigonal P321, built from tetrahedral and octahedral cation sites rather than from planar borate groups
discriminate_from.borocarbide_1221: a boride-carbide intermetallic, not an oxide, and listed only because the formula contains B
discriminate_from.mayenite: a complex calcium aluminate framework oxide with cage anions. The nearest structural idea in the taxonomy, but a different cation set, a different anion and a cubic cell

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 037 for the Al-B-Ba-K-Li-O host, two single-crystal samples of K3Ba3Li2Al4B6O20F from a paper on the physical properties of this nonlinear optical crystal.

[ref 2] gives K3Ba3Li2Al4B6O20F P-62c mp-1195057 at hull 0.000 on 1 ICSD reference, an exact formula match. That is a single reference, but the entry is the compound itself rather than a neighbour, and the paper is a single-crystal study that reports the structure, so the space group is well supported for this host even though the reference count is thin.

This is a genuine one-off. The compound is a designed NLO crystal rather than a member of a studied thermoelectric family, and it appears here because someone measured its thermal transport. The entry is kept narrow for that reason rather than generalised to a family that may not exist in this dataset.
The fluorine in the formula is a structural anion on its own site, not a dopant, even though it falls below the 5 at.% split and is listed as a dopant candidate in the chunk file.

display_name: Molten chalcogen (covalent chain melt above the melting point)
formula_archetype: elemental S, Se or Te, or a chalcogen-rich melt, measured entirely above its melting point

discriminate_from.liquid_metal: the existing melt entry, written for liquid metals and molten alloys with electronic conduction assumed. Liquid selenium is a semiconductor: it is a covalent melt of twofold-coordinated chain fragments with a band gap, and it undergoes its own semiconductor-to-metal transition on heating. Filing it under liquid_metal would assert free-electron transport that the measurement is specifically about not having
discriminate_from.molten_salt: the entry proposed in chunk 025 for ionic melts such as molten KNO3, which conduct by ion migration. A chalcogen melt is neither ionic nor metallic, which is why the taxonomy now needs a third melt entry rather than a second
discriminate_from.amorphous: a solid without long-range order at the measurement temperature. Amorphous selenium is a real and important material, but it is glassy selenium below the glass transition, not selenium above its melting point, and the two have different transport
discriminate_from.trigonal_te: the ambient crystalline structure of the element, the helical chain structure that selenium and tellurium share. It is the correct entry for solid selenium and is recorded on the Se host as an alternative for exactly that reason

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 037 for the Se host, three samples of In-doped selenium from a paper on the electrical conductivity and thermoelectric power of liquid selenium.

It follows the precedent set by molten_salt in chunk 025: where a paper measures a melt, the record should say so rather than attach the crystalline structure the material has at room temperature. The reasoning that kept ionic melts out of liquid_metal keeps covalent chalcogen melts out of it too.

No mp_id belongs on this entry. [ref 1] TEDesignLab does return Se P3_121 mp-14 at hull 0.006 on 27 ICSD references, which is a correct description of the ambient trigonal solid and simply not the state measured. The various cubic Se entries in [ref 2] at hulls of 0.18 to 0.59 are high-pressure or computed cells and are not reached on heating either.

The chunk file shows no measured range line for this host, so the temperature window could not be checked against the 494 K melting point from the data. The assignment rests on the paper title, which says liquid selenium, and the Se record is held at medium confidence for that reason.

The chain-fragment structure of the melt is also why doping is hard to describe here: indium cross-links and terminates selenium chains rather than taking a lattice site, so the Se host records its role as unknown rather than as substitutional.

formula_archetype: R2T6Al19 (R = rare earth; T = Co, Fe, Ru)

discriminate_from.caco2al8_pbam: the other aluminide in the same paper and the same host. CaCo2Al8 is the 1-2-8 stoichiometry, orthorhombic Pbam, with the rare earth in a channel of the aluminium framework. The 2-6-19 phase has a different transition-metal-to-aluminium ratio and a different framework, and the two coexist in the Al-Co-Pr host, which is why both entries are needed
discriminate_from.y2co3ga9_type: the 2-3-9 stoichiometry, Cmcm, the family the Ce2T3Al9 compounds belong to. Nearest neighbour in stoichiometry and chemistry and the easiest confusion; 2-6-19 is twice as transition-metal-rich per rare earth
discriminate_from.cecr2al20_cage: the 1-2-20 CeCr2Al20 cage compound, cubic Fd-3m, the most aluminium-rich of this group. Its rare earth sits in a closed Frank-Kasper Al16 cage; the 2-6-19 framework is not a closed-cage structure
discriminate_from.ybfe2al10_cage: the 1-2-10 YbFe2Al10 cage aluminide, orthorhombic Cmcm, another rare-earth-in-aluminium-framework compound at an intermediate stoichiometry

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 038 for the Al-Co-Pr host, which holds PrCo2Al8 and Pr2Co6Al19 from a single 2005 paper titled exactly PrCo2Al8 and Pr2Co6Al19: Crystal structure and electronic properties. The 1-2-8 member has a home in the taxonomy already; the 2-6-19 member does not, and without this entry it would have to be filed as unresolved.

The space group is recorded as C2/m but is NOT confirmed and must not be trusted by stage 2. No reference line in the chunk file covers the 2-6-19 stoichiometry at all -- [ref 2] returns only Pr7Al7Co6 P4/mbm, Pr2AlCo2 C2/m, Pr2Al3Co14 R-3m, Pr2Al2Co15 R-3m and PrAl4Co Pmma, none of which is this compound -- so the value here rests on recollection of the R2T6Al19 family and nothing else. The paper reports a single-crystal structure determination, so stage 2 should read the space group out of it and correct this entry.

The entry is written for the R2T6Al19 family rather than for Pr2Co6Al19 alone because the 2-6-19 stoichiometry recurs across the rare earths with Co, Fe and Ru, and a one-off entry would have to be duplicated the next time one appears.
The Al-Co-Pr host record is flagged is_mixed and carries this id as an alternative rather than as its primary prototype, because PrCo2Al8 and Pr2Co6Al19 are one sample each and neither dominates.

display_name: GaFeO3 / AlFeO3-type polar orthorhombic oxide (kappa-alumina related)
formula_archetype: ABO3 with A = Al, Ga, Fe and B = Fe, Cr, at a tolerance factor far too small for perovskite

discriminate_from.perovskite: the default reading of any ABO3 formula and the trap this entry exists to avoid. AlFeO3 is not a perovskite: Al3+ is far too small for the twelve-coordinate A site, and the compound instead builds a polar framework of corner- and edge-sharing octahedra plus one tetrahedral cation site, in Pna2_1 rather than Pnma
discriminate_from.corundum: the structure the same cations adopt as the binaries alpha-Al2O3 and alpha-Fe2O3. The 1:1 ordered ternary is a distinct polar structure, not a cation-ordered corundum
discriminate_from.spinel: the other ordering the Al-Fe-O chemistry adopts, as the FeAl2O4 hercynite spinel that [ref 2] ranks first for this host. Spinel is cubic and centrosymmetric with tetrahedral and octahedral cations in a close-packed oxygen array; this type is orthorhombic and polar, and the two are different compounds at different Al:Fe ratios rather than polymorphs
discriminate_from.ymno3_hexagonal: the other entry reached for when an ABO3 oxide refuses to be a perovskite because the A cation is too small. YMnO3 goes hexagonal P6_3cm with five-coordinate Mn; AlFeO3 stays orthorhombic and keeps octahedra

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 038 for the Al-Fe-O host, which holds AlFeO3 alongside a lithium ferrite spinel. [ref 2] supports the structure directly: AlFeO3 Pna2_1 (33) mp-25693 at hull 0.029 with 1 ICSD reference.

The reference PRIMARY for this host is Al2FeO4 Fd-3m mp-31801 on 3 ICSD references, which is the hercynite spinel, and that is a correct description of the chemistry but not of this composition. The host record is therefore flagged mixed and carries both prototypes.

This structure type is the same one as kappa-Al2O3 and epsilon-Fe2O3, which is why the entry is named for the family rather than for AlFeO3 alone. It is a well-studied magnetoelectric because the polar Pna2_1 framework is non-centrosymmetric.

The single ICSD reference behind the space group is thin in the sense the chunk header describes, but the entry it comes from is the compound itself rather than a neighbouring stoichiometry, and it agrees with the polar orthorhombic structure this family is known for.

formula_archetype: AT5X2 or AT2X5 (A = actinide or rare earth; T = Pd, Ni; X = Al)

discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: the other body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm intermetallic in the taxonomy and the one a reader will reach for on seeing I4/mmm with an f-electron element. ThCr2Si2 is the 1-2-2 BaAl4 derivative with a single transition-metal layer per cell; this type has a much thicker transition-metal-aluminium slab between the actinide layers, which is why its 5f electrons are more two-dimensional and why NpPd5Al2 superconducts where its 122 relatives do not
discriminate_from.baal4_type: the parent of the whole BaAl4 / ThCr2Si2 tetragonal family, also I4/mmm, at the 1-4 binary stoichiometry. Same symmetry, much simpler cell
discriminate_from.hocoga5_115: the other heavy-fermion tetragonal layered aluminide-gallide type, P4/mmm, where the 1-1-5 stoichiometry stacks CeIn3 and CoIn2 blocks. It is the nearest thing in spirit -- a quasi-two-dimensional f-electron superconductor built by inserting a transition-metal block -- but the block and the symmetry differ
discriminate_from.cacu5: the hexagonal way a 1-5 stoichiometry is usually built. NpPd5Al2 has five palladium per actinide but is tetragonal and has two additional aluminium atoms, and is not a CaCu5 derivative

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 038 for the Al-Np-Pd host, two single-crystal samples of NpPd5Al2 from the two Physical Review B papers on its transport, magnetic and Kondo behaviour. NpPd5Al2 is the transuranium heavy-fermion superconductor reported in 2007, and its structure is described in that literature as the tetragonal ZrNi2Al5-type, I4/mmm.

Note the element-role swap. In ZrNi2Al5 the aluminium is the majority species; in NpPd5Al2 palladium occupies the sites aluminium holds in the prototype and aluminium occupies the nickel sites. The type name is kept because that is what the literature uses, but stage 2 should not assume the element ordering follows the prototype formula.

The space group here comes from materials knowledge, not from the references, and stage 2 should confirm it. [ref 2] returns only NpAl3Pd2 P6/mmm mp-1206258 at hull 0.104 with no ICSD reference -- a computed entry at a different stoichiometry and a different symmetry, which is neither the compound measured nor evidence for this one. The Al-Np-Pd host record is held at medium confidence for that reason.

Transuranium compounds are thinly represented in both reference sets, so an absent reference here says more about the snapshot than about the compound. Both papers are single-crystal studies that report the structure, so the assignment is confirmable by reading.

display_name: Al12W-type (bcc packing of aluminium icosahedra, 1/0 approximant)
formula_archetype: Al12M (M = W, Mo, Re, Mn, Tc, Cr)

discriminate_from.quasicrystal_approximant: the entry for genuine Mackay- and Bergman-cluster approximants, whose unit cells are large and whose clusters are hierarchical. Al12W is often called the 1/0 approximant because it is a body-centred packing of single aluminium icosahedra, but it is a small ordered cell with a fully determined structure and should not be filed with the large approximants whose structures stage 2 cannot resolve. The distinction matters in this host because the Al-Re system also produces true icosahedral quasicrystals
discriminate_from.cecr2al20_cage: the other aluminium cage entry, CeCr2Al20, cubic Fd-3m, where the guest sits inside a sixteen-atom Frank-Kasper aluminium cage. Same idea of a single heavy atom inside an aluminium polyhedron, different polyhedron, different symmetry and a second metal in the framework
discriminate_from.cual2_c16: the tetragonal C16 aluminide, the simple binary aluminium-rich intermetallic. Much lower aluminium content and no icosahedral coordination
discriminate_from.ub12_boride: the cubic cage entry on the boride side, a twelve-atom cuboctahedral boron cage. The formula looks similar and the structure is not

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 038 for the Al-Re host, whose two compositions are Al12Re and Al11Re4. [ref 2] supports this one directly: Al12Re Im-3 (204) mp-1648 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references, the top-ranked entry for the host.

The dataset tags the composition Al12Re_IAC_1_0, where IAC_1_0 is the curator writing the 1/0 approximant designation into the composition string. That is the reason this entry exists separately from quasicrystal_approximant: the 1/0 label is accurate but the structure is a small ordered cell that stage 2 can resolve to mp-1648, unlike the 2/1 and higher approximants.

The second composition in the host, Al11Re4, is a different and more complex intermetallic and is not covered by this entry. Its structure could not be established from the evidence available, so the Al-Re host is flagged mixed with unresolved_crystalline as the alternative rather than being stretched to fit here.
The papers on this host are about aluminium-based icosahedral quasicrystals and approximants, so the surrounding literature is quasicrystalline even though this particular phase is periodic.

formula_archetype: ASn2Pn2 (A = Na, K, Sr; Pn = P, As)

discriminate_from.caal2si2_zintl: the other trigonal layered Zintl entry at the same 1-2-2 stoichiometry, and the one this composition would otherwise be forced into. CaAl2Si2 is P-3m1 with one [Al2Si2] slab of corner- and edge-sharing tetrahedra per cell and a divalent cation between slabs. Here the cation is a monovalent alkali, the anionic block is a puckered SnAs double layer, and the stacking is rhombohedral with three slabs per cell
discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: the third 1-2-2 layered type, body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm. Same formula again, different symmetry and a different anion network, and its A cation sits in a square antiprism rather than between van der Waals slabs
discriminate_from.tetradymite: the rhombohedral R-3m layered chalcogenide with van der Waals gaps, which this compound resembles in stacking and shares a literature with, since both are studied for anisotropic transport. Bi2Te3 is a quintuple slab of one metal and one chalcogen with an empty gap; here the slab is an SnAs bilayer and the alkali occupies the gap
discriminate_from.layered_ges: SnAs-type bonding appears in both, but GeS/SnS is an orthorhombic puckered 1-1 structure with no intercalated cation
discriminate_from.nazn4as3_type: the closest entry in the whole taxonomy and the one to check first: also R-3m, also an alkali layer against an anionic pnictide slab, also proposed by this project. It sits at AM4X3 with a thicker mixed slab of two different anion environments, where this type is a single [Sn2As2] bilayer at AM2X2. If either entry is rejected in review these two should be considered together

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 039 for the As-Na-Sn host, two polycrystalline samples of NaSn2As2 from the paper on axis-dependent carrier polarity. NaSn2As2 is one of the goniopolar materials, whose Seebeck coefficient changes sign between the in-plane and cross-plane directions, and that anisotropy is a property of exactly this layered stacking, so the prototype is the point of the measurement rather than incidental to it.

[ref 2] supports it directly: Na(SnAs)2 R-3m (166) mp-9378 at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference. One reference is thin attestation. The other entry returned for the host, Na5SnAs3 P2_1/c mp-5248, is a different stoichiometry and is not the compound measured.
The space group comes from the reference and from the structure literature on NaSn2As2 and NaSn2P2, not from the paper, so stage 2 should confirm the slab count and the Na site.

formula_archetype: AB2

discriminate_from.crsi2_c40: the hexagonal C40 stacking of the same AB2 close-packed layer sequence, P6_222. C40, C54 and C11b differ only in the stacking period and are routinely mistaken for one another on formula alone
discriminate_from.tisi2_c54: the orthorhombic Fddd member of that same trio. Its entry, proposed in chunk 5, closes by asking for this one by name
discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: the other I4/mmm structure in the taxonomy and the one a tetragonal AB2 gets confused with. ThCr2Si2 is a ternary 1-2-2 BaAl4 derivative with three distinct crystallographic sites and an X-X dimer along c; C11b is a binary with no third element and no dimer
discriminate_from.alb2: hexagonal AlB2 puts a planar honeycomb net of the B species between metal layers. C11b has no such net, only close-packed layers stacked ABB
discriminate_from.laves_phase: the other way an AB2 intermetallic packs, tetrahedrally close-packed as cubic C15 or hexagonal C14. Same stoichiometry, a different principle

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 039 for the Au-Yb host, whose two compositions are YbAu2 and YbAu3. [ref 2] ranks YbAu2 I4/mmm (139) mp-1668 first for the host at hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, which is the C11b type, and five references is good attestation by the standards of this tail.

This id was requested by name in chunk 5. The tisi2_c54 entry ends with the line that Al6Re5Si4 in the Al-Re-Si host is reported as MoSi2-type and has no home; that host should be revisited if this entry is accepted.
MoSi2 itself is a much-studied high-temperature silicide, so the entry is likely to be wanted again further down the tail rather than serving only this host.

formula_archetype: AnB2C (An = U, Th)

discriminate_from.borocarbide_1221: the other borocarbide entry, LuNi2B2C, body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm, where B-C-B units bridge rare-earth layers across a transition-metal sheet. That family is the nickel borocarbide superconductors; here there is no transition metal at all and the symmetry is rhombohedral
discriminate_from.alb2: the hexagonal diboride, and the entry a UB2 fragment would suggest. Adding the carbon changes the boron net and the stacking, and UB2C is not a carbon-doped UB2
discriminate_from.boron_carbide: the icosahedral B12 entry. At B2C per metal the boron is nowhere near icosahedral; it forms two-dimensional networks with the carbon
discriminate_from.crb_feb_chain: the low-boron binary borides with zigzag boron chains. Ternary here, and the carbon is a structural constituent rather than an impurity

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 039 for the B-C-U host, two samples of UB2C from the paper on electron correlation effects and ferromagnetic order in beta-UB2C. The paper names the beta polymorph explicitly, so the compound has at least two forms and the one measured is identified.

[ref 2] gives UB2C R-3m (166) mp-11332 at hull 0.051 with 2 ICSD references. It ranks UBC Cmcm mp-5816 above it on 3 references, but UBC is a different stoichiometry and is not what this paper made. The R-3m cell is the evidence for the space group named here; it was not taken from the paper and stage 2 should confirm which polymorph R-3m corresponds to.
Actinide borocarbides are thinly covered in both reference sets, so two ICSD references for the exact composition is better support than it looks.

formula_archetype: M2B5-x (M = Mo, W, Re, Tc), boron-deficient with wide homogeneity

discriminate_from.alb2: the parent idea and the entry these would otherwise be forced into. AlB2 alternates metal layers with one flat honeycomb boron sheet. Here the boron sheets alternate flat and puckered, the stacking period is three times longer and rhombohedral, and the boron sublattice is systematically deficient. MoB2 and Mo2B5 are different compounds in the same binary and should not share a label
discriminate_from.wb4_type: the next boride up in the same two binaries, hexagonal P6_3/mmc at M:B of 1:4. The B-Mo and B-W hosts each hold one composition of each type, which is why both entries are proposed together
discriminate_from.crb_feb_chain: the low-boron end of the same binaries, with boron in zigzag chains rather than sheets
discriminate_from.cr5b3_type: the metal-rich tetragonal boride, again the same chemistries at a different boron content
discriminate_from.boron_carbide: icosahedral boron, which does not appear until far higher boron fractions and not with these metals

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 039 for the B-Mo and B-W hosts, which hold Mo2B5 and W2B5 respectively, both from the same 1979 paper on the physical properties of the higher borides of molybdenum and tungsten. One paper, two chemistries, the same pair of phases in each.

Note the hull values. Both R-3m entries sit far above the hull in the 2019 snapshot, 0.450 and 0.547, while carrying 4 and 1 ICSD references. This is the case the chunk header warns about: hull is not the selector, deposition is, and these are long-known refractory phases rather than computational curiosities.
The composition is written M2B5 by convention but the phase is boron-deficient and is more accurately W2B5-x; the boron count should not be taken literally in stage 2.

formula_archetype: MB4 (M = W, Mo, Mn, Cr), with partially occupied boron sites

discriminate_from.w2b5_type: the other higher boride in the same two binaries and the same paper, rhombohedral R-3m at a lower boron content. The two are adjacent phases in the same phase diagram and are the reason both hosts are flagged mixed
discriminate_from.ycrb4_type: the ternary RMB4 borides with five- and seven-membered boron rings, orthorhombic Pbam. Same MB4 boron count in the formula, but two metals of different size and a completely different boron net
discriminate_from.alb2: the honeycomb diboride. WB4 is often described as an AlB2-derived structure with extra boron in the metal layer, but the boron sites are partially occupied and the cell is doubled along c, so it is not the same structure
discriminate_from.b12x2_alpha_boron: icosahedral boron with an inter-icosahedral species. WB4 is boron-rich for a transition-metal boride but has no icosahedra; it is still a layered metal-boron structure
discriminate_from.ub12_boride: the cubic cage boride at MB12. Higher boron content and a genuine boron polyhedron around the metal

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 039 alongside w2b5_type, for the same two hosts and the same paper on the higher borides of molybdenum and tungsten. WB4 and MoB4 both return P6_3/mmc entries with 3 ICSD references each.

Both entries sit high above the hull in the 2019 snapshot. That is expected for a phase whose boron sites are partially occupied, since a defect structure cannot be represented faithfully by an ordered computational cell, and it is not evidence against the phase.
WB4 is also studied as a superhard material, so the entry may be reached again from a mechanical rather than a thermoelectric direction.
The composition is nominal. The stoichiometry of the tungsten tetraboride phase has been revised more than once in the literature, and stage 2 should not assume exactly four boron per metal.

display_name: Cr5B3-type tetragonal boride and the Mo5SiB2 T2 phase
formula_archetype: M5X3, and the ternary M5SiB2 T2 phase (M = Mo, W, Nb, Cr)

discriminate_from.tl5te3: the entry that already carries the Cr5B3 structure type in this taxonomy, but as a thallium telluride. Tl5Te3 is a Cr5B3-derived tetragonal chalcogenide with mobile heavy cations and semiconducting transport; this entry is the metallic refractory boride branch of the same type, and filing a molybdenum boride under a thallium telluride would be a routing error even though the space group is shared
discriminate_from.mo2feb2_u3si2: the other ternary molybdenum boride, tetragonal P4/mbm at 2-1-2 with isolated boron pairs. Same chemistry, a different boron motif and a different cell
discriminate_from.w2b5_type: the boron-rich end of the same binaries. At M5B3 the boron is in isolated atoms and pairs inside a metal framework, not in sheets
discriminate_from.crsi2_c40: the disilicide the Mo-Si binary reaches at much higher silicon content. The T2 phase is a boride with silicon in it, not a silicide with boron in it
discriminate_from.a15_cr3si: the other refractory Mo-Si intermetallic, cubic Pm-3n. Mo3Si and Mo5SiB2 coexist in the same alloys and are easy to conflate

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 039 for the B-Mo-Si host, two bulk samples of Mo5SiB2 from the paper on the electrical and thermal properties of single-crystalline Mo5X3 phases. [ref 2] returns exactly one entry for the host, SiB2Mo5 I4/mcm (140) mp-4984 at hull 0.000 with 4 ICSD references, so the evidence is unambiguous.
The T2 phase is one of the central constituents of Mo-Si-B ultra-high-temperature alloys, which is why single crystals of it exist to measure at all.

The taxonomy already describes the Cr5B3 type in passing, inside the tl5te3 entry, but only as the parent of a chalcogenide. This entry gives the type its own home so that borides are not routed through a telluride.

formula_archetype: A3B-B2-O9, equivalently A(B-1/3B-2/3)O3 (A = Ba, Sr; B- = Ca, Mg, Zn, Ni; B- = Nb, Ta)
typical_space_group: P-3m1 (164) when ordered; Pm-3m (221) or Fm-3m (225) when the B site disorders

discriminate_from.double_perovskite: the 1:1 rock-salt B-site ordering at A2BB-O6, cubic Fm-3m with a doubled cell. This entry is the 1:2 ordering, where two B- layers alternate with one B- layer along the cubic body diagonal, giving a trigonal cell. The two orderings are set by the charge and radius difference between the B cations and produce different symmetries, and 1:2 order is the reason these compositions carry one-third and two-thirds B-site occupancies rather than halves
discriminate_from.perovskite: the disordered aristotype, which is where these compositions end up when the ordering is lost. Heavy substitution on the B site, as with the iron here, does exactly that, so the distinction is a matter of degree and stage 2 should take the ordering from the diffraction pattern rather than from the formula
discriminate_from.hexagonal_perovskite_polytype: the face-sharing polytypes a large A cation drives. Both are trigonal or hexagonal and both are reached from a barium perovskite, but the 1:2 ordered type is still a fully corner-sharing octahedral network, only with a chemically ordered B sublattice
discriminate_from.layered_double_perovskite: A-site rather than B-site ordering, with the ordering driven by oxygen vacancies in the lanthanide layer
discriminate_from.ruddlesden_popper: an intergrowth with rock-salt layers, which changes the A:B ratio. Here the A:B ratio is still exactly 1:1

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 039 for the Ba-Ca-Nb-O and Ba-Ca-Fe-Nb-O hosts, four compositions across two hosts, all of the form BaCa0.33(Nb,Fe,Y)0.67O3. That Ca:Nb ratio of one to two is the signature of the 1:2 ordered complex perovskite, and both hosts come from the same paper on the role of dopants in the electrical and catalytic properties of these materials.
[ref 2] supports it: Ba3CaNb2O9 P-3m1 (164) mp-1214569 at hull 0.000, the only entry it returns at hull zero for that host, though with no ICSD reference attached in the snapshot.

BCN18, Ba3Ca1.18Nb1.82O9-d, is a well-known high-temperature proton conductor, which is what these samples are being measured as. The off-stoichiometry in its name is the oxygen-vacancy and proton-uptake variable, so a formula in this family should not be expected to be exactly 3-1-2.

Where iron substitutes heavily on the niobium site, as in BaCa0.33Nb0.34Fe0.33O3, the 1:2 order is likely to be partial or lost. Those records name this prototype but keep perovskite as the alternative rather than asserting long-range order that no measurement here establishes.

display_name: Gillespite-type layered cuprosilicate (Han Blue, Egyptian Blue)
formula_archetype: AMSi4O10 (A = Ba, Ca, Sr; M = Cu, Fe)

discriminate_from.cuprate_chain: the other entry built on square-planar CuO4. In the cuprates those squares share corners into chains or planes and the copper carries the conduction. Here each CuO4 square is isolated, bridged only through silicate rings, which is why the compound is an insulator and a pigment rather than a conductor, and why its magnetism is that of a two-dimensional lattice of nearly free spins
discriminate_from.tenorite: binary CuO, also with square-planar copper. No silicate framework and no alkaline-earth layer
discriminate_from.fresnoite: the other barium silicate entry in the taxonomy, Ba2TiSi2O8, also layered and also tetragonal. Its sheets are built of Si2O7 groups and square-pyramidal TiO5, and it is a polar piezoelectric; the gillespite sheets are four-membered silicate rings around a square-planar cation and the structure is centrosymmetric
discriminate_from.delafossite: layered copper oxide again, but with linearly coordinated Cu(I) between octahedral layers. Here copper is divalent and square-planar
discriminate_from.langasite: another complex tetrahedral-framework silicate reached from oxide chemistry, but a piezoelectric germanate-silicate framework, not a layered sheet silicate

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 039 for the Ba-Cu-O-Si host, two single crystals of BaCuSi4O10 from the paper on the heat capacity, thermal expansion and heat transport of Han Blue. The reference agrees on the structure once the formula is rewritten: BaCu(Si2O5)2 is BaCuSi4O10, and mp-6127 is P4/ncc (130) with 4 ICSD references, which is the gillespite type.

The material is the ancient pigment Han Blue, and its calcium analogue CaCuSi4O10 is Egyptian Blue. Both are studied now for their isolated Cu(II) square lattices rather than for their colour, and the same isolated-square motif is why they turn up in a thermal transport study.
This is a genuinely insulating silicate rather than a thermoelectric candidate, and it is in the set because heat transport was measured. Stage 2 should expect no carrier transport to model.

formula_archetype: AMO4 (A = Ca, Sr, Ba or Pb; M = W or Mo)

discriminate_from.perovskite: the other barium tungstate and molybdate in this data set. A scheelite has isolated MO4 tetrahedra and eight-coordinate A, so it is a wide-gap insulator; BaMoO3 and BaWO3 are corner-sharing MO6 perovskites and are metallic. One oxygen per formula unit separates them and the transport could hardly be more different
discriminate_from.rutile: also AO2-derived and tetragonal, but built from edge-sharing octahedral chains rather than isolated tetrahedra
discriminate_from.reo3_wo3: the binary WO3 framework of corner-sharing octahedra, with no large A cation at all
discriminate_from.sc2w3o12_type: the other isolated-WO4-tetrahedra family here. A2M3O12 is orthorhombic and fully corner-linked through the A octahedra, and its high-pressure form is a defect scheelite, which is exactly why the two need to stay apart
discriminate_from.fresnoite: another Ba oxide with isolated tetrahedral anions, but a layered silicate-titanate with square-pyramidal Ti

structure_database_candidates.source: ref 2 on the Ba-Mo-O host, hull 0.000, icsd 9, primary

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 040 for the Ba-O-W host, two polycrystals of BaWO4 from a paper on the thermal and mechanical properties of BaWO4 crystal. The structure type is named as absent from the taxonomy in the discriminate_from block of sc2w3o12_type, proposed from chunk 030, so this closes that gap.

The reference agrees strongly: BaWO4 I4_1/a (88) mp-19048 carries 11 ICSD references at hull 0.000 and is the best-attested entry in the host. TEDesignLab instead returns Ba3W2O9, which is a different compound and not the composition measured.

Scheelites are wide-gap insulators grown as laser and scintillator crystals, and this sample is in the set because thermal conductivity was measured on such a crystal. Stage 2 should expect no carrier transport.
BaMoO4 is the scheelite that the Ba-Mo-O reference ranks first, so this entry also covers the molybdate that has to be argued away there in favour of perovskite BaMoO3.

display_name: BaCu6-dTe6Q quaternary copper telluride (Q = S, Se)
formula_archetype: BaCu6-dTe6Q (Q = S or Se)
typical_space_group: not established here; Materials Project carries the composition only as a low-symmetry P2 (3) cell and no ICSD-backed setting was available

discriminate_from.ba3cu14te12_polytelluride: the nearest neighbour and the entry this would otherwise be forced into. Ba3Cu14-dTe12 is a ternary barium copper telluride with a Cu:Te ratio near 1.2; here the ratio is near 1.0 and a third chalcogen occupies its own site, which is the compositional variable the paper scans. Both are copper-deficient, so the deficiency is not what separates them
discriminate_from.tetrahedrite: also a copper-deficient chalcogenide with a low thermal conductivity attributed to loosely bound Cu, but a cubic 12-4-13 framework with no large alkaline-earth cation
discriminate_from.ba_1214_chalcogenide: the other barium copper chalcogenide proposed in this project. The 1-2-1-4 compounds are ordered tetrahedral frameworks with a group 14 element; this one has no tetrel and four times the copper
discriminate_from.argyrodite: the other family whose transport is dominated by mobile copper or silver, but built on a rigid chalcogen sublattice with cations disordered over many partial sites

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 040 for the Ba-Cu-Se-Te host, whose two samples are BaCu5.9SeTe6, from the paper on the thermoelectric properties of the quaternary chalcogenides BaCu5.9STe6 and BaCu5.9SeTe6.

The space group is deliberately left open. The only reference entry is a computed P2 (3) cell at hull 0.053 with no ICSD backing, which is the kind of low-symmetry ordering Materials Project generates for a partially occupied site rather than a measured structure. Stage 2 must resolve the setting from the paper, not from this entry.

The copper deficiency in Cu5.9 is intrinsic to the compound rather than a doping choice, and the low thermal conductivity these compounds are studied for is attributed to that partially occupied, loosely bound copper. Stage 3 should read the missing 0.1 Cu as non-stoichiometry, not as a vacancy dopant.

formula_archetype: (BiCuSeO)n(Bi2O2Se)m, n = m = 2 for Bi6Cu2Se4O6

discriminate_from.zrcusias_1111: BiCuSeO itself, one of the two members of the intergrowth. The 1111 structure alternates Bi2O2 and Cu2Se2 layers one for one; the intergrowth inserts an extra Bi2O2Se block, which halves the copper content and changes the carrier count, so calling the intergrowth 1111 would misstate both
discriminate_from.bi2o2se_layered: the other member. Bi2O2Se alternates Bi2O2 layers with Se square layers and contains no copper at all
discriminate_from.misfit_layered_chalcogenide: also two alternating subsystems, but incommensurate ones with no common cell. This intergrowth is commensurate and has a single periodic cell
discriminate_from.homologous_tetradymite: the same idea of stacking two block types in a variable ratio, but on the rocksalt and quintuple-layer blocks of the Pb-Bi-Te system

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 040 for the Bi-Br-Cu-O-Se host, two bulk samples of Bi6Cu2Se3BrO6 from a paper on the electrical and thermal transport properties of an n-type member of this family.

The composition is what identifies it: Bi6Cu2Se4O6 is exactly two BiCuSeO formula units plus two Bi2O2Se units, and the bromide here replaces one selenium, which is the aliovalent substitution that makes the compound n-type where BiCuSeO is a p-type conductor.
The only reference entry is Cu3BiSe2BrO8 mp-628637, a different compound of the same five elements, so no mp_id is carried. Stage 2 must resolve the structure from the paper.

This matters beyond the two samples here: BiCuSeO is a large and well-studied host in this data set, and an intergrowth that halves its copper content is not the same material even though four of its five elements match.

formula_archetype: A16Pn11 (A = Ca or Sr; Pn = Sb or Bi)

discriminate_from.yb14mnsb11_zintl: the entry this is closest to and shares a host with. A14MPn11 has a central MPn4 tetrahedron, a linear Pn3 unit and isolated Pn3-; A16Pn11 has two more A cations per formula and no transition-metal-centred tetrahedron, so Ca16Bi11 and Ca14AlBi11 are two distinct compounds in the Bi-Ca host rather than one with a substitution
discriminate_from.zintl_11_6_12: a different A:Pn ratio and a different polyanion
discriminate_from.th3p4: also a cation-rich pnictide with isolated anions, but cubic and with a fixed 3:4 ratio
discriminate_from.zintl_9_4_9: the other cation-rich Zintl stoichiometry in the taxonomy, with its own polyanion topology

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 040 for the Bi-Ca host, which holds one sample of Ca16Bi11 and one of Ca14AlBi11 and therefore needs two prototypes.

The space group is left unverified on purpose. The compound is reported in the literature as its own A16Pn11 structure type, but no setting was confirmed against a reference here and neither TEDesignLab nor Materials Project returns the composition. TEDesignLab offers only Ca2Bi and Materials Project only Ca5Bi3, Ca11Bi10 and CaBi2, none of which is either composition in this host.

The description that is load-bearing is the count, not the setting: sixteen cations to eleven pnictogens, with no transition metal. If a reviewer can attach a setting and an ICSD entry this record should be upgraded rather than merged into the 14-1-11 entry.
Ca11Bi10 in the reference is a different compound again, the Ho11Ge10 type, and should not be used to resolve this one.

formula_archetype: R12Co5Bi (R = Y or a heavy rare earth)
typical_space_group: not verified here; reported as a tetragonal structure type of its own

discriminate_from.th3p4: the other rare-earth pnictide intermetallic family used for thermoelectrics here, but cubic, with a 3:4 ratio and no transition metal
discriminate_from.yb14mnsb11_zintl: also a very cation-rich rare-earth pnictide, but a Zintl phase with a defined polyanion. The 12-5-1 compounds are metallic with a single isolated Bi per formula and a cobalt sublattice that carries the magnetism
discriminate_from.mn5si3_d88: another cation-rich binary-derived intermetallic with a stuffed site, which is the closest structural idea, but hexagonal and with no rare earth
discriminate_from.laves_phase: the default answer for a rare-earth transition-metal binary, ruled out by the 12:5 ratio and by the bismuth

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 040 for the Bi-Co-Gd host, whose two samples are Gd12Co5Bi and Gd12Co5.3Bi from an inorganic chemistry paper that reports the compounds themselves.

The setting is left unverified. The compounds are reported as a structure type of their own in the R12Co5Bi series, but no space group was confirmed against a reference here and neither reference returns the composition.

The 5.3 in Gd12Co5.3Bi is the interesting part of the pair: the cobalt site is partially occupied and the paper varies it, so stage 3 should read the excess as non-stoichiometry on a host site rather than as a dopant.
The rare-earth sublattice is magnetic, so transport in this family is coupled to magnetic order and a thermopower measured across an ordering temperature is not describing a structural transition.

display_name: CsMBi3Te6 and CsM2Bi3Te7 layered caesium bismuth telluride (M = Pb, Sn)
formula_archetype: CsMBi3Te6 and CsM2Bi3Te7 (M = Pb or Sn)

discriminate_from.csbi4te6: the parent of the family and the entry this would otherwise be forced into. CsBi4Te6 is held together by Bi-Bi bonds within the anionic slab, and that bond is the structural feature its low-temperature performance is attributed to. Replacing one bismuth by a divalent Pb or Sn removes the Bi-Bi bond and leaves a plain rocksalt-type slab, so the two are not one prototype with a substitution
discriminate_from.homologous_tetradymite: also rocksalt-type slabs of Pb, Bi and Te, but neutral slabs stacked directly on one another with no alkali metal between them
discriminate_from.tetradymite: the binary quintuple layer, with no cation between the slabs
discriminate_from.bi_chalcogenide_complex: the catch-all for Bi chalcogenides whose every composition is its own structure. These two are a defined pair of stoichiometries reported together, so they earn an entry

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 040 for the Bi-Cs-Pb-Te host, one sample each of CsPbBi3Te6 and CsPb2Bi3Te7, from the paper that reports both as new thermoelectric compounds with low-dimensional structures.
Neither reference returns either composition, so there is no mp_id and no space group here. Stage 2 must take the structure from the paper.

The family exists because CsBi4Te6 works well below room temperature, and the measured window here, 79 to 350 K, is that same regime. Grouping these under csbi4te6 would make an intact Bi-Bi bond look like a property of four compounds when it belongs to one.
The M = Sn members are not in this host but are reported in the same paper, so the entry is written to cover them if they appear later in the set.

display_name: RE2O2Pn rare-earth oxide pnictide with a pnictogen square net
formula_archetype: RE2O2Pn (Pn = Sb or Bi), also written RE2PnO2

discriminate_from.bi2o2se_layered: the same I4/mmm alternation of a fluorite-like oxide layer with a flat anion layer, and the entry this would otherwise be forced into.
