The difference is which way round the cations and anions sit and, more importantly, whether the flat layer is bonded: Bi2O2Se has isolated Se2- and a band gap, while RE2O2Pn has a hypervalent, bonded pnictogen square net and is metallic or semimetallic. The square net is the reason these compounds are studied
discriminate_from.zrcusias_1111: the other oxide-pnictide with fluorite-like oxide layers, but with a transition-metal pnictide slab in place of the bare square net
discriminate_from.hfcusi2_112_square_net: the same square-net motif and the same argument for splitting it out, but in an oxygen-free 112 pnictide
discriminate_from.fluorite_oxide: the RE2O2 block on its own is fluorite-like, which is why a Ho-Bi-O composition can be mistaken for a rare-earth-stabilised bismuth oxide. Here the bismuth is not in the oxide sublattice at all

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 040 for the Bi-Ho-O host, whose compositions are Ho2BiO3 and Ho2Sn0.2Bi0.8O3 and whose paper is a review of the crystal chemistry of the rare-earth pnictide oxides (RE,Ca)mPnnOm with Pn = Sb or Bi.

The reference supports the structure but not the stoichiometry: mp-1067937 is Ho2BiO2 in I4/mmm with 3 ICSD references at hull 0.000, one oxygen short of the compositions as transcribed. Whether the extra oxygen is real or a transcription error is left on the ledger record rather than resolved here.

This entry is split out of bi2o2se_layered for the same reason hfcusi2_112_square_net was split out of zrcusias_1111 in chunk 022: a bonded square net of the heavy pnictogen is a different electronic object from an isolated chalcogenide ion, and merging them would erase the feature the compounds are measured for.
The family is wide, the review covers Sb and Bi members and mixed RE and Ca cations, so more of these are likely further down the tail.

display_name: Bi14Rh3I9 intermetallic-halide layered weak topological insulator
formula_archetype: Bi14M3I9 (M = Rh), built as [(Bi4Rh)3I]2+ [Bi2I8]2-

discriminate_from.bii3_layered_trihalide: the entry a Bi-I-Rh composition would otherwise be forced into. BiI3 is a molecular layer of edge-sharing BiI6 octahedra with bismuth in the 3+ state throughout. Here the halide is confined to [Bi2I8]2- ribbons that act only as an insulating spacer, and the part that carries the transport is a two-dimensional honeycomb intermetallic sheet of Rh-centred Bi cubes in which bismuth is metallic. Filing it as a trihalide would hide exactly the feature it is measured for
discriminate_from.bi_chalcogenide_complex: the other place a complicated bismuth compound tends to land, but that entry is for chalcogenides where every composition is its own structure. This is a single well-defined compound with a known cell
discriminate_from.tetradymite: not a quintuple-layer chalcogenide at all, despite both being called topological insulators -- the topology here is weak rather than strong and comes from stacking the honeycomb sheets, not from a single Bi2Te3 slab

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 041 for the Bi-I-Rh host, whose single composition is transcribed Bi1.4Rh3I9 and is Bi14Rh3I9, the compound the paper on minimum thermal conductivity in weak topological insulators reports.

The structure is an alternation of a cationic [(Bi4Rh)3I]2+ honeycomb slab, in which RhBi8 cubes share edges, with an anionic [Bi2I8]2- spacer layer. That separation of a conducting slab from an insulating spacer is the structural reason the compound has an ultralow, glass-like lattice thermal conductivity.
No Materials Project or TEDesignLab entry is offered for this host, so no mp_id is carried and the C2/m setting comes from the published crystal chemistry rather than from a reference line here.
Related compounds exist in the same intergrowth family (Bi13Pt3I7, the Bi-Rh-Cl-I series), so the entry is written for the family rather than the single compound.

display_name: Layered oxycarbonate, a carbonate layer replacing an apical oxide layer in a perovskite-derived block
formula_archetype: A4M2O6(CO3), equivalently A2MO3(CO3)0.5 (A = Sr, Ba; M = Co, Cu, Mn)
typical_space_group: P4/mmm (123), with I4/mmm (139) and larger orthorhombic supercells where the triangular carbonate groups order

discriminate_from.ruddlesden_popper: the oxide part is the same K2NiF4-derived block of A cations and MO layers, and that is the entry this would otherwise be forced into. The difference is that a planar CO3 group replaces the rocksalt oxide layer between the blocks, so the carbon is a structural anion with its own geometry rather than an impurity or a second phase, and the M polyhedra become square pyramids or chains rather than octahedra
discriminate_from.misfit_cobaltite: the other Sr-Co-O layered candidate, but that one stacks a rocksalt block against a CdI2-type CoO2 sheet with an incommensurate ratio. Here there is no CoO2 sheet and no misfit -- the stacking is commensurate
discriminate_from.composite_multiphase: the reading to avoid. Carbon in a fired oxide is usually milling residue or an added conductive phase, but in these compounds the carbonate is part of the crystal structure and is why the compound exists
discriminate_from.perovskite: the A and M cations sit in a perovskite-like arrangement, but the carbonate layer cuts the octahedral network so the framework is not three-dimensional

structure_database_candidates.source: ref 2, hull 0.634, no icsd -- a carbonyl, not a carbonate, and recorded here only to show that the reference line for this host does not reach the right chemistry

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 041 for the C-Co-O-Sr host, whose single composition is Sr4Co2O6CO3.

The compound is the cobalt member of the oxycarbonate family whose best-known member is the cuprate Sr2CuO2CO3. Both are made by firing a carbonate precursor under conditions where the carbonate is retained in the structure instead of being driven off.

The whole reference line for this host lists cobalt carbonyls at hulls above 0.3 and no ICSD support. A carbonyl is a molecular Co(CO)n unit and a carbonate is a CO3 2- anion; the databases confuse the two because both are written C and O next to a metal. That is recorded rather than followed.
Space group is given as a range because the carbonate orientation orders differently across the family and the exact setting for the cobalt member is not established from the compositions alone.

formula_archetype: A3N4
typical_space_group: P6_3/m (176) for the beta form; P31c (159) for the alpha form built from the same tetrahedral network with a different stacking

discriminate_from.sic_polytype: the other covalent ceramic that appears as a matrix or a reinforcement in the same composites. SiC is a binary adamantine structure with four-coordinate carbon; Si3N4 has three-coordinate nitrogen bridging corner-sharing SiN4 tetrahedra into rings, which is a different network topology
discriminate_from.wurtzite: the tetrahedral network is related but Si3N4 is not a 1:1 compound and its nitrogen sits at the centre of a planar triangle of silicon, so the two cannot share an entry
discriminate_from.composite_multiphase: in this dataset Si3N4 is met as the insulating matrix of a graphene composite, so the host record is a composite while this entry names what the matrix is

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 041 for the C-N-Si host, where the curator records Si3N4 with 17vol percent graphene nanoplatelets and Si3N4 with 4vol percent reduced graphene oxide. The host is recorded as composite_multiphase and this entry is named as the matrix.

beta is the stable form reached by sintering, alpha is the form the starting powder is usually in, and hot pressing converts alpha to beta. Both are the same tetrahedral network with different stacking, so they are kept in one entry with the alpha setting noted.

Si3N4 itself is an insulator and contributes almost nothing to the transport in these samples; it is the graphene network that conducts. The entry exists so the matrix can be named rather than left blank.
No Materials Project or TEDesignLab entry for binary Si3N4 is offered on this host line -- the reference line lists carbodiimides and Si2CN4 instead -- so no mp_id is carried.

prototype: R2MW2O10, built from edge-sharing W2O10 octahedral dimers
formula_archetype: R2MW2O10 with R a rare earth and M a divalent metal (Cd, Mg, Mn, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn)
typical_space_group: monoclinic; the family is reported in both the P2_1/c (14) and C2/c (15) settings and the setting for the cadmium member is not fixed by the composition alone

discriminate_from.tungsten_bronze: the bronzes are non-stoichiometric AxWO3 phases with a corner-sharing WO6 framework and metallic or semimetallic transport from partial W reduction; this entry is a line compound with fully oxidised W6+ in isolated W2O10 dimers
discriminate_from.perovskite: the formula can be read as a defect double perovskite, but the tungsten octahedra here are edge-sharing dimers rather than a corner-sharing three-dimensional network, so the two are not the same framework
discriminate_from.cu2v2o7_pyrovanadate: the other entry built from an edge-sharing or corner-sharing M2O7 dimer unit; that one is a vanadate with tetrahedral V and a different dimer geometry

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 042 for the Cd-O-Pr-W host, whose single composition is CdPr2W2O10 from a paper on three new ceramic tungstates.

Neither TEDesignLab nor Materials Project offers any entry on this host line, so the space group rests on the structural chemistry of the R2MW2O10 family rather than on a reference, and the assignment is recorded at low confidence.

The distinguishing motif is the W2O10 dimer of two edge-sharing WO6 octahedra, with R in high (eight or nine) coordination and the divalent metal octahedral. Confirm the setting and the cadmium coordination against the paper before this entry is folded into a v4 seed.

formula_archetype: A2BO4 with A a large divalent cation and B a tetravalent cation

discriminate_from.spinel: the competing structure for the same A2BO4 formula and the one this project actually meets: spinel is cubic Fd-3m with a close-packed oxygen array, while Sr2PbO4-type is orthorhombic and built from ribbons of edge-sharing BO6 octahedra separated by A cations. Cadmium stannate takes the orthorhombic form as a bulk ceramic and the spinel form as a sputtered transparent conducting film, so the two cannot be merged
discriminate_from.ruddlesden_popper: also an A2BO4 formula, but Ruddlesden-Popper n=1 is the tetragonal K2NiF4 perovskite-rocksalt intergrowth, a layered structure with corner-sharing octahedra
discriminate_from.rocksalt_oxide: the parent close packing that both A2BO4 arrangements derive from, at a 1:1 stoichiometry with no cation ordering

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 042 so the orthorhombic form of Cd2SnO4 can be named in other_polymorphs rather than left unrecorded. The host record itself is assigned to spinel, because both papers on that host are on thin films.

TEDesignLab makes Pbam mp-5966 the PRIMARY entry for Cd2SnO4 with 3 ICSD references, against 1 for the Fd-3m entry mp-1104726, so the reference and the assignment disagree and the disagreement is recorded on the host.
The type is a genuine structure type beyond cadmium stannate -- Ca2SnO4 and Sr2PbO4 itself take it -- so it is proposed as a prototype rather than as a note on the spinel entry.

formula_archetype: MX2 with X a halogen

discriminate_from.cdi2_1t: the same electrically neutral X-M-X sandwich with octahedral metal coordination, differing only in how the sandwiches stack: CdI2 is the hexagonal two-layer stacking in P-3m1, CdCl2 the cubic three-layer stacking in R-3m. They are kept apart because the reference space group is what an assignment is tested against, and 164 against 166 would read as a disagreement every time
discriminate_from.bii3_layered_trihalide: the trihalide relative, where one third of the octahedral sites in each layer are vacant and the metal sublattice is a honeycomb rather than a complete triangular net
discriminate_from.nias: the three-dimensional limit of the same octahedral stacking, with every layer of octahedral sites filled and no van der Waals gap

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 042 for the Cl-Fe host, whose only composition is FeCl2 and whose Materials Project PRIMARY entry is FeCl2 R-3m mp-23229 with 4 ICSD references.

The chlorides of the late 3d metals take the CdCl2 stacking while the corresponding iodides and bromides mostly take CdI2; this is the structural reason the entry is needed rather than a difference in bonding.
Magnetic ordering (FeCl2 orders near 24 K) changes the magnetic cell, not the crystallographic prototype, and the measured 11-47 K window spans that ordering without crossing a structural transition.

formula_archetype: A2BX6 with A a large monovalent cation (K, Rb, Cs) and B a tetravalent metal (Hf, Zr, Sn, Te, Pt, Pd, Re)

discriminate_from.double_perovskite: the ordered A2BB-prime-X6 double perovskite has two different octahedral cations alternating and a fully connected corner-sharing framework. Here every second octahedral site is empty instead, so the BX6 octahedra are isolated and share no corners at all. The formula looks identical and the space group is the same Fm-3m, which is exactly why the two have to be separated by hand
discriminate_from.perovskite: the ABX3 aristotype, whose octahedra are corner-connected in three dimensions. Removing half the B cations breaks that network and is what gives these compounds their very low lattice thermal conductivity
discriminate_from.halide_perovskite_hybrid: also a halide with heavy B cations, but a connected ABX3 framework with a molecular A cation; the transport interest there is photovoltaic rather than the rattling isolated octahedra here
discriminate_from.antifluorite: the A2B arrangement of the cation and octahedron centres is literally antifluorite, which is where the K2PtCl6 description comes from, but the antifluorite entry is for simple A2B compounds with monatomic anions and does not describe a molecular octahedral anion
discriminate_from.fluorite_oxide: same cubic cation array, no discrete octahedral anion

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 043 for the Cs-Hf-I and Cs-I-Zr hosts, whose single compositions are Cs2HfI6 and Cs2ZrI6 from one computational transport paper. The Materials Project entries are Cs2HfI6 Fm-3m mp-29398 at hull zero with 1 ICSD reference and Cs2ZrI6 Fm-3m mp-1206511 at hull zero with no ICSD count.

The taxonomy has no A2BX6 entry at all and both the perovskite and double_perovskite entries would misdescribe the connectivity, which is the whole physical point of this family: isolated BX6 units and loosely bound A cations give glass-like lattice thermal conductivity, and that is why these compounds are computed as thermoelectrics.
Both hosts here are theory-only, so the entry rests on the composition and on the Materials Project settings rather than on a measured sample.

formula_archetype: R6T2X with R a rare earth, T a late 3d metal (Co, Ni, Fe) and X a p-block element (Ga, Sn, In, Sb)

discriminate_from.th7fe3: the other rare-earth-rich R-T binary framework in the taxonomy, at R7T3 and hexagonal P6_3mc, with no third element. The Ho6Co2Ga type is the ternary ordered relative, where the p-block atom takes its own site rather than substituting into the transition-metal sublattice
discriminate_from.ho4co3_type: R4T3, the neighbouring rare-earth-rich binary, which has no third element and a different rare-earth-to-cobalt ratio
discriminate_from.mn5si3_d88: the other cation-rich stuffed intermetallic, hexagonal and binary-derived
discriminate_from.laves_phase: the RT2 default for a rare-earth transition-metal system, ruled out by the 6:2 ratio and by the third element
discriminate_from.zrnial_fe2p: the other ordered ternary intermetallic with trigonal-prismatic metalloid coordination, but at 1:1:1 and hexagonal

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 043 for the Co-Nd-Sn host. Materials Project returns Nd6Co2Sn Immm mp-1210166 at hull 0.028 with no ICSD count, which agrees with the Ho6Co2Ga setting and is the only entry in the reference that matches the composition as written.

The taxonomy carries nothing between R7T3 and RT2 for a ternary with a p-block third element, which is a real gap: the R6T2X compounds are a large family and several of them are measured for magnetic and transport work.
The setting is taken from the Materials Project entry and from the structure type, not from a measured pattern in the paper.

formula_archetype: R12T6X with R a rare earth, T = Co or Ni and X a p-block element (In, Sn, Ga)
typical_space_group: not verified here; reported as a tetragonal structure type of its own in the R12T6X series

discriminate_from.ho6co2ga_type: the other rare-earth-rich ternary in the same Nd-Co-Sn system and the one that shares this host. R6T2X has three rare earths per transition metal, R12T6X has two, and the paper reports them as separate line compounds, so the two cannot be merged into one entry
discriminate_from.r12co5bi_type: the closest relative in the proposed set, at R12T5X rather than R12T6X. One transition metal per formula apart, and the proposal for that entry also left the setting unverified. A reviewer should decide whether the two are one family
discriminate_from.th7fe3: the binary rare-earth-rich framework with no third element
discriminate_from.laves_phase: the RT2 default, ruled out by the 12:6:1 ratio

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 043 for the Co-Nd-Sn host, whose second composition is Nd12Co6Sn. Neither reference returns anything at this composition, so nothing here is corroborated by a database entry.

The space group is deliberately left unstated rather than guessed. What is certain from the composition is that Nd12Co6Sn is not the same phase as Nd6Co2Sn, which is why the host is recorded as mixed instead of being forced onto one prototype.
Confidence in the entry is low and it should be checked against the source paper before it is folded into a v4 seed file.

formula_archetype: M2A2BO6+d, read as an intergrowth of an [M2O2+d] rocksalt-type bilayer with an [A2BO4] single perovskite block
typical_space_group: not verified here; the cuprate 2201 archetype is I4/mmm (139), with orthorhombic and incommensurately modulated variants common

discriminate_from.bscco_cuprate: the same 2201 intergrowth topology, but that entry is written for the superconducting bismuth cuprates and carries their homologous 2212 and 2223 members and their CuO2-plane physics. A cobaltite with a gallium-bearing bilayer is the same structural idea in a different chemistry and should not be filed as a cuprate
discriminate_from.ruddlesden_popper: the closest non-cuprate relative. RP stacks single rocksalt AO layers between perovskite blocks; 2201 inserts a full M2O2 bilayer instead, which is an extra rocksalt layer and a different cation count
discriminate_from.misfit_cobaltite: the other layered strontium cobaltite family and the one the neighbouring Co-O-Pb-Sr host in this chunk takes. Misfits are incommensurate composites with an irrational CoO2 count per formula; here the CoO2 count is exactly one, so the compound is commensurate and has a single periodic cell
discriminate_from.aurivillius: also a bismuth-bearing layered oxide with a fluorite-like bilayer, but the bilayer there is [Bi2O2] alternating with multi-octahedron perovskite slabs of variable thickness
discriminate_from.perovskite: the aristotype; this is a two-dimensional intergrowth with a single octahedral layer, not a three-dimensional framework

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 043 for the Co-Ga-O-Sr host, whose only composition is (Ga0.33Co0.67)2Sr2CoO6 from a paper announcing it as a new layered cobaltite.

The reading rests on the formula splitting exactly: [(Ga,Co)2O2+d] plus [Sr2CoO4] gives M2Sr2CoO6+d with nothing left over, which is the 2201 cation and anion count. Bi2Sr2CoO6 is the known cobaltite member of the same series, so a cobaltite 2201 is not a new idea, only a new bilayer chemistry.

Neither reference returns anything for this host, so nothing is corroborated by a database entry and no space group is claimed. A reviewer should check whether gallium in the bilayer is tetrahedral, which would make this closer to the Ga-1212 cuprate architecture than to a rocksalt bilayer and would mean the entry needs rewriting or splitting.

display_name: A2BaCu8Te10 copper polytelluride cage compound (A = K, Rb)
formula_archetype: A2BaCu8Te10 (A = K, Rb)
typical_space_group: not verified here; the compound is reported as a copper telluride framework enclosing the alkali and barium cations, and no setting is claimed from composition alone

discriminate_from.ba3cu14te12_polytelluride: the other barium copper polytelluride already in the taxonomy. Both are built from a copper telluride framework carrying Te-Te bonds, but that one has no alkali metal and a different Cu:Te ratio. Here two alkali cations per formula sit in the framework cavities alongside the barium, and it is that pair that sets the electron count and the Te-Te bond order
discriminate_from.cu2se_superionic: a simple binary whose cation sublattice is mobile inside a rigid anion array. This is the opposite arrangement: the copper is part of the rigid framework and the guest cations are the large alkali and alkaline earth ions
discriminate_from.chevrel: also cations in the channels of a rigid chalcogenide framework, but there the framework is built from discrete Mo6 octahedral clusters rather than a continuous copper telluride network
discriminate_from.clathrate_i: the archetypal cage compound, whose host is a four-connected tetrahedral main-group network with guests inside closed polyhedra. The cages here are cavities in a copper telluride framework, and the tellurium is polymeric rather than a closed shell
discriminate_from.tl5te3: the other heavy-cation telluride with cations in a telluride framework, but it is a filled variant of a binary telluride with no transition metal

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 044 for two hosts from the same paper on the thermoelectric properties and electronic structure of the cage compound K2BaCu8Te10: Cu-K-Te (K2BaCu8Te10 and K2.1Ba0.9Cu8Te10) and Cu-Rb-Te (Rb2BaCu8Te10).

Neither reference contains the measured phase. TEDesignLab returns K4Cu8Te11, KCuTe and KCu3Te2 for the potassium host and Materials Project returns K2(CuTe)5 and K2Cu2Te5, all single-ICSD entries and none of them A2BaCu8Te10, so nothing here rests on a database match.
The barium falls below the 5 at.% dopant threshold only because the formula has 21 atoms; it is a required structural cation, not a dopant, and the records for both hosts say so.
No space group and no mp_id is claimed. Stage 2 must take the structure from the paper.

formula_archetype: (Pb,Cu)Sr2(Ca,R)Cu2O7 (R = Y, Yb and other small rare earths)
typical_space_group: P4/mmm (123), taken from the 1212 family rather than from a database entry

discriminate_from.hg_tl_1212_cuprate: the same single-reservoir 1212 stacking of two CuO2 planes about a bare cation layer, but that entry is written for A = Hg and Tl, where the reservoir is one A-O sheet whose oxygen excess d is the doping variable. In the lead member the reservoir is a mixed (Pb,Cu)O block in which copper is a required constituent, so the doping knob is a cation ratio and a rare-earth-for-calcium substitution rather than an interstitial oxygen count
discriminate_from.ruthenocuprate: also a 1212 with a transition metal in the reservoir, but the RuO2 layer is a full corner-sharing octahedral sheet giving O8 rather than O7, and the entry exists for the ferromagnetic superconductor physics that ruthenium brings
discriminate_from.ybco_cuprate: the reservoir is a one-dimensional CuO chain and the alkaline earth is barium; here the reservoir is a two-dimensional lead-bearing sheet on strontium, and there is no chain ordering and so no orthorhombic twinning
discriminate_from.bscco_cuprate: a double rocksalt reservoir bilayer and an incommensurate modulation, neither of which this has

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 044 for Cu-O-Pb-Sr, whose two compositions are (Pb0.75Cu0.25)Sr2(Ca0.5Y0.5)Cu2O7 and the ytterbium analogue, from a paper on superconductivity in Pb-based 1212 cuprates.

Materials Project returns only triclinic P-1 and monoclinic C2/m Sr-Ca-R-Cu-Pb-O entries around hull 0.02 with no ICSD backing, which are computed orderings rather than the measured tetragonal phase. The space group here therefore comes from the 1212 family, not from the reference, and that disagreement is recorded on the assignment.

The taxonomy already splits the 1212 architecture by the reservoir cation -- hg_tl_1212_cuprate for Hg and Tl, ruthenocuprate for Ru -- and its own note says the split is by the A cation and nothing else changes. This entry follows that convention rather than widening the mercury entry.

formula_archetype: (Nb,M)Sr2RCu2O8 (M = Ti, Cu; R = rare earth)
typical_space_group: P4/mmm (123) expected for the 1212 stacking; the one Materials Project entry for this chemistry is body-centred I4/mcm (140) instead

discriminate_from.ruthenocuprate: isostructural in the strict sense: the same 1212-O8 framework with an octahedral MO2 reservoir layer between the two CuO2 planes. That entry is written around RuSr2GdCu2O8 and exists for its ferromagnetic-superconductor physics, which a diamagnetic Nb(V) reservoir does not have; the niobium member is also stabilised by titanium or copper co-substitution on the reservoir site rather than by oxygen stoichiometry. Kept separate by the reservoir cation, exactly as Hg and Tl are kept separate from Ru. A reviewer who prefers one general M-1212 entry can merge the two and nothing else changes
discriminate_from.hg_tl_1212_cuprate: the single-reservoir family, where the reservoir is one A-O sheet and the compound is an O7 1212 on barium. An octahedral reservoir layer adds the eighth oxygen and removes the interstitial-oxygen doping knob
discriminate_from.pb_1212_cuprate: the lead member, also on strontium, but its reservoir is a mixed (Pb,Cu)O sheet at O7 rather than a corner-sharing octahedral MO2 layer at O8
discriminate_from.ybco_cuprate: a CuO chain reservoir on barium with A-site ordering of yttrium; the 1212 rare earth here plays the same spacer role but the reservoir chemistry is entirely different

structure_database_candidates.note: hull 0.022 with 1 ICSD reference. The body-centred I4/mcm setting is not what the primitive 1212 stacking gives, so it is recorded rather than adopted.

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 044 for Cu-Eu-Nb-O-Sr, whose compositions are (Nb0.9Ti0.1)Sr2EuCu2O8 and (Nb0.75Cu0.25)Sr2EuCu2O8, from a paper on structure and superconductivity in new Nb-based cuprates.

The formula settles the architecture: Sr2RCu2O8 with a single further cation is the 1212 count, and the O8 stoichiometry requires the reservoir cation to be octahedrally coordinated, which is what Nb(V) takes.
The one reference entry disagrees on the space group and rests on a single ICSD reference, so no setting is asserted as confirmed.

formula_archetype: RF3 (R = La to Nd and other large rare earths)

discriminate_from.fluorite_oxide: the CaF2 type, which is where the small heavy rare-earth trifluorides and the mixed alkali rare-earth fluorides end up. Tysonite is not a fluorite defect variant: the rare earth is eleven-coordinate and the fluorine sits on three inequivalent sites, two of which carry the ionic conduction, so the two types differ in coordination and in transport mechanism rather than only in vacancy count
discriminate_from.nayf4_gagarinite: the mixed sodium rare-earth fluoride, where an alkali shares the cation sublattice and the stable form is hexagonal but of a different type
discriminate_from.bii3_layered_trihalide: the other trihalide entry, which is a layered van der Waals iodide with discrete slabs. The trifluoride is a dense three-dimensional ionic framework with no van der Waals gap
discriminate_from.k2ptcl6_a2bx6: an ordered halide with isolated octahedral anions, not a continuous framework

structure_database_candidates.note: hull 0.000 with 21 ICSD references, the best-attested entry for this chemistry and in agreement with the assignment.

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 044 for F-La (LaF3 and Eu-doped LaF3) from a paper on the thermal conductivity of rare earth fluoride crystals.

The taxonomy had no entry for a dense fluoride framework of any kind, which is why this is a new prototype rather than a reuse. The compound is a fluoride ion conductor measured for its thermal conductivity rather than a thermoelectric, so the entry is here for completeness of the classification.

structural_class is written as framework halide, which is NOT one of the structural classes declared in prototypes_seed_v3.json -- the list carries framework oxide and no halide class. Folding this entry into v4 needs that class added, or the entry retyped; check_annotations validates structural_class against the declared list and would otherwise fail. The same applies to nayf4_gagarinite, proposed from the same chunk.

display_name: NaYF4 (hexagonal beta gagarinite-type / cubic alpha fluorite-derived)
formula_archetype: NaRF4 (R = Y and the rare earths)
typical_space_group: P-6 (174) or P6_3/m (176) for the hexagonal beta form; Fm-3m (225) cation-disordered for the cubic alpha form

discriminate_from.fluorite_oxide: the cubic alpha form IS a cation-disordered fluorite, so that entry describes half of this one. It is scoped to MO2 oxides and carries neither the alkali sharing the cation site nor the hexagonal beta form, which is the thermodynamically stable polymorph and the one most polycrystalline preparations contain
discriminate_from.tysonite_laf3: the binary rare-earth trifluoride framework with no alkali. Adding sodium at a 1:1 cation ratio changes both the site chemistry and which polymorphs are reachable
discriminate_from.k2ptcl6_a2bx6: an ordered A2BX6 halide built from isolated BX6 octahedra; here the fluorine is shared between cations in a continuous framework
discriminate_from.halide_perovskite_hybrid: an ABX3 corner-sharing halide framework, a different anion count and a different connectivity

structure_database_candidates.note: hull 0.000 but flagged AMBIGUOUS and with no ICSD count shown. I4_1/amd is a scheelite-like setting and matches neither the reported alpha nor the reported beta form, so it is recorded as a disagreement rather than adopted.

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 044 for F-Na-Y, whose single composition is NaYF4, from a 1983 paper on thermoelectric power studies of polycrystalline NaYF4 samples.

Which polymorph the samples hold cannot be decided from the formula: alpha and beta differ in symmetry and cation order but not at all in composition. The entry therefore names both and stage 2 must take the answer from the paper. The measured window, 313 to 399 K, is far below the alpha-beta transformation range, so the sample keeps whatever form the synthesis produced.
structural_class is framework halide, which is not declared in prototypes_seed_v3.json; see the note on tysonite_laf3, proposed from the same chunk.

formula_archetype: A2BT2O7, which in the gallate line is written ABGa3O7 with A a large divalent cation and B a rare earth sharing the same eight-coordinate site

discriminate_from.langasite: the other trigonal-or-tetragonal rare-earth gallate framework grown as a piezoelectric single crystal, La3Ga5SiO14 in P321. Langasite has five gallium per formula across three distinct polyhedra including an octahedral site; melilite has three gallium, all tetrahedral, in a single sheet. Both are wide-gap gallates with a rare earth, so formula alone will confuse them
discriminate_from.fresnoite: the closest structural relative already in the taxonomy: also a layered oxide built from a tetrahedral sheet with large cations between the sheets. Fresnoite Ba2TiSi2O8 carries a square-pyramidal TiO5 group in the sheet, which melilite does not have; melilite sheets are tetrahedra only
discriminate_from.perovskite: SrGdGaO4-type and the Sr-Gd-Ga-O perovskites are the other phases of this chemistry, built from corner-sharing GaO6 octahedra. Melilite has no octahedral gallium at all, which is why its conductivity is ionic-or-insulating rather than metallic
discriminate_from.garnet: the other cubic rare-earth gallate, Gd3Ga5O12, at a different cation ratio and fully three-dimensional
discriminate_from.zircon_zrsio4: also a tetragonal oxide with isolated tetrahedral anion groups, but one tetrahedral cation per formula and no sheet

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 045 for the Ga-Gd-O-Sr host, whose single composition is Nd-doped SrGdGa3O7 grown as a single crystal. The melilite group is absent from prototypes_seed_v3.json even though the taxonomy already carries three of its neighbours among the piezoelectric and laser-host oxides (fresnoite, langasite, langatate), so the gap is a hole in an area the taxonomy otherwise covers.

The A site takes Sr and Gd together in a disordered eight-coordinate position, so the formula is better read as (Sr,Gd)2Ga2(GaO4)... the sheet is built from GaO4 tetrahedra sharing corners into five-membered rings, with the fifth gallium bridging. A refinement is what settles the Ga distribution; the prototype does not.

Melilites are a known ultralow-thermal-conductivity family for the same reason the langasites are: a soft tetrahedral sheet with heavy cations loosely held between the layers. That is the thermoelectric interest, not the transport, which is insulating.

[ref 2] offers only Sr2GdGaO5 Fmmm (69) for this host, which is a different compound at a different Ga content, not a polymorph of SrGdGa3O7. No melilite entry appears in either reference for this chemistry.

formula_archetype: ABO4 with A an eight-coordinate large cation and B a tetrahedral cation (Si, P, V, As, Cr)

discriminate_from.scheelite_awo4: the other tetragonal ABO4 with isolated tetrahedra, and the one the taxonomy already has. Zircon I4_1/amd and scheelite I4_1/a differ in how the AO8 polyhedra and BO4 tetrahedra link, and the choice is set by the size of A: small trivalent rare earths and Zr give zircon, large divalent Ca-Sr-Ba-Pb give scheelite. Zircon also converts to a scheelite-type form under pressure, so the two are genuinely one phase field seen at different A radii
discriminate_from.fergusonite_retao4: the monoclinic scheelite derivative taken by the rare-earth niobates and tantalates. Same REBO4 formula and the same rare earths, so only the B cation and the symmetry separate them: REVO4 and REPO4 are zircon, RENbO4 and RETaO4 are fergusonite
discriminate_from.rutile: also a tetragonal oxide framework but built from edge-sharing octahedral chains with no isolated tetrahedral group
discriminate_from.x2_re2sio5_monosilicate: the other rare-earth orthosilicate family with isolated SiO4 groups, at a different RE to Si ratio and monoclinic
discriminate_from.pyrochlore: RE2B2O7 with both cations octahedral, the phase these chemistries take at the 2:2:7 ratio. [ref 2] lists Gd2V2O7 Fd-3m for the same host, which is that compound and not a polymorph of GdVO4

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 045 for the Gd-O-V host, whose composition is Nd-doped Lu-Gd vanadate laser crystal. Zircon is one of the most heavily studied ABO4 structure types and was missing from prototypes_seed_v3.json, which carries only the scheelite side of the family (itself a chunk proposal, not a seed entry).
The mp_id is copied from the [ref 2] line of the chunk file, which asserts I4_1/amd (141) for GdVO4 with seven ICSD references. That is the zircon setting, so reference and prototype agree here.

Nd:GdVO4 and Nd:YVO4 are laser hosts rather than thermoelectrics, and the thermoelectric interest in this host is thin: two samples, one paper, a Seebeck-and-conductivity characterisation of a laser crystal. The entry is still worth having because the zircon-type phosphates and vanadates recur as low-conductivity oxides.
Zircon transforms to a scheelite-type polymorph near 6 GPa. That is a pressure transition, not a thermal one, so it belongs in other_polymorphs rather than in a thermal phase sequence.

prototype: YNbO4 fergusonite, the monoclinic scheelite derivative
formula_archetype: REMO4 with RE a rare earth or Y and M = Nb or Ta
typical_space_group: P2/c (13), also set as I2/a or C2/c depending on cell choice; the parent tetragonal scheelite form I4_1/a (88) appears above the ferroelastic transition

discriminate_from.scheelite_awo4: the tetragonal aristotype, and what fergusonite becomes on heating through its ferroelastic transition. The distortion is small in atom positions but it halves the symmetry and makes the material twinned and strongly anelastic, which is exactly the mechanism credited for the low thermal conductivity, so collapsing the two would erase the physics of interest
discriminate_from.zircon_zrsio4: the other tetragonal REBO4 with isolated tetrahedra, taken by REVO4 and REPO4. The niobates and tantalates are too large for the zircon field and distort to fergusonite instead
discriminate_from.perovskite: the other phase of this chemistry and the reason the Gd-O-Ta host is mixed rather than single: RETa3O9 is an A-site-deficient perovskite of corner-sharing TaO6 octahedra, at a completely different Ta content from RETaO4
discriminate_from.ln2mw2o10_double_tungstate: the other rare-earth plus d0-cation oxide framework with isolated tetrahedral anions, at a 2:1:2 cation ratio
discriminate_from.pyrochlore: RE2B2O7, the 2:2:7 phase with octahedral B; fergusonite has no octahedral network

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 045 for the Gd-O-Ta host. The rare-earth tantalates and niobates are an active ultralow-thermal-conductivity family for thermal-barrier coatings and the taxonomy had no entry for them; the nearest thing was the scheelite proposal from an earlier chunk, whose formula_archetype is explicitly limited to A = Ca, Sr, Ba, Pb with M = W or Mo.

The monoclinic-to-tetragonal ferroelastic transition in RETaO4 sits well above the measured window for this host (373 to 1073 K) at roughly 1400 to 1700 K depending on the rare earth, so the samples stay monoclinic throughout and no phase array entry is needed for it. Those temperatures are from general knowledge of the family, not from the papers.

YTaO4 additionally has an M-prime form in P2/a that differs in the tantalum coordination. Which form a sample holds depends on synthesis, so stage 2 should take it from the paper rather than from the composition.

prototype: PbCl2 cotunnite, and the CaH2 saline-dihydride line within it
formula_archetype: AX2 with a nine-coordinate A cation

discriminate_from.interstitial_hydride: the entry this would otherwise be forced into, and a different kind of material. interstitial_hydride is the metallic MHx line typified by PdH0.66, cubic and with hydrogen occupying interstices of a metal lattice over a continuous composition range. The saline dihydrides are line compounds in which hydrogen is an ordered anion on its own sublattice, they are semiconducting rather than metallic, and they are orthorhombic. YbH2 is the second kind
discriminate_from.fluorite_oxide: the eight-coordinate cubic AX2, which is where these compounds go at higher X content or higher temperature. Yb also forms a cubic hydride toward YbH2.5, and [ref 2] lists a cubic YbH2 entry, so the two settings sit side by side in the same chemistry and have to be kept apart
discriminate_from.antifluorite: the inverse arrangement at A2B, with the cation in the fourfold site; the coordination roles are swapped
discriminate_from.pbfcl_matlockite: the layered ternary ordering of the same cotunnite parent, in which the two anion species separate onto distinct layers and the symmetry rises to P4/nmm. Cotunnite is the single-anion parent
discriminate_from.tysonite_laf3: the AX3 rare-earth halide with nine-and-eleven-fold coordination, the next composition along in the same size regime

structure_database_candidates.source: ref 2, hull 0.000, icsd 2, not marked primary

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 045 for the H-Yb host, whose compositions are YbH1.85 and YbH1.88. Neither the seed nor the earlier proposals cover a saline dihydride; interstitial_hydride is the only hydride entry and it describes metallic interstitial solutions, which these are not.

The reference and the prototype disagree here and the disagreement is recorded on the assignment: [ref 2] marks YbH2 Fm-3m (225) mp-634751 as PRIMARY on three ICSD references at hull 0.059, while the Pnma entry mp-864603 sits at hull 0.000 with two references and is not marked primary. Hydrogen positions are poorly determined by X-ray diffraction and the cubic cell is what a metal-only refinement returns, which is the likely origin of the count. The orthorhombic CaH2-type form is the accepted ambient structure of YbH2 and is also the lower-energy one in the same dump.

The sub-stoichiometry, H at 1.85 to 1.88 rather than 2, is the carrier-concentration knob for this material rather than an impurity, so the role is non_stoichiometry. It does not change the prototype.
Cotunnite is also the high-pressure form of many AX2 compounds, ZrO2 and the alkaline-earth fluorides among them, so the entry will be wanted again beyond the hydrides.

formula_archetype: AM2Pn2 with A a divalent cation, M a group 13 metal and Pn a pnictogen

discriminate_from.caal2si2_zintl: the other AM2Pn2 Zintl arrangement and the one this has to be kept apart from. CaAl2Si2 is trigonal P-3m1 (164) with one [M2Pn2] slab per cell and no metal-metal bonding between slabs; this type is hexagonal P6_3/mmc (194) and stacks two slabs per cell. Same formula, different structure, and the space group is what tells them apart
discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: the tetragonal I4/mmm AM2X2 arrangement, the third member of the 1-2-2 family and the one with a square M net rather than a honeycomb one
discriminate_from.cain2_ligage_hexagonal: also hexagonal and also built on group 13 honeycomb nets, but at AM2 with no pnictogen sublattice at all
discriminate_from.zrcusias_1111: the layered quaternary at ABCD; this is a ternary with no oxide or fluoride layer between the slabs

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 046 for the In-P-Sr host, whose two samples are both SrIn2P2. The seed taxonomy covers AM2Pn2 Zintl phases only through caal2si2_zintl, which is trigonal P-3m1, while [ref 1] gives Sr(InP)2 at P6_3/mmc (194), ICSD-backed and on the hull. Filing it under caal2si2_zintl would assert the wrong space group and the wrong interslab connectivity.

The space group is taken from [ref 1]. The structural description, a doubled stacking in which the indium layers are joined through the slab, is from general knowledge of the EuIn2P2 and EuIn2As2 magnetic semiconductors and has not been read out of any paper here, so it should be checked in stage 2.
The arsenide members EuIn2As2 and SrIn2As2 are axion-insulator and topological-semimetal candidates and are measured for transport, so this entry is likely to be wanted again.

formula_archetype: AV3Sb5 with A an alkali metal (K, Rb, Cs)
typical_space_group: P6/mmm (191) for the undistorted cell; a 2x2 in-plane charge-density-wave superstructure forms below roughly 78 to 104 K depending on A

discriminate_from.kagome_staircase_m3v2o8: the only other kagome entry in the taxonomy and a completely different material: an insulating orthorhombic vanadate whose kagome net is buckled into a staircase. This is a metallic antimonide with a flat, undistorted vanadium kagome net
discriminate_from.cacu5: the closest structural relative. CaCu5 is also P6/mmm and also contains a kagome net of the minority atoms; AV3Sb5 is what that motif becomes when an antimony honeycomb is interleaved and the alkali metal takes the large site
discriminate_from.alb2: also a hexagonal P6/mmm layered intermetallic with a large cation between honeycomb sheets, but with one honeycomb net per cell and no kagome sublattice
discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: the other alkali-spaced layered pnictide family measured for superconductivity, but tetragonal I4/mmm with square nets

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 046 for the K-Sb-V host, whose two samples are KV3Sb5 from the paper that reported the family. Neither reference covers the host and the taxonomy had no entry for a kagome metal of any kind.

The vanadium kagome net is the reason these compounds are studied: it puts Dirac points, a flat band and a van Hove singularity near the Fermi level, and the compounds superconduct at about 1 K on top of a charge-density-wave state.

That charge-density-wave order is a genuine structural transition inside the 12 to 294 K window measured here and is recorded on the assignment. It was reported after the discovery paper this host comes from, so the transition temperature is general knowledge rather than paper evidence.

formula_archetype: elemental metal A, and substitutional alloys between two such metals
typical_space_group: P6_3/mmc (194), four atoms per cell in an ABAC stacking sequence

discriminate_from.solid_solution_alloy: the generic entry a rare-earth alloy would otherwise fall into. That entry records only that two species share one lattice; it does not say which lattice. The light rare earths are dhcp rather than hcp or fcc, and the fourfold ABAC stacking is the whole content of this entry
discriminate_from.ni3sn_d019: the ordered-hcp AB3 superstructure, also P6_3/mmc. That is two elements ordering on a two-layer stack; this is one element on a four-layer stack with no chemical ordering at all
discriminate_from.cu3au_l12: the ordered-fcc AB3 superstructure, the cubic counterpart
discriminate_from.a7_rhombohedral: the other low-symmetry elemental entry, the semimetallic A7 arrangement of As, Sb and Bi. dhcp is a true close packing and fully metallic

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 046 for the La-Nd host, whose compositions are Nd0.75La0.25 and Nd0.63La0.37, from a paper on the thermoelectric power of Nd1-xLax and Ce1-xLax alloys. Lanthanum and neodymium are both dhcp at ambient conditions and are completely miscible, so the alloy keeps the structure of both end members.

[ref 2] offers only computed La-Nd orderings, La3Nd in I4/mmm and three LaNd3 settings, none with an ICSD reference and all above the hull. Those are ordering trials on what is a random solid solution and are not evidence about this material; the disagreement is recorded on the assignment.
La, Pr and Nd share this structure and all three are measured for low-temperature transport, so the entry should be reusable. Ce is the exception in that block and is fcc at room temperature.

formula_archetype: elemental A, and the chi-phase intermetallics built on the same cell
typical_space_group: I-43m (217), 58 atoms in the cubic cell on four inequivalent sites

discriminate_from.beta_al3mg2_samson: the other giant-unit-cell entry and the one this is easiest to confuse with. The Samson phase has over a thousand atoms per cell with intrinsic partial occupancy; A12 has exactly 58 atoms on fully occupied sites. The Mg17Al12 gamma phase of that same host is an A12 structure, which is why the line between them is worth drawing
discriminate_from.quasicrystal_approximant: a periodic stand-in for an aperiodic structure. A12 is an ordinary crystal that simply has a large cell
discriminate_from.a15_cr3si: the other complex cubic intermetallic entry, at AB3 with beta-tungsten chains rather than a 58-atom elemental cell
discriminate_from.solid_solution_alloy: manganese dissolved in a disordered alloy on a simple lattice; this is the element in its own ambient structure

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 046 for the Mn host, whose two samples are elemental manganese from a paper titled Origin of low thermal conductivity in alpha-Mn. The taxonomy carries several elemental structures but none for A12, and alpha-Mn is the ambient form of the element up to about 1000 K.

The 58-atom cell with four inequivalent manganese sites is exactly why the element is measured in a thermoelectric context: it gives a very low lattice thermal conductivity for a pure metal, which is what the paper is about.
[ref 2] also lists BaMn28, CaMn28 and YbMn28 in the same space group. Those are interstitially stuffed A12 cells at a different composition, not the element.

formula_archetype: M5X3 (M = Mo, W, Nb, Ta, V; X = Si, Ge)
typical_space_group: I4/mcm (140), 32 atoms in the body-centred tetragonal cell

discriminate_from.cr5b3_type: the entry that already claims I4/mcm at M5X3 and the one this is easiest to lose. Cr5B3 and W5Si3 are two distinct structure types that share the space group and the tI32 Pearson symbol but differ in their atomic positions: Cr5B3 carries isolated boron atoms plus boron pairs, W5Si3 has no X-X pairs at all. Mo5SiB2 is the Cr5B3 branch of this chemistry and Mo5Si3 is the W5Si3 branch, so the Mo-Si-B and Mo-Si hosts must not collapse onto one id
discriminate_from.mn5si3_d88: the other common 5:3 silicide and the reason a bare A5B3 formula does not settle the structure. D8_8 is hexagonal P6_3/mcm with chains of face-sharing metal octahedra and an interstitial site; D8_m is tetragonal and has no such site. Both types occur in the same binaries
discriminate_from.a15_cr3si: the neighbouring phase in the Mo-Si binary, cubic Pm-3n at Mo3Si. The two coexist in as-cast alloys and are easy to conflate
discriminate_from.mosi2_c11b: the disilicide end of the same binary, body-centred tetragonal at MoSi2. Different stoichiometry and a layered rather than framework metal arrangement
discriminate_from.crsi2_c40: the hexagonal disilicide branch, reached in Cr and W silicides rather than at 5:3

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 047 for the Mo-Si host, two single-crystal samples from a paper on the electrical and thermal properties of single-crystalline Mo5X3. Mo5Si3 is the W5Si3 (D8_m) type and the taxonomy had no entry for it: the tetragonal 5:3 silicides were previously reachable only through cr5b3_type, which is a different structure type, or mn5si3_d88, which is hexagonal.
Mo5Si3 is a refractory structural intermetallic measured here for its transport anisotropy, and the D8_m cell is strongly anisotropic, which is why single crystals were grown.

The related ternary Mo5SiB2 T2 phase already has an entry at cr5b3_type from chunk 039. Reviewers should read the two together and confirm the type split rather than merging them on the shared space group.

formula_archetype: A(x)M2(PO4)3 (A = Na, Li, Ca, Sr, Ba, vacancy; M = Zr, Ti, Nb, Hf)
typical_space_group: R-3c (167); the alkaline-earth and low-alkali members distort to C2/c or P-3c1

discriminate_from.fluorite_oxide: the yttria-stabilised zirconia matrix that NZP is added to in this host, and the phase that actually carries most of the material. Fluorite has one eight-coordinate cation site and a simple anion sublattice; NZP is a rigid corner-linked framework of ZrO6 octahedra and PO4 tetrahedra with open channels, and its near-zero thermal expansion is the reason it is added at all
discriminate_from.zrw2o8_type: the other low-and-negative-thermal-expansion framework already in the taxonomy. ZrW2O8 is cubic, built from WO4 tetrahedra with one terminal oxygen and no guest channel; NZP is rhombohedral with an occupiable A site running through it
discriminate_from.sc2w3o12_type: the A2M3O12 negative-expansion family, a different framework topology and no alkali channel
discriminate_from.zircon_zrsio4: also a zirconium orthotetrahedral oxide, but with isolated tetrahedra and eight-coordinate zirconium in a tetragonal cell rather than an octahedral-tetrahedral channel framework
discriminate_from.garnet: the other dense cubic framework silicate or phosphate; garnet has no open channel and no mobile A site

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 047 for the O-P-Zr host, whose two samples are plasma-sprayed coatings of yttria-stabilised zirconia with 4 and 5 mol percent Ca0.5Sr0.5Zr4P6O24 added. NZP is the standard abbreviation for the NaZr2P3O12 family and is what the paper calls the additive.
Phosphorus enters this host only through the NZP phase, so without this entry the host would have to be labelled by its zirconia matrix alone and the phosphorus would go unexplained.

The A site is what makes the family: it is fully occupied by one monovalent cation in NaZr2P3O12, half occupied by a divalent cation in CaZr4P6O24, and can be empty, which is why the formula is written with a variable A content.
Neither reference covers the host, so no mp_id is recorded. Materials Project does carry NZP-type zirconium phosphates and stage 2 should resolve one.

formula_archetype: MO2 with a stereochemically active lone pair
typical_space_group: P4_12_12 (92) and its enantiomorph P4_32_12; Pbca (61) for beta-TeO2, the tellurite form

discriminate_from.rutile: the parent the cell is derived from, and the entry paratellurite would otherwise be forced into. In rutile the metal is six-coordinate in a straight octahedron; in paratellurite the tellurium lone pair drops the coordination to four in a trigonal bipyramid, the TeO4 units share corners rather than edges, and the cell becomes enantiomorphic tetragonal. The chirality is the basis of the acousto-optic applications and is not a detail
discriminate_from.anatase: the other TiO2 polymorph entry, tetragonal I4_1/amd with edge-sharing octahedral chains; unrelated connectivity
discriminate_from.bismite_alpha_bi2o3: the other heavy post-transition lone-pair oxide in the taxonomy, monoclinic and at M2O3 rather than MO2
discriminate_from.v2o5_layered: also a lone-pair-free layered oxide of a high-valent cation, but genuinely layered; paratellurite is a three-dimensional corner-sharing network

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 047 for the O-Te host: two TeO2 samples, one from a paper on the temperature dependence of the thermal conductivity of tellurium dioxide and one from a paper on a NaNbO3 composite. The taxonomy had no tellurium oxide entry at all.

beta-TeO2 (tellurite, Pbca) is the mineral form and is kept in the same entry because it is the same TeO4 trigonal-bipyramidal building unit with a different linkage; it is metastable with respect to paratellurite and is not reached by heating alpha-TeO2, so it belongs in other_polymorphs rather than in a thermal sequence.
TeO2 also appears in this dataset as a surface oxide on tellurium and as an additive, so this entry gives those a name without relabelling their hosts.

formula_archetype: MP2 (M = Ni, Pd, Pt)

discriminate_from.pyrite: the cubic Pa-3 polymorph of the very same compound, and the reason this entry exists. Both forms are built from M and P-P pairs in octahedral coordination, but the monoclinic form is the ambient-pressure phase with a different pair orientation and layer stacking, and the paper behind this host is explicitly about how divergent the two polymorphs of NiP2 are. Filing both under pyrite would erase the distinction the measurement was made to show
discriminate_from.marcasite: the orthorhombic Pnnm relative of pyrite, reached in FeSb2 and NiSb2. NiP2 monoclinic is not a marcasite: the cell is C-centred monoclinic and the coordination differs
discriminate_from.beta_wp2_type: the other low-symmetry diphosphide entry, orthorhombic and noncentrosymmetric with P-P chains rather than isolated pairs
discriminate_from.nisi3p4_type: a ternary nickel silicophosphide in the same chemistry family, not a binary MP2

structure_database_candidates.source: ref 2, written Yb3(Si3Pd10)2, hull 0.000, no ICSD reference, primary

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 048 for the Pd-Si-Yb host. One of its two samples is Yb3Pd20Si6, from a paper on the physical phenomena of the cage compounds RE3Pd20Si6 (RE = Yb, Lu).

The rare earth occupies two distinct cage sites, 4a and 8c, of the Cr23C6-type ordering. The 8c guest is the loosely bound one, and it carries the heavy-fermion and quadrupolar physics that made Ce3Pd20Ge6 and Ce3Pd20Si6 well known. Stage 3 should therefore treat the rare earth as a host species on two sites, not as the filler of one cage.
[ref 2] has the formula at mp-1207621 in Fm-3m but with no ICSD backing, so the space group rests on the literature for the family rather than on a measured reference in the snapshot.

The telluride analogue petzite, Ag3AuTe2, has the same type and the paper title is plural, so the entry is written for the Ag3AuX2 pair.

The compound is made topotactically from Li2RuO3 by exchanging the interlayer lithium for silver, so it sits between li2mo3_honeycomb and delafossite and matches neither entry as written.
The iridium member is a Kitaev spin-liquid candidate, so the family is likely to recur. No reference covers the host and no mp_id is proposed.

formula_archetype: RTAl4Ge2 (R = rare earth, T = Au, Ag)

formula_archetype: RTX or RXX2 (R = rare earth; T and X two species ordered on the three-connected ThSi2 net)

discriminate_from.alpha_thsi2: the centrosymmetric parent, I4_1/amd, with one species on the three-connected net. discriminate_from.spinel: Mn3O4 and mixed-valence Mn spinels also hold Mn3+ and Mn4+, but on a cubic close-packed lattice with no large A cation
discriminate_from.hollandite: a Mn4+ tunnel oxide with edge-sharing double chains of octahedra and a large cation in the tunnels, but with an A:Mn ratio near 1:8, not 1:2

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 056 for the Bi-Mn-O host: one sample, written Bi2Mn4O10 (that is, BiMn2O5), from a paper on magnetic and transport properties helped by local distortions.

The Pbam structure is recalled from the RMn2O5 multiferroic literature and has not been checked against the paper. The chunk 056 [ref 2] lists five Bi-Mn-O phases (MnBiO3 C2/c, Mn7BiO12, Mn2Bi3O7, Mn16Bi16O45, Mn(Bi5O8)5) and none of them is BiMn2O5, so no structure database candidate is recorded. Stage 2 must query MP for BiMn2O5 directly.
Doping chemistry: substitution goes on the A site (rare earth for Bi) or on either Mn site. Fe and Ga prefer the Mn3+ pyramids. No minor elements are present in chunk 056.

display_name: CaC2 / ThC2 metal dicarbide (acetylide C2 dumbbells)
formula_archetype: MC2 with isolated C2 dumbbells (M = alkaline earth, divalent or trivalent lanthanide, actinide)
typical_space_group: I4/mmm (139) for the tetragonal CaC2 type; C2/c (15) for the monoclinic ThC2-type distortion

discriminate_from.rocksalt_nitride_carbide: monocarbides such as TiC or UC have isolated C atoms in octahedral holes. Dicarbides hold C2 dumbbells with a C-C bond
discriminate_from.graphite_layered: graphite intercalation compounds such as EuC6 are layered carbons with metal between the sheets, not salts of discrete C2 units
discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: also body-centred tetragonal I4/mmm, but a ternary with a layered T2X2 block. CaC2 is a distorted rocksalt with C2 units on the anion site

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 057 for the C-Eu host: one sample, EuC2, from a paper on structural phase transitions in EuC2.

The tetragonal CaC2 type is a rocksalt arrangement stretched along c by the aligned C2 dumbbells. Tilting the dumbbells gives the monoclinic ThC2-type cell, C2/c. Several dicarbides pass from monoclinic to tetragonal to cubic (freely rotating C2) on heating. The transition temperatures are recalled, not read from the paper, so no values are recorded here.

The chunk 057 [ref 2] lists EuC2 at I4/mmm (mp-1018177, 2 ICSD references) and at C2/c (mp-1077301, 1 ICSD reference). Both are candidates for stage 2. Which one is the ambient phase must be read from the paper.
Doping chemistry: substitution goes on the metal site. The C2 unit charge (C2 2-) sets whether a dicarbide is a salt-like insulator or a metal (trivalent LaC2 has one extra electron per formula).

formula_archetype: AM3O4 (A = Na, Ca, Sr, Cd, a lanthanide; M = Pd or Pt), with square-planar MO4 units

discriminate_from.pbpdo2_layered: PbPdO2 also holds square-planar PdO4, but as a 1:1 layered or chain oxide, not a 1:3 cubic framework
discriminate_from.perovskite: a 1:1 ABO3 with octahedral B sites. In NaPt3O4 the Pd sits in square-planar coordination and the A cation is in an 8-coordinate cube
discriminate_from.cacu3ti4o12: also cubic, with square-planar Cu. But it is an A-site-ordered perovskite that also has TiO6 octahedra. NaPt3O4 has no octahedral cation

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 057 for the Ca-Cu-O-Pd host: one sample, Ca0.7Na0.3Pd2.5Cu0.5O4, from a paper on a logarithmic temperature dependence of resistivity in hole-doped CaPd3O4.

CaPd3O4 is a narrow-gap semiconductor. Replacing Ca2+ with Na+ adds holes to the Pd-O network and makes it metallic. The Pm-3n structure is recalled from the literature. The chunk offers no reference line for this host, so no structure database candidate is recorded.
Doping chemistry: alkali (Na, Li) on the A site is the hole-doping knob. Cu for Pd goes on the square-planar site.

display_name: Azurite Cu3(CO3)2(OH)2, diamond-chain basic copper carbonate
formula_archetype: Cu3(CO3)2(OH)2

discriminate_from.tenorite: CuO is a binary oxide with no carbonate or hydroxide groups
discriminate_from.molecular_coordination_crystal: azurite is an extended ionic mineral framework, not a packing of discrete neutral complexes
discriminate_from.kagome_staircase_m3v2o8: also a frustrated Cu or Ni magnet built from a corner-sharing motif, but a vanadate with kagome-staircase layers, not a carbonate with diamond chains

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 057 for the C-Cu-H-O host: one single crystal, Cu3(CO3)2(OH)2, from a paper on thermal conductivity and spin state of the spin diamond-chain system azurite.

The Cu2+ S=1/2 ions form distorted diamond chains along b, which is why azurite is studied as a model frustrated quantum magnet. There is also a weak structural transition near 410 K reported in the literature, recalled and not checked.

The chunk 057 [ref 2] ranks Cu3H2(CO4)2 P2_1/c (mp-23733, hull 0.007, 5 ICSD references) PRIMARY. That formula is azurite. It is taken as the mp_id in the ledger record, but structure_database_candidates stays empty until stage 2 resolves it.
Doping chemistry: not a thermoelectric host. Minor elements would substitute on the Cu site.

formula_archetype: AxRE2Cu6-xTe6 (A = K, Rb, Cs; RE = La, Ce, Pr, Nd; x below 1)
typical_space_group: orthorhombic, Immm (71) recalled -- NOT VERIFIED, see notes

discriminate_from.csag5te3_type: the nearest existing entry, also an alkali cation sitting in open tunnels of a coinage-metal telluride framework, but with no rare earth and at a different stoichiometry. Here the framework is built from RE-Te and Cu-Te polyhedra together and the alkali content x is variable and tied to the Cu deficiency
discriminate_from.ba3cu14te12_polytelluride: a coinage-metal polytelluride with a heavy electropositive cation, but with Te-Te bonding and no rare earth
discriminate_from.acu5q3_layered: a layered alkali copper chalcogenide; the double-tunnel compounds are a three-dimensional framework, not a stack of slabs
discriminate_from.unresolved_crystalline: where this host would otherwise be parked; proposed so the family has a home if further members appear down the tail

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 058 for the Ce-Cs-Cu-Te host: one bulk sample, Cs0.772Ce2Cu5.232Te6, from the Chem. Mater. paper on syntheses, structures, and magnetic and thermoelectric properties of double-tunnel tellurides.

The double-tunnel description and the charge balance -- the alkali content x and the Cu deficiency move together, so the total monovalent cation count A + Cu stays at 6 and charge balance with RE3+ and Te2- is kept -- come from the paper title and the formula. The space group is recalled, not read, and must be confirmed from the paper before stage 2.
No structure reference was matched for this host, so there is nothing to test the recalled cell against.

Doping chemistry: x (the alkali tunnel occupancy) and the matching Cu deficiency are the compositional variables, not dopants. Record them as non_stoichiometry if they fall below the 5 at.% cut in other members.

formula_archetype: AM11 with A a large electropositive atom (alkaline earth or rare earth) and M = Zn, Cd or Hg

discriminate_from.nazn13_type: the other Zn-rich cage type, cubic Fm-3m with a Zn-centred icosahedral framework at AZn13. BaCd11 is tetragonal and less Zn rich, with the large atom in a 22-vertex polyhedron
discriminate_from.cacu5: the hexagonal RM5 aristotype that CeZn5 takes. BaCd11 is reached only at much higher M content and is not a CaCu5 derivative
discriminate_from.thmn12_tetragonal: also a tetragonal rare-earth-poor intermetallic (RM12), but body-centred I4/mmm built from CaCu5 slabs with dumbbell substitution, not the BaCd11 framework
discriminate_from.cecr2al20_cage: a cubic cage compound at RT2X20; different stoichiometry and symmetry

structure_database_candidates: CeZn11 I4_1/amd (141) mp-640370 [MP, hull 0.004, 4 ICSD refs] as listed in the chunk 059 ref line
notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 059 for the Ce-Zn host: one single-crystal sample of CeZn11 from the PRB paper on anisotropic transport and magnetic properties and a field-tuned transition.
The BaCd11 assignment is recalled for the RZn11 series and is consistent with the MP ref line, which gives CeZn11 in I4_1/amd with 4 ICSD references.
Doping chemistry: none in this sample. In other RZn11 members the rare-earth site is the natural substitution site.

display_name: Li3MX6 ternary lithium halide (close-packed halide superionic conductor)
formula_archetype: Li3MX6 with M a trivalent metal (Y, Er, In, Sc) and X = Cl or Br
typical_space_group: two variants: C2/m (12) on a cubic close-packed halide array (Li3InCl6, Li3ScCl6), and P-3m1 (164) on a hexagonal close-packed array (Li3YCl6, Li3ErCl6). Both recalled -- NOT VERIFIED, see notes

discriminate_from.rocksalt: the parent of the ccp variant: Li3InCl6 is rocksalt-derived, with Li, In and vacancies ordered over the octahedral sites. LiCl itself is plain rocksalt, and the ordering of trivalent M and vacancies is what makes this a separate structure
discriminate_from.cdcl2_r3m_dihalide: a layered MX2 halide with every second octahedral layer empty. The Li3MX6 compounds fill the octahedral layers partially and in both layers, so they are not layered in the CdCl2 sense
discriminate_from.bii3_layered_trihalide: an MX3 layered trihalide with no lithium
discriminate_from.argyrodite: the other major lithium superionic conductor family, a sulfide-halide with a tetrahedrally close-packed anion frame (Li6PS5Cl)
discriminate_from.k2ptcl6_a2bx6: an A2BX6 antifluorite-like arrangement of isolated octahedra, not a close-packed array with ordered octahedral cations

structure_database_candidates: Li3InCl6 C2 (5) mp-676109 [MP, hull 0.000, no ICSD refs] and Li3InCl6 Fm-3m (225) mp-1111288 [hull 0.231] as listed in the chunk 059 ref line. The C2 cell is taken as a lower-symmetry setting of the C2/m structure; confirm in stage 2
notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 059 for the Cl-In-Li and Cl-Li-Y hosts. Both samples come from the Small paper arguing that good solid-state electrolytes have low, glass-like thermal conductivity, alongside LiCl and Li6PS5Cl.
The two space-group variants are recalled, not read. MP lists Li3InCl6 in C2 rather than C2/m, and no structure reference was matched for Li3YCl6, so neither variant is confirmed by the data here.
Doping chemistry: aliovalent M-site substitution (Zr4+ for Y3+ or In3+) is the usual carrier-concentration knob and creates Li vacancies. Record the Li deficit as non_stoichiometry.

formula_archetype: RTX2 (R = rare earth or U; T = late transition metal Co, Ni, Fe, Cu; X = Si, Ge, Sn, Sb)

discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: the RT2X2 BaAl4-derived tetragonal structure, in the same R-T-X chemistries. The ratio decides: RT2X2 has twice the transition metal of RTX2, and CeNiSi2 is orthorhombic with a stacking of AlB2-like and BaAl4-like slabs rather than the pure BaAl4 derivative
discriminate_from.alb2: the AlB2-like R-X slab is one building block of CeNiSi2, but the structure also carries T-X layers of BaAl4 type and so has T as an essential third component
discriminate_from.zrbesi_ordered_alb2: an ordered AlB2 superstructure at RTX with a 1:1:1 ratio, not RTX2
discriminate_from.banisn3_i4mm: the non-centrosymmetric RTX3 BaNiSn3 type, which appears in the same Ce/La-T-Ge series at a higher X content (LaCoGe3 I4mm in the chunk 060 reference line)

structure_database_candidates: LaCoGe2 Cmcm (63) mp-1095134 [MP, hull 0.000, 2 ICSD refs] as listed in the chunk 060 ref line
notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 060 for the Co-Ge-La host (LaCoGe2, from a paper on transport in intermetallic RCoGe2). An earlier record (Ce-Ge-Ni, chunk 10) already noted CeNiGe2 in that host without a matching entry.
Commonly written with T sites partly vacant (CeNi1-xSi2, CeCo1-xGe2), so a T deficit should be recorded as non_stoichiometry, not as a foreign dopant.
The space group Cmcm is recalled and agrees with the MP entry named above; the prototype assignment of that entry has not been checked beyond its space group.

formula_archetype: M2T12X7 (M = Zr, Hf, rare earth, U; T = Fe, Co, Ni; X = P, As)
typical_space_group: P-6 (174). Recalled -- NOT VERIFIED, see notes

discriminate_from.zr6coas2_type: a hexagonal metal-rich pnictide from the same family of tricapped trigonal-prism structures, but at the opposite end of the metal ratio: M-rich M6TX2 rather than T-rich M2T12X7
discriminate_from.tinisi_co2si: the orthorhombic MTX equiatomic phosphide (HfCoP Pnma in the chunk 060 reference line), with a 1:1:1 ratio
discriminate_from.zrnial_fe2p: the Fe2P-derived hexagonal ZrNiAl type, also built from trigonal prisms in the same chemistries but at an MTX ratio

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 060 for the Co-Hf-P host: Hf2Co12P7, measured 10-297 K in a book chapter on correlated electron systems that also covers Ln3Pt4Ge6.

No structure reference covers Hf2Co12P7. The MP entries listed for the host (Hf2Co4P3 P-62m, Hf2CoP, HfCoP, Hf4CoP, Hf20Co5P11) are other compounds, so neither the space group nor an mp_id can be taken from the data here; P-6 is recalled.
Rare-earth members (Yb2Co12P7, Ce2Co12P7) are studied for valence fluctuation and heavy-fermion behaviour; the M site is where 4f moments sit.

formula_archetype: AxM5X8 (A = Tl, Ba, K, Rb, In; M = Cr, V, Ti; X = S, Se, Te; x = 0.5-1)

discriminate_from.hollandite: the tetragonal I4/m AxM8O16 oxide framework with square 2x2 tunnels; the pseudo-hollandite chalcogenides are monoclinic, with rectangular tunnels built from edge-sharing double octahedral chains and a different M:X ratio (5:8, not 1:2)
discriminate_from.cr3s4_defect_nias: the monoclinic Cr3S4 vacancy-ordered NiAs derivative, also C2/m and in the same chemistries, but with no tunnel cation: vacancies are ordered in alternate metal layers instead
discriminate_from.nias: the parent CrSe/Cr2Se3 NiAs family the Cr-Se host otherwise holds

structure_database_candidates: mp-3407 (TlCr5Se8 C2/m, 3 ICSD refs, from the chunk 061 reference line)
notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 061 for the Cr-Se-Tl host: TlCr5Se8, from a Chem. Mater. paper whose title names the pseudo-hollandite structure. [ref 2] gives TlCr5Se8 in C2/m, mp-3407, hull 0.000, 3 ICSD refs, which matches.
Also resolves the chunk 6 Cr-Se record, which filed BaxCr5Se8 under hollandite and flagged that as a stretch because hollandite is defined as an oxide framework. Those Ba compositions belong here.
The tunnel cation (Tl, Ba) is a structural guest; the role vocabulary has no tunnel-cation value and cage_filler has been used for it.

formula_archetype: AxMo12X14 (A = Cs, Rb, K, Tl, In, with Cu or Ag inserted; X = Se, S)

discriminate_from.chevrel: MxMo6X8, built from single Mo6 octahedral clusters; A2Mo12Se14 is built from Mo12 clusters, two Mo6 octahedra fused by a shared face
discriminate_from.mo9se11_cluster: Ag3.6Mo9Se11, built from Mo9 clusters (two face-shared Mo6), one condensation step short of Mo12
discriminate_from.tl2mo3se3_chain: the infinite-chain (Mo3X3) limit of the same condensation series, with one-dimensional rather than cluster-based transport

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 061 for the Cs-Cu-Mo-Se host: Cu2Cs2Mo12Se14, measured 12-615 K, from an Inorg. Chem. paper with no title captured in the chunk. No structure reference covers it, so no space group or mp_id is taken from the data; R-3 is recalled for the rhombohedral Mo12 cluster series and must be confirmed from the paper.
Cu (or Ag) inserted into the voids between cluster units is a compositional variable like M in the Chevrel phases: it sets the electron count on the cluster rather than acting as a dilute dopant.
Sits between mo9se11_cluster and the proposed a2mo15se19_cluster in the Mo cluster condensation series.

display_name: AMSb4 alkali-triel antimonide Zintl phase (RbGaSb4 / CsGaSb4 type)
formula_archetype: AMSb4 (A = Rb, Cs, K; M = Al, Ga)
typical_space_group: not established here -- NOT VERIFIED, read from the paper

discriminate_from.zintl_5_2_6: A5M2Sb6 with divalent A: chains of MSb4 tetrahedra linked by Sb-Sb bonds; the AMSb4 phases carry a monovalent cation and a much higher Sb:M ratio, so most Sb takes part in Sb-Sb bonded polyanions
discriminate_from.zintl_3_1_3: A3MSb3, isolated or dimerised MSb4 units with far less Sb-Sb bonding
discriminate_from.caal2si2_zintl: layered AM2X2 with a trigonal anionic slab, the 1-2-2 Zintl archetype
discriminate_from.zintl_2_1_2_a2cdsb2: A2MX2 with a divalent tetrahedral metal

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 061 for the Cs-Ga-Sb host: (Ba0.025Cs0.975)1.05GaSb4, from an ACS Appl. Energy Mater. paper titled Discovery of n-Type Zintl Phases RbAlSb4, RbGaSb4, CsAlSb4 and CsGaSb4. The title names four members, so this is a family and not a single compound.

The reference lines for the host, Cs2GaSb2 Pnma and Cs6GaSb3 P2_1/m, are other compounds, so no space group or mp_id is taken from the data. I cannot recall the space group reliably, so none is given; stage 2 must read it from the paper.
The interest is n-type doping of an Sb-rich Zintl phase: Ba2+ on the alkali site is the donor in the chunk 061 composition.

display_name: ALn(MoO4)2 layered alkali rare-earth double molybdate (KY(MoO4)2 / CsDy(MoO4)2 type)
formula_archetype: ALn(MO4)2 (A = K, Rb, Cs; Ln = rare earth; M = Mo, W)
typical_space_group: not fixed here -- the chunk 062 reference offers P2/c (13, 1 ICSD ref) and Pccm (49, computed) for CsGd(MoO4)2; NOT VERIFIED, read from the paper

discriminate_from.scheelite_awo4: the three-dimensional AMO4 scheelite, which the smaller-alkali double molybdates (NaLn(MoO4)2) adopt with A and Ln disordered on one site; the large-alkali members are layered instead, with Ln-Mo-O sheets separated by alkali layers
discriminate_from.ln2mw2o10_double_tungstate: R2MW2O10, built from edge-sharing W2O10 dimers at a different stoichiometry and with a divalent second cation
discriminate_from.lamox_la2mo2o9: the La2Mo2O9 oxide-ion conductor, a rare-earth molybdate with no alkali and a cubic fluorite-related framework
