mp-1213392 (CsGd(MoO4)2 Pccm, hull 0.000, no ICSD ref)
notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 062 for the Cs-Gd-Mo-O host: a single crystal of CsGd(MoO4)2 from a paper titled Thermal Conductivity of a Layered CsGd(MoO4)2 Crystal, measured 10-49 K.

These crystals are studied for cooperative Jahn-Teller transitions of the rare-earth ion at low temperature, which change the space group; the transition temperature for the Gd member is not known here, so none is recorded.
The low-dimensional layering is named in the paper title rather than inferred from the formula.

formula_archetype: CuMO3 (M = Ge, Si), edge-sharing CuO4 plaquette chains linked by corner-sharing MO4 tetrahedral chains
typical_space_group: Pbmm, the Pmma (51) setting, above the spin-Peierls transition; dimerised below about 14 K

discriminate_from.cuprate_chain: Sr2CuO3 / SrCuO2, alkaline-earth cuprates with corner- or edge-sharing CuO chains and no tetrahedral partner; CuGeO3 contains no large cation and its chains are separated by GeO4 tetrahedral chains
discriminate_from.metavanadate_chain: AVO3 with chains of corner-sharing VO4 tetrahedra; here the tetrahedral chains are GeO4 and the magnetic chain is the separate edge-sharing CuO2 ribbon
discriminate_from.perovskite: the ABO3 formula without any perovskite topology: no twelve-coordinate A site and no corner-sharing octahedral network

structure_database_candidates: mp-1087506 (CuGeO3 Pmma, 26 ICSD refs, from the chunk 062 reference line)
notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 062 for the Cu-Ge-O host: a CuGeO3 single crystal in a paper on the thermal conductivity of the spin-Peierls compound CuGeO3, measured 10-40 K.

The spin-Peierls transition near 14 K dimerises the Cu chains and lowers the symmetry; that is a real structural transition inside the 10-40 K window, and the low-temperature cell is commonly given as a doubled orthorhombic cell. The temperature is recalled and should be read from the paper.
Zn-for-Cu and Si-for-Ge substituted crystals are the usual doping series in this compound.

display_name: Trigonal RCuQ2 with half-occupied tetrahedral Cu (ErCuSe2 type)
formula_archetype: RCuQ2 (R = Y and the smaller rare earths; Q = S, Se)
typical_space_group: P-3m1 (164) with Cu statistically on half the tetrahedral sites -- recalled, NOT VERIFIED; ordered computed cells appear in P3m1 (156)

discriminate_from.caal2si2_zintl: the fully occupied AM2X2 parent: the same octahedral cation layer and tetrahedral double layer, but with every tetrahedral site filled; in RCuQ2 only half the Cu sites are occupied, which is what makes the formula RCuQ2 rather than RCu2Q2
discriminate_from.cucrs2_layered: ABX2 with Cu in tetrahedral sites between octahedral CrS2 layers, rhombohedral R3m and fully ordered, with one tetrahedral Cu layer per octahedral layer
discriminate_from.cdi2_1t: the RQ2 octahedral layer on its own, without the interlayer Cu
discriminate_from.chalcopyrite: the other CuMQ2 formula, a fully tetrahedral sphalerite superstructure; the rare earth here is octahedral and too large for a tetrahedral site

structure_database_candidates: mp-675180 (ErCuSe2 P3m1, no ICSD ref, chunk 062)
mp-675349 (DyCuSe2 P3m1, no ICSD ref, chunk 062)
notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 062 for the Cu-Er-Se, Cu-Dy-Se and Cu-Gd-Se hosts, all three from one J. Alloys Compd. 2014 paper on the thermoelectric properties and crystal and electronic structure of semiconducting RCuSe2.
The larger rare earths (La to about Gd) take the monoclinic LaCuS2 type instead, so the Gd member sits at the boundary and must be confirmed from the paper; it is filed here at low confidence.
The Cu site half-occupancy is a structural feature, not a dopant: Cu deficit or excess beyond RCuQ2 is non_stoichiometry.

formula_archetype: ACu7-xQ4 (A = K, Rb, Tl, NH4; Q = S, Se)

discriminate_from.pseudo_hollandite_tlv5s8: a tunnel chalcogenide of octahedral transition metals; here the framework is built from Cu in tetrahedral and trigonal coordination and the Cu sublattice is partly disordered and mobile
discriminate_from.hollandite: the tetragonal I4/m oxide AxM8O16 with the same tunnel symmetry, but an octahedral oxide framework
discriminate_from.cu2se_superionic: binary Cu2-xQ with a mobile Cu sublattice and no tunnel cation; a K-doped Cu2-xS sample would belong there instead, so the composition has to be checked
discriminate_from.acu5q3_layered: a copper-rich alkali chalcogenide that is layered rather than built around one-dimensional tunnels

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 062 for the Cu-K-S host: KCu6.8S4 films, from a J. Mater. Chem. A paper titled Introducing kalium into copper sulfide for the enhancement of thermoelectric properties.
[ref 2] lists KCu7S4 P1 mp-1223529 (hull 0.019, no ICSD ref), an ordered computed approximant of the disordered tunnel structure, so neither its space group nor its mp_id is taken as the structure.
K sits in the tunnels as a structural guest; the Cu deficit x in KCu7-xS4 sets the hole concentration and is non_stoichiometry.

formula_archetype: Cu3MQ4 (M = V, Nb, Ta; Q = S, Se, Te)

discriminate_from.famatinite: the other Cu3MQ4 family and the one this formula would otherwise be forced into. Famatinite and enargite are full sphalerite or wurtzite superstructures in which every tetrahedral cation site is filled and M is a group-15 or group-14 cation. In sulvanite M is a group-5 transition metal, the cell is a small primitive cube with one formula unit, and the Cu and V tetrahedra share edges around empty sites, so it is not a simple cation-ordered sphalerite
discriminate_from.sphalerite: the parent tetrahedral framework, with one cation species and no ordering
discriminate_from.spinel: CuV2S4 shares the Cu-V-S element set but is a thiospinel with octahedral V, at a different stoichiometry; the two have to be separated by composition

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 063 for the Cu-Se-V host: Cu3VSe4, from a paper titled Thermoelectric properties of p-Type Cu3VSe4 with high Seebeck coefficient.
[ref 1] TEDesignLab gives VCu3Se4 P-43m (215) mp-21855 with 4 ICSD references, and for the Cu-S-V host VCu3S4 P-43m mp-3762 with 10, so the space group rests on ICSD evidence rather than recall.
The sulvanites are studied as p-type thermoelectrics and transparent conductors; flat valence bands from the Cu-Q network give the high Seebeck coefficient.

formula_archetype: RCu2 (R = Ce and the heavier rare earths, Y), and other AB2 KHg2-type compounds

discriminate_from.laves_phase: the other common AB2 intermetallic and the default reading of the formula. Laves phases are tetrahedrally close-packed MgCu2, MgZn2 or MgNi2 with 12-coordinate B and 16-coordinate A; the KHg2 type is an orthorhombic arrangement of B zigzag chains, and the RCu2 compounds are not Laves phases
discriminate_from.alb2: the hexagonal AB2 parent. KHg2 is an orthorhombic distortion of AlB2 in which the flat B honeycomb is puckered, which is why some light rare-earth RCu2 compounds sit on the boundary between the two
discriminate_from.cecu6: the copper-rich Ce-Cu heavy-fermion compound; the Ce-Cu host holds both, separable by the Cu:R ratio

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 063 for the Cu-Y host: YCu2, in a paper titled CeCu2: a new Kondo lattice showing magnetic order, where the yttrium compound is the non-magnetic isostructural reference.
[ref 2] gives YCu2 Imma (74) mp-2698 with 4 ICSD references at hull 0.000, which supports the space group.
In the Kondo-lattice studies the rare-earth site is the variable; Y and La analogues serve to subtract the phonon and conduction-electron background.

formula_archetype: Cu5Zn8, Cu9Al4, Ag5Zn8 and other electron compounds near 21/13 valence electrons per atom

discriminate_from.b2_cscl: beta-brass CuZn, the ordered bcc Hume-Rothery phase at about 3/2 electrons per atom and 45-49 at.% Zn. Gamma brass is its 3x3x3 superstructure with vacancies and relaxed positions, 52 atoms per cubic cell, at higher Zn content
discriminate_from.solid_solution_alloy: alpha brass, the disordered fcc Cu(Zn) solid solution below roughly 38 at.% Zn
discriminate_from.quasicrystal_approximant: gamma brass is built from 26-atom clusters and is sometimes discussed alongside approximants, but it is an ordinary periodic structure with its own MP entry and no quasicrystal to approximate

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 063 for the Cu-Zn host: Zn58.71Cu41.29, from a paper titled Correlation between structural and low-temperature thermoelectric properties of (title truncated).
[ref 2] gives Zn8Cu5 I-43m (217) mp-1368 with 6 ICSD references at hull 0.000 as the Cu-Zn primary.

Brasses change structure with Zn content, alpha fcc, beta bcc/B2, gamma, epsilon hcp, so a Cu-Zn host has to be split per composition; 58.7 at.% Zn sits at the Zn-poor edge of the gamma field, near the beta plus gamma two-phase region.

formula_archetype: PbCuMQ3 (M = Sb, As, Bi; Q = S, Se)

discriminate_from.tetrahedrite: the other copper antimony sulfide thermoelectric, where low lattice thermal conductivity comes from rattling trigonal-planar Cu inside a cubic cage framework. Bournonite has no cage; its low conductivity comes from the stereochemically active lone pairs on Sb and Pb
discriminate_from.stibnite: the Sb2S3 ribbon structure, the lone-pair parent of the sulfosalts but with no Pb or Cu
discriminate_from.skinnerite_cu3sbse3: a copper antimony chalcogenide with a trigonal-pyramidal SbQ3 lone pair and a Cu:Sb ratio of 3 to 1, not a lead sulfosalt
discriminate_from.famatinite: Cu3SbS4, a fully tetrahedral sphalerite superstructure with Sb(V) and no lone pair

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 063 for the Cu-Pb-S-Sb host: PbCuSbS3, from a paper titled Bournonite PbCuSbS3: Stereochemically Active Lone-Pair Electrons that Induce Low Thermal Conductivity.
[ref 2] gives CuSbPbS3 Pmn2_1 (31) mp-649774 with 4 ICSD references at hull 0.004, flagged weak by the chunk rule but consistent with the known orthorhombic mineral.
The mineral is a natural sulfosalt; SbS3 trigonal pyramids and tetrahedral Cu link Pb-centred polyhedra.

formula_archetype: Tl2Cu2MQ4 (M = Sn, Ge; Q = S, Se, Te) -- family extent recalled, NOT VERIFIED
typical_space_group: Ibam (72) for the sulfide per [ref 2]; the telluride is listed only as a computed Fmm2 (42) cell

discriminate_from.stannite_kesterite: Cu2BCX4, the tetrahedral quaternary this formula resembles. Here there are five cations for four anions, the two Cu and the Sn build a tetrahedral Cu-Sn-Q network, and Tl(I) sits outside it as a large lone-pair cation, so the structure cannot be a filled sphalerite
discriminate_from.tl5te3: the thallium telluride intermetallic at 5:3, with no copper-tin framework
discriminate_from.inte_tlse: the 1:1 Tl chalcogenide with eight-coordinate Tl(I), the closest analogy for the thallium site only

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 063 for the Cu-S-Sn-Tl and Cu-Sn-Te-Tl hosts, both from a Chem. Mater. paper titled Exploring Thallium Compounds as Thermoelectric Materials: Seventeen New Thallium Chalcogenides.

[ref 2] gives Tl2Cu2SnS4 Ibam (72) mp-18240 with 1 ICSD reference, and Tl2Cu2SnTe4 Fmm2 (42) mp-1216636 with none. Whether sulfide and telluride are isotypic is NOT VERIFIED; if they are not, the telluride should move to its own entry or to unresolved_crystalline.
The low-dimensional character of the Cu-Sn-Q network (layers or chains, as in the alkali analogues) is recalled rather than checked; dimensionality is given as 3D pending the structure file.

formula_archetype: ACu2O2 (A = Li, Na) with Cu(I) and Cu(II) in equal amounts

discriminate_from.cuprate_chain: the Sr2CuO3 and SrCuO2 chain cuprates. Those are built from corner-sharing CuO4 plaquettes and hold only Cu(II); LiCu2O2 has edge-sharing Cu(II)O4 chains, which makes it a frustrated spin chain with multiferroic order, plus a separate Cu(I) layer
discriminate_from.delafossite: CuMO2 with linear O-Cu(I)-O dumbbells between octahedral layers; LiCu2O2 contains the same Cu(I) dumbbell motif but its Cu(II) layer is chains of square plaquettes, not edge-sharing octahedra
discriminate_from.alpha_nafeo2_layered: LiMO2 layered rock salt, where lithium and the transition metal order in alternate octahedral layers

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 063 for the Cu-Li-O host: LiCu2O2 single crystals, from a paper titled Crystal Growth, Thermal Stability, and Electrical Properties of LiCu2O2.
[ref 2] gives Li(CuO)2 Pnma (62) mp-18162 with 3 ICSD references at hull 0.011; the other Li-Cu-O primaries, Li2CuO2 Immm and LiCuO, are different compositions.
Li/Cu antisite disorder and twinning are common in grown crystals, so a Li-poor or Cu-rich formula is non_stoichiometry rather than a dopant.

formula_archetype: R2M3X5 (R = Sc, Y or heavy rare earth; M = Mn, Fe, Co, Rh; X = Si, Ge)

discriminate_from.u2co3si5_type: the same 2-3-5 stoichiometry, but orthorhombic Ibam with a different arrangement of the transition-metal and silicon sites. The u2co3si5_type proposal already notes that some R2M3X5 members take the tetragonal Sc2Fe3Si5 type instead; the two are distinct structures, not settings of one, so a composition cannot pick between them and the space group has to
discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: the RM2X2 BaAl4 derivative, I4/mmm, which is the ICSD-best-attested phase in the same R-Mn-Si chemistries (DyMn2Si2, ErMn2Si2). The ratio separates them: 1-2-2 against 2-3-5
discriminate_from.tinisi_co2si: the equiatomic RMX Pnma phase that also occurs in these systems (DyMnSi, ErMnSi)

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 064 for the Dy-Mn-Si and Er-Mn-Si hosts: Dy2Mn3Si5 and Er2Mn3Si5, from one paper on magnetism and electronic transport in R2Mn3Si5 (R = Dy, Ho, Er).
[ref 2] gives Er2Mn3Si5 P4/mnc (128) mp-622190 at hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references, which is the Sc2Fe3Si5 type. It has no Dy2Mn3Si5 entry; the Dy member is taken to be isostructural.
The R2Fe3Si5 members are studied for coexisting superconductivity and magnetism, so the family recurs in low-temperature transport work.

formula_archetype: R2Q3 (R = Sc, Y or heavy rare earth; Q = S, Se, Te)

discriminate_from.rocksalt: the parent. Sc2S3 keeps the NaCl anion framework but one cation site in three is empty and the vacancies order, giving an orthorhombic supercell. The monochalcogenides RQ in the same host (ErTe, ErSe) are true rocksalt and stay there
discriminate_from.th3p4: the other R2Q3/R3Q4 sesquichalcogenide structure, taken by the light rare earths (La2Te3, Nd2Te3) with vacancies disordered on a body-centred cubic cation sublattice. The heavy rare-earth sesquitellurides take Sc2S3 instead, so the rare earth decides
discriminate_from.ga2te3_defect_zincblende: the analogous vacancy-ordered derivative of a tetrahedral, not octahedral, parent

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 064 for the Er-Te host: Er2Te3, from a 1966 paper on thermoelectric and electrical measurements in the erbium-tellurium system.
[ref 2] gives Er2Te3 Fddd (70) mp-14643 at hull 0.000 with 2 ICSD references. The host primary is ErTe Fm-3m with 3, which is the monotelluride, a different composition.
The vacancies are part of the structure, not a dopant: deviations toward R3Q4 fill them and are non_stoichiometry.

formula_archetype: M2XO4 with M a divalent octahedral cation (Mg, Fe, Mn, Co, Ni) and X = Si, Ge; also LiFePO4-type phosphates

discriminate_from.spinel: the high-pressure form of the same M2SiO4 formula (ringwoodite, ahrensite), cubic Fd-3m with Si on the tetrahedral and M on the octahedral site. It is heavily represented in ICSD because of mantle-mineral work, so a reference ranking by ICSD count can put it first, but it is never reached on heating at ambient pressure. The olivine is the ambient phase
discriminate_from.larnite_ca2sio4: the Ca2SiO4 polymorph family. gamma-Ca2SiO4 is olivine-like, but the Ca silicates run through a distinct beta/alpha-prime/alpha sequence on heating and are kept in their own entry; olivine here is for the small-cation M2SiO4 members that do not transform before melting

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 065 for the Fe-O-Si host: Fe2SiO4 from a paper on iron-oxide scales on Si-containing steels, where fayalite forms at the scale-steel interface.

[ref 2] ranks Fe2SiO4 Fd-3m (227) mp-18816 first on 29 ICSD references at hull 0.037. That is the high-pressure spinel polymorph; the ambient olivine Pnma entry was not listed in the chunk file, so its mp_id has to be resolved in stage 2.
Fayalite melts near 1478 K with no polymorphic change at ambient pressure, so a thermal measurement stays in one phase.

formula_archetype: RF3 with R = Sm to Lu and Y (the smaller rare earths)

discriminate_from.tysonite_laf3: the trigonal P-3c1 trifluoride of the large rare earths (La to Nd). The rare earth decides: the light ones are tysonite, the heavy ones beta-YF3. Several of the heavy trifluorides turn to a tysonite-like or alpha-YF3 form only close to their melting points, well above any transport window
discriminate_from.cotunnite_pbcl2: a different Pnma halide, AX2 not AX3; the space group alone does not separate them, the stoichiometry does

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 065 for the F-Ho host: HoF3 single crystal, from a paper on the thermal conductivity of rare-earth fluoride crystals.
No structure reference was matched for this host in the chunk file, so the space group is from materials knowledge and the mp_id is left for stage 2.
The same paper measured other rare-earth trifluorides; the ones from Sm onward belong here, La to Nd in tysonite_laf3.

formula_archetype: A3M2Pn4 with A a divalent cation (Ca, Sr, Eu), M a group 13 metal (Al, Ga, In) and Pn = P, As
typical_space_group: C2/c (15) for the Ca3Al2As4 type; Pnnm (58) for the Sr3In2P4 type

discriminate_from.zintl_5_2_6: the Ca5Al2Sb6 A5M2Pn6 chain Zintl, also built of MPn4 tetrahedra, but more A-rich and with ladder-like double chains. Separate on the A:M:Pn ratio, 3:2:4 against 5:2:6
discriminate_from.zintl_3_1_3: the A3MPn3 Zintl built of isolated or dimerised tetrahedra; MP lists Eu3GaP3 and Eu3InP3 in the same hosts, so again the ratio decides
discriminate_from.euin2p2_type: the layered AM2Pn2 phase of the same Eu-In-P chemistry, with M-M bonded slabs

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 065 for the Eu-Ga-P and Eu-In-P hosts: Eu3Ga2P4 and Eu3In2P4 from one paper on phase characterisation, thermal stability and high-temperature transport of Eu3M2P4 Zintl phosphides.

This is a composition family covering two closely related structure types built from corner- and edge-sharing MPn4 tetrahedra with A cations between them. [ref 2] gives Eu3(GaP2)2 C2/c (15) mp-1189104 and Eu3(InP2)2 Pnnm (58) mp-1188263, each at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference, so the space group is recorded per host and should decide any split in stage 2.
Charge balance (3 Eu2+, 2 M3+, 4 P3-) makes them valence-precise semiconductors; Eu mixed valence is not expected.

formula_archetype: TlMQ2 with M = Ga, In and Q = S, Se, built from M4Q10 adamantane-like supertetrahedra
typical_space_group: C2/c (15), recalled and not verified against a reference

discriminate_from.inte_tlse: the TlSe-type chain structure (I4/mcm) taken by TlGaTe2, TlInSe2 and TlInTe2, with MQ4 tetrahedra sharing edges into chains; the sulfides and TlGaSe2 instead form layers of corner-linked M4Q10 supertetrahedra with Tl between them
discriminate_from.alpha_nafeo2_layered: the TlLnQ2 rare-earth dichalcogenides, where the trivalent cation is octahedral in CdI2-like slabs rather than tetrahedral
discriminate_from.inse_gase_layered: the binary GaSe/InSe layers with M-M bonded Q-M-M-Q sheets and no monovalent interlayer cation

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 066 for the Ga-S-Se-Tl host: TlGaSSe single crystal, from a paper on the temperature dependence of thermal transport in a TlGaSSe crystal. No reference line was shown for the host, so no mp_id or space group is taken from the data.

The monoclinic cell is a stacking of Ga4Q10 supertetrahedron layers with Tl+ in trigonal-prismatic voids between them; polytypes with different stacking periods are common in TlInS2 and should be expected.

TlGaSe2 and TlInS2 have incommensurate and ferroelectric transitions near 100-120 K and 190-220 K respectively. These are small displacive modulations of the same prototype and do not change the assignment.

formula_archetype: RTe3 with R a trivalent rare earth (La-Nd, Sm, Gd-Tm) or Y
typical_space_group: Cmcm (63), often quoted in the Bmmb setting; recalled and not verified against a reference

discriminate_from.pbfcl_matlockite: the RTe2 ditellurides (Cu2Sb/Fe2As-related P4/nmm) with a single Te square net per corrugated RTe slab; RTe3 has a double Te net, van der Waals gaps between the double nets, and is weakly orthorhombic
discriminate_from.th3p4: the R3Te4 / R2Te3 cation-deficient cubic tellurides at lower Te content
discriminate_from.zrte5_hfte5: the pentatellurides, chain-built and orthorhombic but with a transition metal and no square net

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 066 for the Gd-Te host: GdTe3, from a Science Advances paper titled High mobility in a van der Waals layered antiferromagnetic metal. [ref 2] lists Gd2Te3, GdTe2 and GdTe for this chemistry but not GdTe3, so no mp_id is taken.

Each RTe slab is sandwiched between two planar Te square nets; the square nets are the conducting layers and host an incommensurate charge density wave, with T_CDW near 377 K for GdTe3 and rising for lighter rare earths. The CDW is a modulation within the same prototype, not a change of prototype.
Rare-earth magnetism orders at low temperature (about 12 K for GdTe3) and is likewise not a structural change.

formula_archetype: U6T with T = Mn, Fe, Co, Ni

discriminate_from.laves_phase: UFe2, the MgCu2-type C15 Laves phase of the same binary at the opposite end of the composition range
discriminate_from.cual2_c16: the CuAl2 C16 type, also I4/mcm and also a tI12 A2B arrangement; U6Mn is tI28 at a 6:1 ratio with transition-metal chains along c
discriminate_from.alpha_u_a20: elemental orthorhombic alpha-U, which forms alongside U6Fe in U-rich alloys

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 066 for the Fe-U host: U6Fe, from a paper on thermoelectric power in uranium intermetallics.

[ref 2] gives U6Fe I4/mcm (140) mp-21108 at hull 0.028 with 7 ICSD references, which agrees with the recalled type. U6Fe and U6Co are superconductors near 4 K and 2 K, which is how this family usually appears in the transport literature.

display_name: Na4Ge13 hexagonal channel framework with Zintl ions in the channels
formula_archetype: Na(x)Ge(y): a four-bonded Ge framework with open hexagonal channels holding Na cations and disordered Ge4 tetrahedral Zintl anions
typical_space_group: P6/mmm (191) as recalled; not confirmed against the paper, which should be checked in stage 2

discriminate_from.clathrate_i: the Na-Ge and K-Ge type I clathrates, where every guest sits in a closed polyhedral cage of a fully four-bonded framework. Here the framework is open along c and the channels hold not only cations but whole Ge4 tetrahedra
discriminate_from.clathrate_ii: Na24Ge136 type II clathrate, the other framework germanide of this binary, again with closed cages and no Zintl anions inside them

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 067 for the Ge-Na host: Na4Ge13, from a paper titled Zintl Ions within Framework Channels: The Complex Structure and Low-Temperature Transport Properties.

[ref 2] offers only NaGe P2_1/c mp-29657, Na12SnGe8 and Na3Ge, all different compositions; no reference entry exists for Na4Ge13 in the 2019 dump. NaGe (P2_1/c) is the simple Zintl salt of isolated Ge4 tetrahedra and is a different compound.
Disorder of the Ge4 tetrahedra in the channels is the structural feature the paper attributes the low thermal conductivity to; stage 2 will need an ordered approximant.

display_name: High-pressure AGe6 germanium framework with guests in channels (BaGe6, SrGe6-d)
formula_archetype: AGe6-d with A = Ba, Sr, Eu: a three-dimensional Ge network of mixed three- and four-bonded atoms, made at several GPa, with the alkaline-earth atoms in one-dimensional channels
typical_space_group: Cmcm (63) for BaGe6; Cmce (64) for SrGe6-d, as recalled and to be confirmed from the paper

discriminate_from.clathrate_i: the ambient-pressure Sr8Ga16Ge30 and Ba8Ge43 type frameworks, fully four-bonded with closed cages. AGe6 frameworks contain three-bonded Ge and the guests sit in channels, not isolated cages
discriminate_from.clathrate_iii_ix: Ba6Ge25 (type IX), the other framework germanide of Ba made at ambient pressure
discriminate_from.alb2: the SrGe2 and BaGe2 layered or Zintl germanides at lower Ge content, which are different compositions

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 067 for the Ge-Sr host: SrGe5.6, from a paper titled High-Pressure Synthesis and Transport Properties of a New Binary Germanide.
[ref 2] lists SrGe2, SrGe, SrGe3, Sr2Ge and Sr5Ge3, all different compositions, so it gives no evidence either way on this phase.
The d in SrGe6-d is a Ge vacancy on the framework, which is what makes the compound a metal or semimetal; it is non-stoichiometry, not doping.

formula_archetype: R2T3X with R = Y, Pr and other rare earths, T = Rh, X = Ge; an R:(T+X) ratio of 1:2
typical_space_group: R-3m (166), taken from ICSD-backed Materials Project entries for the Pr and Y members; the structure-type name is not established here

discriminate_from.laves_phase: the 1:2 ratio invites a Laves reading, and a rhombohedral R-3m cell can be an ordered stacking variant of one; unconfirmed, and the ordering of Rh and Ge on the B sites is what makes this a separate entry
discriminate_from.thcr2si2_122: RRh2Ge2, the tetragonal 122 compound of the same ternary, which [ref 2] ranks higher on ICSD count for both hosts but is a different composition
discriminate_from.tinisi_co2si: the equiatomic RRhGe compounds of the same systems

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 067 for the Ge-Pr-Rh and Ge-Rh-Y hosts: Pr2Rh3Ge and Y2Rh3Ge, from one paper titled A new ternary magnetically ordered heavy fermion compound Pr2Rh3Ge, where Y2Rh3Ge is the non-magnetic reference.

[ref 2] gives Pr2GeRh3 R-3m (166) mp-1077830 and Y2GeRh3 R-3m (166) mp-10214, each at hull 0.000 with 1 ICSD reference (weak). The space group comes from there, not from memory; relating it to a named aristotype (Laves stacking or PuNi3-derived) is left for review.

formula_archetype: ABO4 with A = La-Gd (large rare earths), B = P, As, V; ninefold-coordinated A and isolated BO4 tetrahedra

discriminate_from.zircon_zrsio4: xenotime, the tetragonal I4_1/amd form taken by the smaller rare-earth phosphates (Tb-Lu, Y); separate on the ionic radius of the rare earth, with the boundary near Gd-Tb
discriminate_from.scheelite_awo4: I4_1/a with eightfold A and isolated WO4 or MoO4 tetrahedra; the high-pressure and molybdate/tungstate analogue
discriminate_from.fergusonite_retao4: the monoclinic distortion of scheelite, RETaO4 and RENbO4, with B = Ta or Nb rather than P

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 069 for the La-O-P host: one bulk LaPO4 sample measured 301-1268 K, from a thermophysical-property paper on rare-earth ceramics.

[ref 2] ranks LaPO4 P2_1/c (14) mp-3962 first, hull 0.000 with 5 ICSD references, which agrees with monazite; the space group is taken from there. Monazite LaPO4 is stable to its melting point, so no transition is expected in the window.
Low thermal conductivity and phase stability make monazites thermal-barrier and environmental-barrier candidates, which is why they appear in this dataset.

formula_archetype: A2BO4 with every cation tetrahedral: A = Be, Zn, Li; B = Si, Ge, W, Mo

discriminate_from.olivine_m2sio4: the same A2BO4 formula with octahedral A cations in hexagonal close packing, Pnma; phenakite has all cations tetrahedral in an open framework of channels
discriminate_from.spinel: A2BO4 again, but cubic close-packed with octahedral and tetrahedral sites, Fd-3m
discriminate_from.scheelite_awo4: a single large A cation per WO4 tetrahedron, not two small tetrahedral ones

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 069 for the Li-O-W host: one Li2WO4 ribbon sample from a paper on ultra-low-firing microwave dielectric ceramics.

[ref 2] ranks Li2WO4 R-3 (148) mp-18902 first, hull 0.015 with 3 ICSD references (weak). That agrees with the phenakite form of Li2WO4, which is the ambient phase. A spinel-type high-pressure Li2WO4 is known but not reached on heating.

formula_archetype: A3X with Li2N hexagonal layers bridged by a further Li between them

discriminate_from.alb2: also P6/mmm and hexagonal, but with a graphite-like honeycomb layer of B and no bridging cation; AlB2 has an A:B ratio of 1:2
discriminate_from.antifluorite: Li2O-type A2X on a face-centred cubic anion lattice, the structure of Li2O and Li2S rather than of the nitride

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 069 for the Li-N host: one Li3N sample, from a paper on its low-temperature thermal conductivity.

[ref 2] ranks Li3N P6/mmm (191) mp-2251 first, hull 0.000 with 20 ICSD references, which is strong agreement. The beta-Li3N (Na3As-type, P6_3/mmc) and gamma-Li3N (Li3Bi-type) forms are high-pressure only.
The structural_class is the nearest declared one. Li3N is a layered ionic crystal with Li between the Li2N layers, not a van der Waals solid, and it is a fast Li-ion conductor within the layers.

formula_archetype: A2B with A = Mg and B = Ni or Cu-substituted Ni

discriminate_from.laves_phase: MgNi2, the Ni-rich compound of the same binary, is the hexagonal C36 Laves phase in P6_3/mmc; the Mg:Ni ratio separates them, 2:1 here against 1:2
discriminate_from.cual2_c16: Mg2Cu is not isotypic either: it is orthorhombic Fddd, and CuAl2-type A2B is body-centred tetragonal I4/mcm
discriminate_from.complex_hydride_mg2nih4: the hydride Mg2NiH4 formed from this phase on hydrogenation, with [NiH4]4- complex anions in an antifluorite-derived cell; the metal and the hydride are different structures and are separated by the hydrogen content

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 070 for the Mg-Ni host: one Mg2Ni sample from a paper on magnetoresistance and the Hall effect, most likely in a thin film, since Mg2Ni is chiefly studied as a hydrogen-storage and switchable-mirror film.
[ref 2] ranks Mg2Ni P6_222 (180) mp-2137 first with 13 ICSD references, which is strong agreement. The structure is Mg2Ni's own type (hP18), with no transition on heating before it melts near 1030 K.

formula_archetype: TMSi2 with T = Ti, Zr, Nb and M = Mn, Fe, Co (ZrMnSi2, TiFeSi2 related)

discriminate_from.tisi2_c54: the binary TiSi2 in Fddd, a stacking of the same hexagonal TSi2 layers; TiMnSi2 is a ternary ordering with two transition metals in distinct sites
discriminate_from.crsi2_c40: the hexagonal C40 disilicide, P6_222, the structure of CrSi2 and of MnSi2-poor ternary silicides at other ratios
discriminate_from.hms_chimney_ladder: the Mn-rich MnSi1.75 Nowotny phase, a tetragonal incommensurate chimney ladder, with no second transition metal
discriminate_from.zr3mn4si6_type: a second Mn-rich ternary silicide from the same paper, at 3:4:6 instead of 1:1:2 and tetragonal

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 070 for the Mn-Si-Ti host: one bulk TiMnSi2 sample from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of Zr3Mn4Si6 and TiMnSi2.

[ref 2] ranks TiMnSi2 Pbam (55) mp-21606 first, hull 0.000 with 3 ICSD references. ZrMnSi2 is listed in the same space group under the Mn-Si-Zr host, which supports treating the two as isotypic; that is inference and should be checked.

formula_archetype: T3M4Si6 with T = Zr, Hf and M = Mn

discriminate_from.timnsi2_type: TiMnSi2 and ZrMnSi2 in orthorhombic Pbam at the 1:1:2 ratio; Zr3Mn4Si6 is richer in Mn relative to Zr and tetragonal
discriminate_from.tinisi_co2si: ZrMnSi, the equiatomic Pnma phase of the same ternary, which [ref 2] ranks first for this host
discriminate_from.hms_chimney_ladder: the binary Mn-rich silicide MnSi1.75, which has no Zr

structure_database_candidates.source: ref 2, written Zr3(Mn2Si3)2, hull 0.002, 1 ICSD reference (weak), primary

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 070 for the Mn-Si-Zr host: one bulk Zr3Mn4Si6 sample from a paper on the thermoelectric properties of Zr3Mn4Si6 and TiMnSi2.

The space group rests on the single ICSD-backed Materials Project entry at this exact formula. I cannot name a better-known isotype, so the id is the compound itself; if the paper or ICSD identifies it with an existing type, fold it into that one.

display_name: Phosphate tungsten bronze (MPTB / DPTB), ReO3 slabs separated by phosphate layers
prototype: (PO2)4(WO3)2m monophosphate tungsten bronze and Ax(P2O4)2(WO3)2m diphosphate tungsten bronze
formula_archetype: (PO2)4(WO3)2m (MPTB) or Ax(P2O4)2(WO3)2m with A = K, Na, Rb in hexagonal or pentagonal tunnels (DPTB-h, DPTB-p); m = slab thickness in WO6 octahedra
typical_space_group: not fixed: orthorhombic or monoclinic for MPTB and hexagonal or orthorhombic for DPTB depending on m and on the tunnel cation, so take it from the paper

discriminate_from.reo3_wo3: the parent WO3 has continuous corner-shared WO6 octahedra in three dimensions; here ReO3-type slabs m octahedra thick are cut off by PO4 or P2O7 layers, which makes the electronic structure quasi-two-dimensional
discriminate_from.tungsten_bronze: the tetragonal or hexagonal AxWO3 bronzes have no phosphate and their A cation sits in tunnels of an uninterrupted WO6 framework
discriminate_from.vanadium_bronze: a vanadate, not a tungstate, and without phosphate slabs

notes: Proposed while annotating chunk 071 for the O-P-W host: one single crystal of K1.2P4W8O32 from a paper on a phase transition in that compound, measured 12-289 K.

These are the textbook low-dimensional charge-density-wave oxides: the Fermi surface of the ReO3 slabs nests, and the CDW transitions are structural superlattice modulations inside the transport window.
